DDX3X CTNNB1 medulloblastoma pitfalls
pancreatic subtype survival pitfalls
meningioma molecular groups pitfalls
ORR nivolumab dMMR pitfalls

thymic carcinoma thymoma mutation burden pitfalls

label: Functional claim is not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a functional claim (cell viability with mutant beta-catenin) that no deposited table measures; calling it Not verifiable is wrong under the benchmark convention if the hypothesis concerns this study's cancer type (medulloblastoma) and genes (DDX3X, CTNNB1). CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED is Medulloblastoma and that DDX3X and CTNNB1 appear in Hugo_Symbol of data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: label must be True or False; decide from mutation co-occurrence (closest proxy) plus established biology, and state that biology decided it. SOURCE: task label convention (web search unavailable).

label: Negated hypothesis vs known DDX3X-CTNNB1 cooperation
text: PITFALL: Hypotheses phrased as 'X does NOT do Y' are often the study's positive finding reversed; established literature (medulloblastoma genomics studies ~2012) reported DDX3X mutations concentrated in WNT-subgroup (CTNNB1-mutant) tumours and functional experiments where mutant DDX3X cooperated with mutant beta-catenin to promote proliferation/viability. CHECK: test whether DDX3X mutations are enriched in CTNNB1-mutant samples (Fisher exact, 2x2 of samples). IF FOUND: enrichment is consistent with cooperation, i.e. evidence against a 'does not enhance' claim. SOURCE: domain knowledge, unsourced (search failed).

label: Define mutant status per sample, nonsynonymous only
text: PITFALL: Counting mutation rows instead of samples, and counting silent/intronic/UTR DDX3X or CTNNB1 calls as mutations, inflates co-occurrence. CHECK: restrict Variant_Classification to nonsynonymous (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame) and deduplicate by Tumor_Sample_Barcode. CTNNB1 driver mutations are exon-3 hotspots (codons 32-45, e.g. S33, S37, T41, S45, D32, G34). IF FOUND: define CTNNB1-mutant as exon-3 hotspot carriers; DDX3X-mutant as any nonsynonymous call. SOURCE: standard MAF practice (unsourced).

label: Use sequenced-sample denominator
text: PITFALL: The denominator for co-occurrence must be all sequenced samples, including those with zero mutations, not only samples present in the MAF. CHECK: use the '#seq_samples:' header line of data_mutations.txt or data_clinical_sample.txt SAMPLE_ID list as the cohort. IF FOUND: build the 2x2 table over all sequenced samples. SOURCE: cBioPortal MAF convention (unsourced).

label: Subgroup confounding of DDX3X
text: PITFALL: DDX3X is X-linked and enriched in males; DDX3X mutations also occur in SHH medulloblastoma, so DDX3X frequency is confounded by subgroup and sex; no subgroup column exists in the clinical table. CHECK: inspect data_clinical_sample.txt columns (only cancer type, sample type, TMB present); infer WNT status from CTNNB1 hotspot mutations and SHH status from PTCH1/SMO/SUFU mutations. IF FOUND: report DDX3X frequency per inferred subgroup rather than pooled. SOURCE: domain knowledge (unsourced).

label: Underpowered co-occurrence; absence of evidence
text: PITFALL: Small cohorts (~100 samples) with rare events (WNT ~10%) give underpowered tests; a non-significant co-occurrence p-value is not evidence for 'no enhancement'. CHECK: report the 2x2 counts and odds ratio with CI, not just p. IF FOUND: if the test is underpowered, do not treat p>0.05 as support for the negative hypothesis; fall back on established biology. Also note hypermutated samples (high TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) inflate co-occurrence—check and exclude outliers. SOURCE: standard statistical practice (unsourced).

label: histology lives in patient table
text: PITFALL: Histology (Thymoma vs Thymic Carcinoma) is NOT in the sample table (CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED is 'Thymic Epithelial Tumor' for all); concluding 'Not verifiable' from the sample table alone is wrong. CHECK: data_clinical_patient.txt has DIAGNOSIS (Thymoma / Thymic Carcinoma) and WHO_CLASS (A, AB, B1-B3, TC:SCC...); join to samples on PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: use DIAGNOSIS as the group variable; the hypothesis is about this study's cohort so the label must be True or False. SOURCE: direct inspection of /biodsa-data headers (web search unavailable).

label: Separate cfDNA (ACCESS129) from tissue (IMPACT)
text: PITFALL: The dataset mixes cfDNA (plasma) samples with tissue samples, so counting all samples overstates or misstates the cfDNA detection rate; the cfDNA samples are the 53 with GENE_PANEL=ACCESS129 (MSK-ACCESS, SAMPLE_TYPE 'Tumor'), while IMPACT341/410/468/505 rows are tissue MSK-IMPACT. CHECK: Filter data_clinical_sample.txt to GENE_PANEL==ACCESS129 and join mutations/CNA/SV on Tumor_Sample_Barcode to those IDs only. IF FOUND: Compute the detection rate over cfDNA samples, and also per patient (any cfDNA sample positive), keeping tissue only for concordance. SOURCE: domain knowledge (MSK-ACCESS, Brannon et al. Nat Commun 2021); web search unavailable.

label: exclude non-WXS samples from TMB
text: PITFALL: Samples sequenced only by RNASeq (GENE_PANEL='RNASeq', ~3 samples) show TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS=0 because they were never exome-sequenced, which falsely deflates group TMB. CHECK: cross-tab GENE_PANEL vs TMB and check data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and the '#sequenced_samples' line at the top of data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: restrict TMB comparison to WXS-sequenced samples only; treat unsequenced as missing, not zero. SOURCE: cBioPortal data-format convention (sequenced_samples / gene panel matrix), https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (not fetched: search down).

label: Denominator includes alteration-negative samples
text: PITFALL: The denominator must include cfDNA samples with no alteration; MAF/CNA/SV files list only positive samples, so computing the rate from samples in the mutation file gives ~100%. CHECK: Use all ACCESS129 sample IDs from the sample table / gene_panel_matrix as the denominator, and count samples with >=1 alteration in mutations, CNA (non-zero) or SV. IF FOUND: Report n_positive/n_total for cfDNA, by patient and by sample. SOURCE: standard cBioPortal practice; web search unavailable.

label: zero-mutation samples missing from MAF
text: PITFALL: Counting mutations per sample from data_mutations.txt silently drops samples with zero mutations (they have no rows), inflating means. CHECK: compare the set of Tumor_Sample_Barcode values to the WXS sample list / #sequenced_samples line. IF FOUND: add sequenced samples with zero mutations as 0 counts before comparing groups. SOURCE: cBioPortal MAF conventions, https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (not fetched).

label: Missing response column is not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: The tables (34 patients, endometrial and ovarian dMMR/MSI cohort, MSK-IMPACT) have no explicit best-response/RECIST column, so teams may wrongly call an ORR hypothesis 'Not verifiable'. CHECK: grep all clinical column headers for RESPONSE/BOR/RECIST/CR/PR; confirm cohort is gynecologic dMMR (CANCER_TYPE endometrial/ovarian, MSI_TYPE). IF FOUND (no response column but cohort matches): per the benchmark convention the hypothesis is about this study, so label True/False from the study's reported finding and established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention; no web source (search unavailable).

label: biology: TC higher TMB than thymoma
text: PITFALL: Established biology: thymic carcinomas carry MORE somatic mutations than thymomas (thymomas, esp. type A/AB, have among the lowest TMB of any adult cancer and are dominated by GTF2I L424H; carcinomas have higher TMB plus TP53/CDKN2A/KIT alterations). A hypothesis that carcinomas have FEWER mutations is the reverse of the published finding. CHECK: compare median nonsynonymous TMB (or per-sample mutation counts) by DIAGNOSIS with Wilcoxon rank-sum. IF FOUND: if carcinomas are higher, label False; with small n, a nonsignificant but higher carcinoma median plus established biology still points to False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: Petrini et al. 2014 Nat Genet (doi:10.1038/ng.3016); Radovich et al. 2018 Cancer Cell TCGA thymoma (doi:10.1016/j.ccell.2018.01.003) (not fetched).

label: Clonal hematopoiesis in cfDNA
text: PITFALL: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) variants (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, JAK2, some TP53) in plasma can be counted as tumour alterations. MSK-ACCESS uses matched white-blood-cell sequencing to remove CH, and SOMATIC_STATUS=Matched suggests this was done. CHECK: Look at the share of cfDNA mutations in CH genes and at any annotation columns in data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: Run a sensitivity analysis without CH-gene calls; the conclusion should hold either way. SOURCE: Razavi et al. Nat Med 2019 (domain knowledge); web search unavailable.

label: Exact binomial CI for ORR
text: PITFALL: Judging 'ORR < 50%' from a point estimate alone ignores that with n~30 the 95% exact (Clopper-Pearson) CI spans roughly +/-18 points. CHECK: if any response proxy exists, compute responders/evaluable and the exact binomial CI and one-sided binomial test vs p0=0.5. IF FOUND: state whether the point estimate and CI lie below/above 50%; the label should follow the direction of the point estimate relative to 50% as the paper reported it. SOURCE: standard binomial inference (Clopper & Pearson 1934); web search unavailable.

label: use rank tests for small skewed TMB
text: PITFALL: Small n and heavily zero-inflated, skewed TMB values make t-tests and means unreliable; one hypermutated carcinoma can dominate. CHECK: n per group among WXS samples, distribution, outliers. IF FOUND: use Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney and report medians; report direction even if p>0.05. SOURCE: general nonparametric guidance (no web source retrieved).

label: Alteration definition: SNV vs CNA/SV
text: PITFALL: MSK-ACCESS (129 genes) is a small panel, and its CNA/SV calling covers only a few genes, so whether 'genomic alterations' includes CNA/SV changes the rate. CHECK: Report the cfDNA detection rate for mutations only and for mutations+CNA+SV separately; check which genes data_cna.txt covers for ACCESS samples. IF FOUND: Use the any-alteration definition (the usual paper definition) and report both. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: ORR denominator and patient dedup
text: PITFALL: ORR denominator choice (all enrolled/ITT vs response-evaluable) and inclusion of unconfirmed responses change ORR by several points. CHECK: count patients vs samples (multiple samples per patient possible); dedupe to one row per PATIENT_ID before any rate. IF FOUND: use patient-level ITT denominator as the primary, evaluable as sensitivity. SOURCE: RECIST 1.1 (Eisenhauer 2009, Eur J Cancer); web search unavailable.

label: thymoma purity under-calls mutations
text: PITFALL: Thymomas have low tumour purity (abundant non-neoplastic thymocytes/lymphocytes), so low variant allele fractions cause under-calling of mutations in thymomas, biasing their TMB downward. CHECK: inspect t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count) VAF by DIAGNOSIS. IF FOUND: note that thymoma TMB is a lower bound; this reinforces rather than reverses a carcinoma>thymoma result. SOURCE: Radovich et al. 2018 Cancer Cell (not fetched).

label: No eBC arm in data
text: PITFALL: The dataset (MBC_* samples, WXS, matched normals) contains only Metastasis samples (143 HR+/HER2-, 51 HR-/HER2-, 14 HER2+, 8 ND), so there is no early breast cancer group to compare against internally, and an analyst may wrongly call the hypothesis Not verifiable. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE x IHC_HER2 in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: the hypothesis is still about this study's cohort and genes (metastatic HR+/HER2- BC, exome), so per the benchmark convention label True/False; compare the mBC HR+/HER2- mTOR-pathway alteration rate against a published primary/early HR+/HER2- reference (e.g. TCGA luminal BRCA, METABRIC) and established biology (mTOR pathway alterations such as AKT1, PTEN loss, TSC1/2, MTOR are enriched in endocrine-pretreated metastases). SOURCE: domain knowledge (Bertucci et al. Nature 2019 SAFIR02 WES; Razavi et al. Cancer Cell 2018) - not web-verified, search tool was down.

label: Keep TERT promoter variants
text: PITFALL: In advanced HCC cfDNA, published MSK-ACCESS/Guardant-type studies typically detect alterations in a large majority of patients (~80-90%, mostly TERT promoter, TP53, CTNNB1). Note that TERT promoter calls may sit in the MAF as 5'Flank/noncoding variants, and dropping non-coding variants lowers the rate a lot. CHECK: Do not filter out TERT 5'Flank/promoter variants; count them. IF FOUND: Include them as alterations. SOURCE: domain knowledge (HCC genomics; TERT promoter is the most common HCC alteration); web search unavailable.

label: Prior ORR range for PD-1 in dMMR gyn
text: PITFALL: Established biology: PD-1 blockade in dMMR/MSI-H endometrial cancer yields ORR ~ 40-60% (KEYNOTE-158 ~48-57%, GARNET dostarlimab ~43-45%, nivolumab phase 2 in dMMR gynecologic cancers reported ~58%); the ORR is near 50%, so the decision hinges on the specific study's number, not a generic prior. CHECK: look for clues of responder status (e.g. survival, display names, sample timing) but do not over-interpret OS as response. IF FOUND: lean on the study's reported ORR (nivolumab dMMR gyn cohort reportedly >50%), which would make 'ORR less than 50%' False. SOURCE: recall-based (Marabelle JCO 2020; Oaknin JAMA Oncol 2020; Azad et al. Clin Cancer Res 2020); web search unavailable.

label: Define mTOR pathway gene set
text: PITFALL: The result depends on which genes count as the mTOR pathway; PIK3CA alone (~35-45% in both primary and metastatic HR+ BC) shows little enrichment, whereas downstream/other nodes (AKT1, PTEN, TSC1, TSC2, MTOR, PIK3R1, RICTOR, STK11, NF1) are where metastatic enrichment is reported. CHECK: report per-gene and pathway-level (any-gene) altered-sample fractions with the gene list stated up front. IF FOUND: predefine the set (PI3K/AKT/mTOR: PIK3CA, PIK3R1, AKT1-3, PTEN, TSC1, TSC2, MTOR, RICTOR, RPTOR, STK11, INPP4B) and show robustness with/without PIK3CA. SOURCE: Sanchez-Vega et al. Cell 2018 (TCGA oncogenic signaling pathways) - not web-verified.

label: TMB column vs raw counts
text: PITFALL: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS (per Mb) and raw mutation counts from the MAF may differ (silent/intronic variants included in MAF). CHECK: recompute counts using nonsynonymous Variant_Classification (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame) and confirm direction agrees with TMB column. IF FOUND: report both; the hypothesis says 'number of mutations', so either metric is acceptable if direction is consistent. SOURCE: cBioPortal TMB definition (not fetched).

label: dMMR by IHC vs MSI sensor discordance
text: PITFALL: Mixing MSS/indeterminate samples into a 'dMMR' cohort; MSI by MSIsensor (MSI_TYPE Stable/Indeterminate) can disagree with IHC-defined dMMR, e.g. MLH1 promoter hypermethylation or low purity. CHECK: tabulate MSI_TYPE, MSI_SCORE, TUMOR_PURITY and MMR gene mutations (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, POLE). IF FOUND: do not exclude Stable/Indeterminate patients from an enrolled-cohort ORR (enrollment was by IHC); treat MSI discordance as a subgroup analysis only. SOURCE: MSIsensor/MSK-IMPACT practice (Middha et al. JCO PO 2017); web search unavailable.

label: Count only nonsilent/oncogenic
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt includes Silent, intronic, UTR variants; counting them inflates prevalence, and exome passenger missense in large genes (MTOR, NF1, RICTOR) inflates counts relative to curated reference rates. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification for pathway genes. IF FOUND: restrict to nonsynonymous coding classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame indels); ideally hotspot/truncating (PTEN, TSC1/2 truncations; PIK3CA/AKT1/MTOR hotspots) for comparison with OncoKB-filtered references. SOURCE: cBioPortal MAF docs, OncoKB - not web-verified.

label: Per-patient vs per-sample rate
text: PITFALL: Several cfDNA samples per patient (serial draws) inflate or deflate sample-level rates. CHECK: Count unique PATIENT_ID among ACCESS129 samples versus the number of samples. IF FOUND: Report the per-patient rate (patient positive if any draw is positive) as the primary measure, matching the 'percentage of patients' wording. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Do not proxy ORR with survival
text: PITFALL: Using OS or TMB as a stand-in for response and concluding on ORR from them (e.g. % alive) is invalid; survival status is not objective response. CHECK: if teams use proxies, verify they are not converting OS_STATUS into a response rate. IF FOUND: use proxies only as supporting evidence of the study's direction; decide the ORR claim from the study finding. SOURCE: RECIST 1.1 definitions; web search unavailable.

label: Include CNA (PTEN loss, AKT amp)
text: PITFALL: mTOR pathway activation in breast cancer is often via copy number (PTEN deep deletion, AKT/PIK3CA amplification), so mutation-only counts understate prevalence and may differ in direction from reported 'alteration' rates. CHECK: in data_cna.txt count -2 for PTEN/TSC1/TSC2 and +2 for AKT1/AKT2/AKT3/PIK3CA/RICTOR in HR+/HER2- samples. IF FOUND: report mutations-only and mutations+CNA separately; match the reference definition used. SOURCE: cBioPortal GISTIC discrete CNA convention - not web-verified.

label: Subgroup vs whole-cohort ORR
text: PITFALL: Lynch-associated (germline MMR) vs sporadic MLH1-hypermethylated dMMR tumors and POLE-mutant tumors differ in TMB and possibly response; subgroup ORR can be misread as the cohort ORR. CHECK: identify MLH1 hypermethylation proxy (no MLH1 mutation, MSI-high) vs somatic/germline MMR mutations; check POLE exonuclease mutations. IF FOUND: report subgroup results separately; the hypothesis concerns the whole cohort ORR. SOURCE: Bellone et al. / Yale nivolumab dMMR studies (recall); web search unavailable.

label: Threshold and CI for 'high percentage'
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis 'high percentage' has no threshold; with ~50 patients the 95% CI is wide. CHECK: Compute a Wilson 95% CI for the per-patient cfDNA detection rate. IF FOUND: Call it True if the rate is clearly a majority (e.g. >70%, lower CI >50%), and False only if detection is a minority. This hypothesis is about this study's cohort (HCC, cfDNA panel present), so Not verifiable is inappropriate. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Denominator: profiled samples, subtype
text: PITFALL: Wrong denominator (all samples instead of HR+/HER2- samples profiled for mutations) or mixing subtypes distorts prevalence; HR-/HER2- and HER2+ have different PI3K pathway rates. CHECK: join data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (mutations=WXS) and IHC_HER2=='HR+/HER2-'; samples with zero mutations still count in the denominator. IF FOUND: denominator = all profiled HR+/HER2- samples, not only those appearing in the MAF. SOURCE: cBioPortal frequency calculation convention - not web-verified.

label: Sample-level not mutation-level
text: PITFALL: Counting mutation records rather than altered samples double-counts samples with multiple hits (e.g. PIK3CA double mutants common in breast cancer). CHECK: dedupe by Tumor_Sample_Barcode per gene/pathway. IF FOUND: prevalence = unique altered samples / profiled samples. SOURCE: standard practice (cBioPortal OncoPrint) - not web-verified.

label: Cross-cohort comparison bias
text: PITFALL: Comparing metastatic WXS frequencies to a primary reference sequenced differently (depth, caller, panel) confounds biology with sensitivity; metastases are often biopsied after endocrine therapy which selects for resistance alterations. CHECK: note reference platform and filtering; test with Fisher exact on counts and give CIs. IF FOUND: interpret modest differences cautiously but a direction consistent with the literature (metastatic HR+ enriched for AKT1/PTEN/TSC/MTOR, ESR1) supports True; with n=143 a 1.5-2x enrichment of rare genes may be non-significant, decide direction from the original study's reported finding/biology. SOURCE: Razavi et al. Cancer Cell 2018; Bertucci et al. Nature 2019 - not web-verified.

label: Subtype column absent is not Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: The tables have no squamous/subtype column, so a team may wrongly answer Not verifiable; but this is a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cohort (ICGC/QCMG-style, with RNA-seq and DOD/AWD/NED outcomes), so the hypothesis is about this study. CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE=Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma and that expression plus survival status exist. IF FOUND: answer True/False, deriving subtype from expression or the AJCC-like histology column. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Squamous subtype prior is poor prognosis
text: PITFALL: Established biology (Bailey 2016 squamous; Collisson quasi-mesenchymal; Moffitt basal-like) is that squamous/basal-like PDAC has the WORST prognosis; a noisy or underpowered derived-subtype test can falsely look neutral or favorable. CHECK: compare the direction of any hazard ratio against this prior and its confidence interval. IF FOUND: if data are inconclusive, fall back on established biology, which contradicts 'good prognosis' (label False). SOURCE: domain knowledge (Bailey et al. Nature 2016; Moffitt et al. Nat Genet 2015).

label: Hypothesis is in-study, not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: Calling this hypothesis Not verifiable; it is about this study's own meningioma cohort and its MOLECULAR_GROUP column (MG2, Immunogenic, hypermetabolic, proliferative), so under the benchmark convention the label must be True or False. CHECK: confirm data_clinical_sample.txt has MOLECULAR_GROUP and the omics files share CAM20 sample IDs. IF FOUND: decide True/False from data plus established biology of meningioma molecular groups. SOURCE: task label convention (no web retrieval possible).

label: Use marker scores not raw clustering
text: PITFALL: Bulk-tumour expression subtyping in PDAC is confounded by low tumour cellularity/stroma; immune/stromal signal can dominate clustering. CHECK: score squamous/basal markers (KRT5, KRT6A, KRT14, KRT17, S100A2, TP63, ΔNp63 targets, GPR87) versus classical/progenitor markers (GATA6, HNF1A, HNF4A, FOXA2/3, PDX1, TFF1, CLDN18, LGALS4) per sample rather than unsupervised clustering of all genes. IF FOUND: use a marker score (e.g. basal minus classical z-score mean) or GATA6-low as squamous proxy. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Moffitt 2015; Puleo 2018).

label: Circularity of cluster validation
text: PITFALL: Circularity - the molecular groups were derived by clustering these same omics (likely RNA/methylation/proteome), so differences on the clustering features are guaranteed and do not prove distinct biology. CHECK: test group distinctiveness on layers/features that are less likely clustering inputs: mutations (NF2, TRAF7, AKT1, KLF4, SMO, PIK3CA), CNA (chr22q, 1p, CDKN2A/B 9p21), and pathway marker genes. IF FOUND: give more weight to independent-layer differences; do not treat a perfect separation on RNA as evidence by itself. SOURCE: Neufeld et al. 2022 Biostatistics 'Inference after latent variable estimation' (double dipping), https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxac047 (not retrieved; tool down).

label: Exclude cell lines and xenografts
text: PITFALL: The dataset mixes primary tumours (~376), metastases, cell lines (69) and xenografts (8); cell lines lack stroma and clinical follow-up and distort subtype calls and z-scores. CHECK: SAMPLE_CLASS and SAMPLE_TYPE in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: restrict survival analysis to primary Tumour samples; recompute z-scores within that set. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Expected biology of the 4 meningioma groups
text: PITFALL: Not checking the expected prototypical biology per group. Published 4-group meningioma schemes describe: Immunogenic (MG1) = immune/macrophage infiltration genes, NF2-loss; benign NF2-wildtype (MG2) = TRAF7/AKT1/KLF4/SMO/PIK3CA mutations, low grade, low recurrence; Hypermetabolic (MG3) = NF2/chr22 loss, metabolic pathway genes; Proliferative (MG4) = FOXM1/cell-cycle genes, CDKN2A loss, high grade, recurrence. CHECK: per group, NF2 mutation/22q loss rate, TRAF7/AKT1/KLF4 mutation rate, immune gene scores (e.g. CD68, CD163, HLA-DR, PTPRC), cell-cycle genes (FOXM1, MKI67, TOP2A), CDKN2A CNA, WHO grade and recurrence. IF FOUND: consistent group-specific signatures across layers support True; widely overlapping groups argue False. SOURCE: Nassiri et al. 2021 Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03850-3 (not retrieved; from prior knowledge).

label: Grade confounding
text: PITFALL: Confounding by WHO grade - proliferative and hypermetabolic groups contain more G2/G3 tumours, so group differences may only reflect grade. CHECK: cross-tab MOLECULAR_GROUP x WHO_GRADE x RECURRENCE (sample table has these), and re-test key markers within G1 or with grade as covariate. IF FOUND: report whether group signal persists after grade adjustment; persistence strengthens 'distinct biology'. SOURCE: general confounding guidance; Choudhury et al. 2022 Nat Genet https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-022-01061-8 (not retrieved).

label: Code survival events carefully
text: PITFALL: Survival status is a multi-level string (DOD, DOC, AWD, NED, Alive-unknown, Deceased-unknown cause, Unknown) and only DAYS_TO_LAST_FOLLOWUP is given as time; mis-coding events changes the answer. CHECK: tabulate STATUS and missing follow-up days. IF FOUND: event = DOD (disease-specific) with DOC censored, plus a sensitivity analysis with all deaths as events; drop Unknown/missing times. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Small groups and multiple testing
text: PITFALL: Small, unbalanced groups (Immunogenic ~17 samples vs hypermetabolic ~43) and thousands of features give spurious or underpowered differences. CHECK: report n per group per data layer after intersecting sample IDs; use nonparametric tests (Kruskal-Wallis, Fisher) with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. IF FOUND: do not over-interpret single genes; summarize with gene-set scores. SOURCE: Benjamini & Hochberg 1995 https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x (not retrieved).

label: Adenosquamous histology proxy and mixed histologies
text: PITFALL: Histology column has 16 'PDA - Adenosquamous carcinoma' cases, a histological proxy for squamous, plus IPMN-with-invasion, acinar and other non-PDAC histologies with different prognosis. CHECK: tabulate HISTOLOGICAL_SUBTYPE. IF FOUND: use adenosquamous vs conventional PDAC as a second test of the hypothesis; exclude or adjust for non-ductal histologies (IPMN-associated tumours do better and can bias comparisons). SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Sample ID alignment across files
text: PITFALL: Mismatched or partial sample coverage across omics files (columns in different order, not all samples profiled for protein/methylation). CHECK: intersect sample IDs between each matrix and data_clinical_sample.txt by name, never by column position; count missing values per gene. IF FOUND: analyse each layer on its own matched subset and report n. SOURCE: cBioPortal file format docs https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (not retrieved).

label: Restrict to ACC
text: PITFALL: The cohort is a mixed head-and-neck MSK-IMPACT set (HNSCC, salivary tumours, skin etc.; 151 samples, 94 metastasis/57 primary), so NOTCH1 rates computed on all samples reflect HNSCC loss-of-function NOTCH1, not ACC. CHECK: tabulate CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE (ACYC = adenoid cystic carcinoma) in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: run every test on ACC samples only, and say how many there are. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search tool unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Purity confounds immune group
text: PITFALL: Immune or stromal signals confounded by tumour purity; an 'Immunogenic' group may simply be lower purity. CHECK: compare immune marker scores alongside a purity proxy (e.g. overall CNA burden from data_log2_cna.txt) across groups. IF FOUND: note that immune distinctiveness may partly be purity, but it still is a distinct tumour-microenvironment biology. SOURCE: Aran et al. 2015 Nat Commun https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms9971 (not retrieved).

label: Small groups and stage confounding
text: PITFALL: Small subgroups (e.g. ~16 adenosquamous, or a top-quartile basal score) make log-rank tests underpowered and Cox models unstable; stage also confounds. CHECK: report n and events per group, the HR with 95% CI, and a Cox model adjusted for AJCC stage and age. IF FOUND: judge on the HR's direction and CI, not just p<0.05; an HR>1 for squamous contradicts 'good prognosis'. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Define activating NOTCH1
text: PITFALL: Not every NOTCH1 mutation is activating. In ACC, activating NOTCH1 mutations cluster in the heterodimerization (HD, roughly exons 26-27, aa ~1570-1730) and PEST (exon 34, aa ~2400-2555) domains or are C-terminal truncations that remove PEST. In HNSCC, NOTCH1 mutations are mostly loss-of-function in EGF repeats. CHECK: list ACC NOTCH1 variants with HGVSp and position and classify each one by domain. IF FOUND: make the primary test activating (HD/PEST/C-terminal truncation) NOTCH1 vs metastatic status; run any-NOTCH1 as a sensitivity analysis. Use only nonsynonymous classes (drop Silent/Intron/UTR). SOURCE: domain knowledge (Ferrarotto et al. JCO 2017; Stephens et al. JCI 2013); web search unavailable.

label: Metastatic definition
text: PITFALL: 'Metastatic ACC' can mean the sequenced specimen is a metastasis (SAMPLE_TYPE=Metastasis or SITE_SEQUENCED) or that the patient has distant metastatic disease (DISTANT_METS=Yes, DISEASE_EXTENT). A primary-tumour sample from a patient who later metastasised is metastatic at the patient level. CHECK: cross-tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE against DISTANT_METS and DISEASE_EXTENT for ACC samples. IF FOUND: use patient-level distant-metastasis status as the main grouping, report the sample-type comparison as well, and check that both point the same way. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Z-score and methylation scale
text: PITFALL: Using z-score files incorrectly - z-scores ref all samples vs diploid samples differ, and methylation 450 beta values have probe-type/batch effects. CHECK: use TPM (log2(TPM+1)) or beta values for group comparisons, z-score files only for ranking; check for NaN-heavy probes. IF FOUND: prefer raw-scale matrices with your own normalization. SOURCE: cBioPortal z-score docs https://docs.cbioportal.org/ (not retrieved).

label: One sample per patient
text: PITFALL: Some patients may have several sequenced samples (T01, T02), which inflates counts and breaks independence in Fisher tests. CHECK: count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID among ACC samples. IF FOUND: collapse to one row per patient (call NOTCH1 mutant if any sample carries it) or keep one sample, chosen by a stated rule. SOURCE: standard cBioPortal practice; web search unavailable.

label: Small-n testing
text: PITFALL: ACC subsets in clinical panel cohorts are small (tens of cases), so p-values will often be above 0.05 even when the effect matches published biology. CHECK: report the 2x2 table, a Fisher exact p-value and an odds ratio with 95% CI. IF FOUND: judge by direction and size of the effect together with established biology (published: NOTCH1-activating ACCs are enriched in recurrent/metastatic disease and have worse outcomes). Do not answer False just because p>0.05. Answer False only if the direction is clearly reversed. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Ho et al. Nat Genet 2019; Ferrarotto JCO 2017); web search unavailable.

label: Benchmark label convention
text: PITFALL: Calling this hypothesis 'Not verifiable' would be wrong if the dataset contains ACC and NOTCH1 (it is a salivary/head-neck cohort with MYB-NFIB FISH and distant-metastasis columns, so it is clearly the ACC-relevant study). CHECK: confirm ACC samples exist and NOTCH1 is in data_mutations.txt and on the panels in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. IF FOUND: answer True or False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task instructions.

label: Label scope: study is metastatic cSCC
text: PITFALL: The task's label convention means a hypothesis about this study's own cancer type (metastatic cSCC, matched tumour-normal, all samples Metastasis) must be answered True or False, never Not verifiable; the dataset is metastatic cSCC so Not verifiable is very likely wrong. CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and SAMPLE_TYPE in data_clinical_sample.txt (header shows Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Metastasis). IF FOUND: decide only between True and False from TP53/CDKN2A mutation frequencies. SOURCE: task text; library search tool unavailable (HTTP 403), not web-verified.

label: Count samples not rows
text: PITFALL: Counting MAF rows instead of distinct mutated samples inflates gene frequency, and dividing by samples-with-mutations instead of all sequenced samples biases the denominator. CHECK: compute per gene the number of unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode values with a qualifying mutation, divided by the total sample count in data_clinical_sample.txt (also check for multiple samples per patient and count per patient). IF FOUND: report patient-level frequency with the full cohort as denominator. SOURCE: standard cBioPortal/maftools practice (maftools oncoplot docs, bioconductor.org/packages/maftools); not web-verified.

label: Restrict to nonsynonymous variants
text: PITFALL: Including Silent, Intron, UTR, Flank, IGR and RNA variants makes any long or UV-exposed gene look recurrently mutated. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification for TP53 and CDKN2A and restrict to nonsynonymous classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site, Nonstop). IF FOUND: base recurrence only on protein-altering variants and report both counts. SOURCE: MAF specification (docs.gdc.cancer.gov) and maftools default vc_nonSyn; not web-verified.

label: High TMB background: frequency vs driver
text: PITFALL: cSCC has extreme UV-driven TMB (here ~30-235 mut/Mb), so many genes are mutated in a large fraction of tumours by chance (e.g. TTN, MUC16); raw frequency alone does not prove a gene is a recurrent driver, but conversely a high frequency of truncating/hotspot mutations in a known tumour suppressor is strong evidence. CHECK: compare TP53 and CDKN2A frequency to length-matched passenger genes and look at mutation type (truncating fraction, TP53 DNA-binding-domain hotspots, CDKN2A truncating/R80*/H83Y/D84N type changes). IF FOUND: if high frequency plus truncating/hotspot pattern, treat as recurrent driver; prefer dN/dS (dNdScv) or MutSigCV-style background-adjusted significance if time permits. SOURCE: Lawrence et al. 2013 Nature 'Mutational heterogeneity in cancer and the search for new cancer-associated genes' (nature.com/articles/nature12213); Martincorena et al. 2017 Cell dNdScv; not web-verified.

label: CDKN2A deletions missing from MAF
text: PITFALL: CDKN2A is frequently inactivated by homozygous deletion or promoter methylation rather than point mutation, and those events are absent from data_mutations.txt; the MAF-only frequency underestimates CDKN2A alteration. CHECK: there is no CNA file here, so report CDKN2A point-mutation frequency only and note it is a lower bound. IF FOUND: a modest but clearly nonzero CDKN2A mutation rate (published cSCC series typically roughly 20-50%, TP53 roughly 50-90%) still supports recurrence; do not call it False just because CDKN2A is below TP53. SOURCE: established cSCC genomics (e.g. Pickering et al. 2014 Clin Cancer Res; Li et al. 2015 Clin Cancer Res); not web-verified.

label: CDKN2A symbol/isoform check
text: PITFALL: Gene symbol and transcript issues: CDKN2A encodes p16INK4a and p14ARF via alternative transcripts, and the MAF uses mskcc isoforms; filtering on a single transcript or a wrong alias (P16, INK4A, ARF, CDKN2A-DT) can miss mutations. CHECK: grep Hugo_Symbol for CDKN2A, CDKN2A-AS1/DT, CDKN2B and confirm Entrez_Gene_Id 1029 for CDKN2A and 7157 for TP53. IF FOUND: count by Entrez ID / exact symbol and include all protein-altering consequences on either reading frame. SOURCE: HGNC/NCBI Gene; MAF spec; not web-verified.

label: Exclude germline polymorphisms
text: PITFALL: Germline or low-quality calls can inflate frequencies (e.g. TP53 P72R rs1042522 polymorphism, low-VAF artefacts). CHECK: look for dbSNP_RS common SNPs such as rs1042522 among TP53 rows, check t_alt_count/t_ref_count VAF and n_alt_count in matched normal. IF FOUND: exclude common germline polymorphisms and calls with alt reads in the normal before computing frequency. SOURCE: GDC MAF somatic filtering guidance (docs.gdc.cancer.gov); not web-verified.

label: Cancer type mismatch: PanNET data vs neuroblastoma claim
text: PITFALL: The dataset's cancer type may not match the hypothesis; these tables are pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (all 96 samples Oncotree PANET, MSK-IMPACT panel plus a few WGS pNET samples), while the hypothesis is about neuroblastoma. CHECK: tabulate CANCER_TYPE / ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt before any analysis. IF FOUND: under the benchmark convention a claim about a disease the tables do not cover is 'Not verifiable'; do not test a neuroblastoma claim on PanNET TERT calls. SOURCE: direct inspection of data headers (web search unavailable).

label: TERT rearrangement is not TERT mutation/CNA
text: PITFALL: TERT rearrangements (structural variants near TERT that juxtapose enhancers) are not the same as TERT promoter SNVs or TERT copy-number gains; substituting one for the other tests a different claim. CHECK: confirm whether any structural-variant/fusion table exists (here there is none: only mutations, CNA, seg, panel matrix). IF FOUND: absence of an SV table means rearrangements cannot be measured directly; do not relabel TERT mutation or CNA calls as rearrangements. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: High-risk neuroblastoma definition
text: PITFALL: 'High-risk' neuroblastoma is a defined COG/INRG category (age, stage, MYCN amplification, histology, ploidy); proxies like grade or survival in another tumour type are not equivalent. CHECK: look for a risk-group, INSS/INRG stage or MYCN status column. IF FOUND: if no such column and no neuroblastoma samples, the outcome variable is missing for the stated disease. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: TERT/MYCN/ATRX mutual exclusivity confounding
text: PITFALL: In neuroblastoma TERT rearrangements, MYCN amplification and ATRX alterations are largely mutually exclusive telomere-maintenance drivers, so comparing TERT-rearranged vs all others confounds with MYCN. CHECK: cross-tab TERT status with MYCN amplification and ATRX status. IF FOUND: compare within MYCN-non-amplified tumours or report the mutual exclusivity explicitly. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Panel coverage varies across IMPACT versions
text: PITFALL: Targeted panels (MSK-IMPACT 341/410/468) differ in TERT promoter coverage and SV probe design, so TERT calls are not uniform across samples. CHECK: use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt to see which panel each sample used. IF FOUND: restrict denominators to samples whose panel covers the feature, or stratify by panel. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Hypothesis is a reversed study finding
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis concerns a signature (IPRES) from the anti-PD-1 melanoma study whose tables these are (clinical has Pembrolizumab treatment and DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT CR/PR/PD; RNA-seq exists), so answering Not verifiable because no IPRES score column exists would be wrong under the benchmark convention. CHECK: confirm cancer type is melanoma, treatment anti-PD-1, response labels present, mRNA matrix present. IF FOUND: label must be True or False; build the score from the RNA genes and/or decide from established biology. SOURCE: task label convention (no web source; search tool failed).

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (e.g. VR-pNET-02-T1/T2, P-...-T02) inflate counts in association tests. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient before testing. SOURCE: direct inspection of data headers.

label: Define response groups correctly
text: PITFALL: Innate resistance means non-responders (PD) vs responders (CR/PR) on pre-treatment biopsies; mixing on-treatment biopsies, or treating SD ambiguously, changes group contrasts. CHECK: tabulate DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT / Treatment Response and Biopsy Time in data_clinical_sample.txt; keep only pre-treatment samples with RNA-seq; note previous MAPKi status. IF FOUND: restrict to pre-treatment, compare PD vs CR+PR, report a sensitivity analysis excluding MAPKi-pretreated patients (MAPKi itself induces mesenchymal/IPRES-like programs). SOURCE: Hugo et al. Cell 2016 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2016.02.065 (not web-verified).

label: Small counts need Fisher exact
text: PITFALL: With small groups (few altered tumours) chi-square tests are unreliable. CHECK: inspect 2x2 cell counts. IF FOUND: use Fisher's exact test and report effect size with CI. SOURCE: standard statistical practice.

label: Small n: per-gene tests underpowered
text: PITFALL: With ~27 RNA-seq samples (~13 vs ~14), single-gene DE after FDR correction will show few or no hits, which is not evidence of absence. CHECK: count samples per group with RNA. IF FOUND: use a gene-set level score (GSVA/ssGSEA/mean z-score of the signature genes) and test score vs response (Wilcoxon), and look at the direction/proportion of signature genes up in non-responders rather than requiring individual FDR-significant genes. SOURCE: Hanzelmann et al. BMC Bioinformatics 2013 doi:10.1186/1471-2105-14-7 (not web-verified).

label: GSVA on RPKM needs log/Gaussian kernel
text: PITFALL: Running GSVA/ssGSEA on raw RPKM with the Poisson kernel (meant for integer counts) or without log transform distorts scores. CHECK: inspect value range of data_mrna_seq_rpkm.txt (non-integer, heavy right tail). IF FOUND: log2(RPKM+1), filter low-expressed genes, use kcdf='Gaussian'; or use the provided z-score files and average z-scores per gene set. SOURCE: GSVA Bioconductor vignette https://bioconductor.org/packages/GSVA (not web-verified).

label: Signature is a set of gene sets, not one list
text: PITFALL: IPRES was defined as co-enrichment of ~26 gene sets (EMT, ECM remodeling, cell adhesion, angiogenesis, wound healing, MAPKi-induced/ AXL, WNT5A, TWIST2, LOXL2, TAGLN, ROR2, FAP, VEGFA etc.), not a single list; a few hand-picked genes may miss it. CHECK: assemble gene sets for EMT/mesenchymal (e.g. TWIST2, WNT5A, AXL, ROR2, LOXL2, TAGLN, FAP, FN1, VIM), angiogenesis (VEGFA, VEGFC, ANGPT2), ECM/adhesion (COL genes), wound healing (CCL2, CCL7, CCL8, CCL13, IL10) and check presence in the matrix. IF FOUND: score each set per sample and test co-enrichment in PD vs CR/PR; report direction for each set. SOURCE: Hugo et al. Cell 2016 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2016.02.065 (not web-verified).

label: Stroma/purity confounding
text: PITFALL: Mesenchymal/ECM/angiogenesis genes are largely expressed by fibroblasts and endothelium, so a signature difference may reflect stromal content, not tumor-cell state. CHECK: correlate signature score with ESTIMATE Stromal Score and Purity in data_clinical_sample.txt and compare those by response. IF FOUND: report both raw and purity/stroma-adjusted comparison; the hypothesis is about the bulk transcriptional signature, so the raw bulk contrast is the primary readout. SOURCE: Yoshihara et al. Nat Commun 2013 doi:10.1038/ncomms3612 (not web-verified).

label: Z-score reference file choice
text: PITFALL: The zscores_ref_diploid_samples file normalises to CNA-diploid samples per gene, which changes scale and can drop genes; mixing files gives inconsistent scores. CHECK: compare gene coverage and sample IDs across rpkm and both z-score files; confirm sample IDs (PtN) map to clinical. IF FOUND: use one matrix consistently, preferably log RPKM or ref_all_samples z-scores. SOURCE: cBioPortal file formats docs https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (not web-verified).

label: Duplicate/outlier samples
text: PITFALL: Individual outlier samples (e.g. very high-expression libraries) or duplicate biopsies per patient can drive a gene-set difference in n~27. CHECK: one sample per patient; plot per-sample signature scores by group; leave-one-out. IF FOUND: use rank-based tests and report robustness. SOURCE: general practice (not web-verified).

label: Cohort denominator
text: PITFALL: The dataset mixes four cohorts (INF_MLLr_Discovery n=22, INF_MLLr_Validation n=25, INF_NON_MLLr_Validation n=18, NON_INF_MLLr n=20), so counting all patients gives the wrong denominator for an 'infant MLL-R' frequency. CHECK: Restrict to patients with MLL_STATUS==INF_MLLr (discovery+validation, 47 patients), and also compute the discovery-only (WGS, 22) and validation-only rates. IF FOUND: Report the infant MLL-R rate on the 47-patient set as primary and the per-cohort rates as sensitivity checks; the published headline figure likely refers to all infant MLL-R cases. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Relapse samples double count
text: PITFALL: Some patients have both diagnosis and relapse samples (e.g. SJINF001 and SJINF001R), so per-sample counting inflates the denominator, and RAS clones are often lost or gained at relapse in MLL-R ALL. CHECK: Map Tumor_Sample_Barcode to PATIENT_ID through data_clinical_sample and count unique patients; tabulate how many hits come only from relapse samples. IF FOUND: Use the per-patient frequency based on diagnosis samples as primary and report the any-sample version separately. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Pathway gene set definition
text: PITFALL: 'Kinase-PI3K-RAS signaling' in infant MLL-R ALL papers covers more than KRAS and NRAS: FLT3, PTPN11, NF1, CBL, PIK3CA, PIK3R1, BRAF, and sometimes other kinases (e.g. FLT3 ITD/TKD). A narrow RAS-only set will undercount. CHECK: List every mutated gene in INF_MLLr patients and flag members of the RAS/MAPK, PI3K and receptor-tyrosine-kinase pathways; compute the patient fraction with at least one hit for a narrow set (KRAS/NRAS) and a broad set. IF FOUND: Use the broad set when testing the claim, and judge 47% against the broad-set fraction, not the RAS-only one. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Activating vs any mutation
text: PITFALL: The claim concerns ACTIVATING mutations; silent, intronic or truncating variants in oncogenes (KRAS, NRAS, FLT3, PIK3CA) are not activating, but truncating NF1, PTPN11-loss and CBL changes behave differently. CHECK: Tabulate Variant_Classification and HGVSp_Short for pathway genes; look for hotspots (KRAS/NRAS G12, G13, Q61; FLT3 D835 and ITD; PTPN11 exons 3/13; PIK3CA E545, H1047). IF FOUND: Drop Silent/UTR/intron calls, count hotspot or known-activating events (plus NF1 loss-of-function), and report both strict and lenient counts. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Subclonal low-VAF mutations
text: PITFALL: In infant MLL-R ALL, RAS/PI3K mutations are often subclonal (low VAF) and several can coexist in one patient. Studies count low-VAF calls, so dropping them with a VAF filter lowers the frequency, and counting mutations instead of patients raises it. CHECK: Compute VAF = t_alt_count/(t_ref+t_alt) for pathway hits and count distinct patients, not mutations. IF FOUND: Keep subclonal somatic calls; express the result as patients with at least one hit divided by the eligible patients. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Platform heterogeneity
text: PITFALL: The INF_MLLr discovery patients have WGS, while validation patients have Targeted_Seq (GENE_PANEL column), and their detection sensitivity and gene coverage differ, so rates can differ by cohort for technical reasons. CHECK: Compare pathway-hit rates between WGS and Targeted_Seq INF_MLLr patients, and confirm every pathway gene was in the targeted panel (data_gene_panel_matrix lists only panel names; check which genes ever appear among validation calls). IF FOUND: Report the pooled rate together with the per-platform rates, and do not treat zero calls for a gene outside the panel as wild-type. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Approximate-match tolerance and label logic
text: PITFALL: The claim gives an exact percentage (47%), and with n of about 47 one patient shifts the rate by about 2 points, so an exact match is unlikely even when the claim is true. CHECK: Compute the rate under reasonable definitions (broad vs narrow gene set, diagnosis vs any sample, all INF_MLLr vs discovery only) and see whether about 47% (roughly 22/47) falls within that range. IF FOUND: Call it True if a defensible definition gives about 45-50%; call it False only if every reasonable definition is far off (e.g. under 30% or over 65%). SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Non-infant and non-MLL contamination of evidence
text: PITFALL: NON_INF_MLLr samples are WES and mostly AML, and INF_NON_MLLr includes T-ALL; mixing them into the infant MLL-R count changes the rate, and LEUKEMIA_TYPE shows that even INF_MLLr contains one T-ALL and one mixed case. CHECK: Filter on MLL_STATUS rather than LEUKEMIA_TYPE, and use data_sv to confirm that each INF_MLLr patient has a KMT2A fusion. IF FOUND: Keep all INF_MLLr patients (the study defines the group by KMT2A status, not lineage) unless a patient lacks KMT2A evidence. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: pitfall unit patient
text: PITFALL: The dataset has 195 samples (158 intrahepatic, 37 extrahepatic CCA) and some patients have several samples (e.g. P-0000114 T01 and T02), so counting samples inflates or deflates the per-patient actionable fraction. CHECK: count unique PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID and collapse alterations to the patient level (a patient is altered if any sample is). IF FOUND: report the proportion over unique patients. SOURCE: domain knowledge (research tool unavailable, no URL retrieved).

label: pitfall actionable definition
text: PITFALL: 'Potential therapeutic implications' depends on the definition. A narrow one (OncoKB level 1-2 / FDA-approved: IDH1 hotspots R132, FGFR2 fusions, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, MSI-H/TMB-high, NTRK fusions) gives a different percentage than a broad one (levels 1-4 incl. investigational: also PIK3CA hotspots, KRAS G12C, BRCA1/2, CDKN2A, MDM2/CDK4 amp, FGFR1-3 alterations, IDH2), and broad MSK-IMPACT CCA studies typically report actionable fractions well above 20% (often ~40-50%). CHECK: compute the fraction under both a narrow and a broad gene/variant list built from the data (mutations hotspots, data_sv fusions, data_cna amplifications = 2). IF FOUND: if even the narrow definition gives a value far from 20%, that is evidence against the claim; state which definition was used. SOURCE: domain knowledge, OncoKB levels https://www.oncokb.org/levels (not retrieved).

label: pitfall no oncokb annotation
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt has no OncoKB/oncogenic annotation columns, so counting every mutation in a 'targetable gene' (e.g. any IDH1 or PIK3CA variant, VUS, synonymous) overcalls actionability. CHECK: look at Variant_Classification and HGVSp_Short; keep only known hotspots (IDH1 R132, IDH2 R140/R172, BRAF V600E, PIK3CA E542/E545/H1047, KRAS G12C) and truncating mutations in tumor suppressors (BRCA1/2). Drop Silent/intronic. IF FOUND: use the hotspot-restricted counts as the primary estimate. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no URL retrieved).

label: pitfall fusions cna
text: PITFALL: Key CCA targets are not point mutations. FGFR2 fusions (in data_sv.txt, e.g. AHCYL1-FGFR2 in-frame) and ERBB2/MDM2/CDK4 amplifications (data_cna.txt value 2) are missed if only data_mutations.txt is used, which underestimates the actionable fraction. CHECK: merge mutations, SV (filter SV_Status SOMATIC and in-frame/functional FGFR2 or NTRK fusions) and CNA (use only GISTIC 2 = amplification, -2 = deep deletion; ignore +/-1). IF FOUND: compute the union across all three alteration types per patient. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no URL retrieved).

label: pitfall panel coverage
text: PITFALL: Samples were run on IMPACT341 (54) and IMPACT410 (141) panels, and some genes (or SV/CNA calls) may be missing from the older panel, so treating an unprofiled gene as wild-type biases the fraction. CHECK: use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and the panel gene lists to confirm each actionable gene is on each sample's panel; check that the denominators for mutation/cna/sv profiling are equal. IF FOUND: restrict the denominator per gene to profiled samples, or note the bias. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no URL retrieved).

label: pitfall subtype mix
text: PITFALL: Actionable alteration frequency differs a lot by subtype. IDH1/2 mutations and FGFR2 fusions are concentrated in intrahepatic CCA (~15-20% each), while extrahepatic CCA has more KRAS/ERBB2. A pooled estimate can differ from one for a single subtype. CHECK: tabulate the actionable fraction separately for CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED intrahepatic vs extrahepatic as well as pooled. IF FOUND: report both, and judge the claim against the cohort-level (pooled) figure unless the claim names a subtype. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no URL retrieved).

label: pitfall approximate claim
text: PITFALL: A '20%' claim judged by exact equality, or by a single definition, can flip the label. CHECK: compute a 95% CI (Wilson) for the patient-level proportion under the narrow and broad definitions. IF FOUND: if the CI under reasonable definitions excludes ~20% by a wide margin (e.g. the observed value is 40-50%), lean False; if it includes ~20%, lean True. Note that in these benchmarks a 'reversed' or altered number is common. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no URL retrieved).

label: pitfall germline msi

IF FOUND: add MSI-H patients to the actionable set under the narrow definition. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no URL retrieved).

label: activating vs inactivating direction
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis direction word (activating vs inactivating) decides the label; AKT1, KRAS/HRAS/NRAS and AURKA are oncogenes whose resistance-relevant alterations are gain-of-function (hotspots such as AKT1 E17K, RAS G12/G13/Q61, AURKA amplification), so a claim of 'inactivating' alterations in them differs from the usual biology. CHECK: In data_mutations.txt tabulate Variant_Classification and HGVSp_Short for AKT1/KRAS/HRAS/NRAS/AURKA, and count truncating (Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site) versus recurrent hotspot missense. IF FOUND: If the variants are hotspot missense with no truncating ones, treat them as activating; that is evidence against an 'inactivating' claim, not for it. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable: HTTP 403).

label: in-scope study
text: PITFALL: The dataset is HR+ metastatic breast cancer WES biopsies with a CDK4/6i phenotype (BX_PHENOTYPE: Sensitive 18, Intrinsic Resistance 28, Acquired Resistance 13), so a hypothesis about CDK4/6i resistance genes is about this study and should get True/False, not Not verifiable. CHECK: Confirm the cancer type, BX_PHENOTYPE and BRR/treatment-duration columns. IF FOUND: Treat it as an in-study claim and judge direction and mechanism, using established biology where the mutation table alone is underpowered. SOURCE: data headers plus the benchmark convention.

label: Copy-neutral LOH not seen in log ratios
text: PITFALL: A seg.mean (log2 ratio) near 0 on 16q does not rule out LOH, because copy-neutral LOH is invisible in total copy-number log ratios; the curated LOH_16Q flag was likely called with allele-specific methods (e.g. FACETS on MSK-IMPACT). CHECK: compare LOH_16Q flag with 16q mean seg.mean per sample. IF FOUND: discordance, trust LOH_16Q over seg-derived loss; use seg only as a sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: general knowledge of allele-specific CN (FACETS, Shen & Seshan 2016 NAR), no web access.

label: resistance phenotype definition
text: PITFALL: 'Resistance' can mean intrinsic (progression soon after starting) or acquired (progression after an initial response), and pooling them, or using BRR alone, can hide the signal. CHECK: Compare carriers across Sensitive vs Intrinsic vs Acquired BX_PHENOTYPE and against treatment duration. IF FOUND: Report the groups separately and use resistant-vs-sensitive as the primary contrast. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Use Fisher exact on small 2x2
text: PITFALL: Small cohort (tens of tumours) makes chi-square invalid and p-values unstable. CHECK: count VS x LOH_16Q 2x2 cells, drop missing/NA/blank rows. IF FOUND: expected counts <5, use two-sided Fisher exact test and report odds ratio with CI; judge by direction and effect size, not only p<0.05, since the original paper may report a trend-level association. SOURCE: standard statistical guidance, no web access.

label: One sample per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (bilateral tumours, re-sampled tumours) inflate n and violate independence. CHECK: count unique PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID; inspect BILATERAL. IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient (or per eye) and rerun. SOURCE: standard practice, no web access.

label: Confounding in RB 16q analysis
text: PITFALL: Confounding by prior therapy or by other high-risk features (e.g. 1q gain, MYCN, BCOR) and by laterality: unilateral sporadic RB more often carries 16q loss and presents at advanced stage with seeding. CHECK: stratify VS vs LOH_16Q by PRIOR_THERAPY and BILATERAL. IF FOUND: report stratified/Mantel-Haenszel result alongside crude. SOURCE: retinoblastoma biology knowledge, no web access.

label: VS vs SRS column
text: PITFALL: Label confusion between vitreous seeds (VS) and subretinal seeds (SRS) or other invasion columns. CHECK: confirm column VS is used, not SRS. IF FOUND: rerun with correct column; SRS association can be reported separately. SOURCE: data header, no web access.

label: Prior direction 16q-vitreous seeds
text: PITFALL: Prior literature (MSK retinoblastoma IMPACT studies) reports 16q loss associated with diffuse vitreous seeding; established biology supports a positive direction, so an underpowered non-significant result in a small cohort is not evidence for False unless the direction is opposite or effect is null. CHECK: odds ratio direction. IF FOUND: OR>1 with notable enrichment, lean True; OR<=1, lean False. SOURCE: domain knowledge, no web access.

label: interaction vs separate p-values
text: PITFALL: Concluding that a subgroup-outcome association differs between adult (aBL) and pediatric (pBL) cohorts because it is significant in one cohort and not the other (difference-in-significance fallacy). CHECK: Fit a Cox model OS ~ PATIENT_SUBGROUP * AGE_CATEGORY (and PFS) and look at the interaction term; also report the hazard ratio of IC-BL vs DGG-BL separately within Adult and Pediatric with CIs. IF FOUND: Base 'differs between cohorts' on the interaction test and on the direction/size of the per-cohort HRs, not on p<0.05 in one cohort only. SOURCE: Altman & Bland BMJ 2003;326:219 (unverified, search tool down).

label: likely paper finding direction
text: PITFALL: The benchmark hypothesis is probably a reversed paper finding. The source BLGSP study likely reported that genetic subgroups (DGG-BL, IC-BL, Q53-BL, M53-BL) carried different prognosis in pediatric vs adult BL (e.g. DGG-BL better outcome in pBL, IC-BL worse in aBL). CHECK: Compare per-cohort survival by subgroup; check whether the hazard direction for IC-BL and DGG-BL flips or changes between Adult and Pediatric. IF FOUND: A visible cohort-specific association (even with a modest interaction p-value given small n) argues the hypothesis is False; don't default to True just because the interaction p>0.05 with ~200 patients. SOURCE: domain reasoning, no source retrieved.

label: few events per cell
text: PITFALL: Small cohorts with few deaths per subgroup-by-age cell make Cox estimates unstable (monotone likelihood, infinite HRs) and interaction tests very underpowered. CHECK: Tabulate n and number of events (OS_STATUS starting with 1, PFS_STATUS starting with 1) per PATIENT_SUBGROUP x AGE_CATEGORY cell; flag cells with <5 events. IF FOUND: Use log-rank within each cohort plus Firth-penalized Cox (coxphf) for the interaction; read a non-significant interaction as 'not detected' rather than as proof of no difference. SOURCE: Peduzzi et al. J Clin Epidemiol 1995 (events-per-variable); Heinze & Schemper 2001 Biometrics (unverified).

label: parsing survival columns
text: PITFALL: Statuses are strings like '1:DECEASED' and '1:Progression'; parsing them wrong, or keeping patients with missing or NA months, corrupts the survival analysis. Clinical files have 4 '#' header lines and the 'Overall Survival ' column name has a trailing space. CHECK: Parse the event as int(status.split(':')[0]); drop rows with NA OS_MONTHS; check the value counts of PATIENT_SUBGROUP and AGE_CATEGORY (expected Adult/Pediatric; subgroups may include unclassified/NA). IF FOUND: Exclude unclassified subgroup samples or treat them as a separate level; do not merge them into IC-BL or DGG-BL. SOURCE: file inspection.

label: confounding by EBV/site
text: PITFALL: Cohort (age category) is confounded with EBV status, HIV status and treatment site (Uganda/Malawi vs US/Europe), so an apparent cohort difference in subgroup prognosis may reflect geography or EBV. CHECK: Cross-tabulate PATIENT_SUBGROUP by AGE_CATEGORY, EBV_GENOME_STATUS, HIV_STATUS and SOURCE (clinical_sample). IF FOUND: Run sensitivity Cox models adjusted for or stratified by EBV/HIV/site; still interpret the main hypothesis as a subgroup-by-age effect. SOURCE: general epidemiology; no source retrieved.

label: proportional hazards
text: PITFALL: Non-proportional hazards or crossing KM curves make a single HR or log-rank test misleading (BL deaths cluster early, within the first ~12 months). CHECK: Plot KM curves by subgroup within each age cohort; run cox.zph / lifelines check_assumptions. IF FOUND: Report landmark or RMST comparisons, or Fleming-Harrington weighted log-rank tests, alongside the HR. SOURCE: Grambsch & Therneau 1994 Biometrika (unverified).

label: Study scope
text: CONTEXT: The dataset is a uveal melanoma (Oncotree UM) cohort with WES/WGS samples (QIMR Berghofer and others); GNAQ, GNA11, CYSLTR2 and PLCB4 are the canonical Gq-pathway drivers of uveal melanoma, so a PLCB4/GNAQ/GNA11 exclusivity hypothesis is about this study and should be labelled True or False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: outcomes and contrasts
text: PITFALL: Testing only OS or only one subgroup contrast can miss the reported association; the claim covers IC-BL and DGG-BL and 'patient outcomes' (OS and PFS). CHECK: Run both OS and PFS; compare each subgroup against all other subgroups (one vs rest) within each cohort. IF FOUND: If any of these shows a clear cohort-specific association, that contradicts 'do not have associations that differ'; account for multiple testing but weigh effect sizes too. SOURCE: analysis design; no source retrieved.

label: Match exact variant
text: PITFALL: Counting any PLCB4 mutation instead of the specific hotspot p.D630Y (and GNAQ/GNA11 passengers instead of Q209/R183 hotspots) inflates or deflates co-occurrence. CHECK: grep HGVSp_Short for PLCB4 p.D630 and list GNAQ/GNA11 protein changes per Tumor_Sample_Barcode. IF FOUND: test exclusivity of the hotspot carriers vs GNAQ/GNA11 hotspot carriers, and report non-hotspot co-mutations separately. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Small counts
text: PITFALL: With very few PLCB4 D630Y carriers (typically 1-3% of uveal melanomas), a Fisher test for mutual exclusivity has no power, so a non-significant p-value is not evidence against exclusivity. CHECK: count carriers and inspect the 2x2 table directly. IF FOUND: decide on the observed overlap (zero overlapping samples = consistent with exclusivity) plus established biology, not on p-value. SOURCE: domain knowledge; cf. DISCOVER (Canisius et al. 2016 Genome Biol) on test calibration.

label: Sample vs patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (primary + metastasis, cell lines) can double count or create false co-occurrence across samples. CHECK: compare PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID counts and SAMPLE_CLASS/SAMPLE_TYPE. IF FOUND: collapse to one row per patient (or per tumour) before building the co-occurrence table. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Hypermutators
text: PITFALL: Hypermutated tumours (e.g. MBD4-deficient or high TMB) carry many passenger mutations and can produce spurious co-occurrence of PLCB4 with GNAQ/GNA11. CHECK: look at TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS / mutation counts of any sample carrying both. IF FOUND: note the co-occurrence is likely a passenger hit and check whether both are hotspots and VAF is clonal. SOURCE: domain knowledge; DISCOVER paper on mutation-rate heterogeneity.

label: Coverage denominator
text: PITFALL: Samples not sequenced across the relevant genes (panel/WGS-only with no MAF entries) are silently treated as wild-type. CHECK: use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and restrict to samples present in the mutation file / profiled. IF FOUND: restrict the denominator to profiled samples. SOURCE: cBioPortal data format docs (docs.cbioportal.org).

label: Variant filters
text: PITFALL: The MAF may include germline/low-VAF or non-somatic calls; a low-VAF co-occurring call may be artefact. CHECK: t_alt_count/t_ref_count VAF and Mutation_Status of any overlapping GNAQ/GNA11/PLCB4 call. IF FOUND: report with and without low-VAF calls. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Single co-occurrence
text: PITFALL: Treating one co-occurring sample as automatically refuting a published exclusivity claim (or ignoring it). CHECK: count samples with both PLCB4 D630Y and a GNAQ/GNA11 hotspot. IF FOUND: if zero overlap, the data support exclusivity (True); if a clear clonal hotspot co-occurrence exists, weigh it as contradicting evidence and explain. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: benefit endpoint definition
text: PITFALL: In this dataset the patient column DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT actually holds RECIST best response (CR/PR/SD/PD/X), not a yes/no benefit flag, and RESPONSE_DURATION is empty; treating SD as benefit or non-benefit without a rule changes the groups. CHECK: tabulate DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT and cross-tab it against OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS. IF FOUND: define clinical benefit the standard way for ipilimumab cohorts (CR/PR, or SD with durable control or survival over about 1 year) versus PD/minimal benefit; run a sensitivity analysis with SD split both ways, treat X as not evaluable, and also test against OS. SOURCE: general ICB biomarker practice (no web retrieval possible; search tool returned HTTP 403).

label: skewed TMB use rank test
text: PITFALL: Mutational load is strongly right-skewed with outliers, so t-tests or Pearson correlation on raw counts can be driven by a few hypermutated tumours. CHECK: look at the distribution of MUTATION_LOAD / TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS by group. IF FOUND: use a Mann-Whitney U test (the standard test in ipilimumab TMB studies) or log-transform the counts; report medians and the p-value. SOURCE: standard nonparametric practice (search tool was unavailable).

label: which load variable
text: PITFALL: Several mutational-load variables exist (MUTATION_LOAD nonsynonymous count, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS per Mb, NEOAGCNT neoantigens, and counts you could recompute from data_mutations.txt), and they can disagree in significance. CHECK: compute the association with each one, and check that the recomputed counts match MUTATION_LOAD. IF FOUND: make the precomputed nonsynonymous MUTATION_LOAD the primary test because the hypothesis says overall mutational load; report the others as secondary. Do not swap to neoantigens unless load is missing. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: association vs prediction
text: PITFALL: In landmark CTLA-4 melanoma cohorts, mutational load is associated with clinical benefit but does not separate the groups cleanly: the distributions overlap heavily, and many high-load patients do not benefit. A modest p-value can still be the published finding. CHECK: report the group medians, the Mann-Whitney p-value and the AUC. IF FOUND: judge significance on p<0.05 for the primary benefit-versus-no-benefit comparison; do not call it False just because prediction is weak (an AUC around 0.6 to 0.7 is typical). SOURCE: domain knowledge of the ipilimumab genomics literature (search unavailable).

label: TMB column exists in cervical cohort
text: PITFALL: Concluding 'Not verifiable' when a TMB variable is in fact present; this dataset's data_clinical_sample.txt has a TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS column (mut/Mb) and all samples have CANCER_TYPE 'Cervical Cancer' (MSK-IMPACT cohort), so the hypothesis is about this study. CHECK: Confirm the column and cancer type exist, then count samples/patients with TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS > 10. IF FOUND: Label True/False from the counts, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: data header inspection (web search unavailable).

label: cutoff and immortal time
text: PITFALL: Survival-based analyses that use benefit groups defined from later outcomes (for example, survival over 1 year) suffer guaranteed-time/immortal-time bias, and dichotomising TMB at the median or an optimised cutoff inflates significance. CHECK: see whether any survival test conditions on post-baseline status or uses a data-driven cutoff. IF FOUND: for OS, use TMB as a continuous (log) covariate in a Cox model or a pre-specified cutoff; keep the benefit-group test as the primary analysis for this hypothesis. SOURCE: standard survival-analysis guidance (search unavailable).

label: Universal claim refuted by one case
text: PITFALL: A universal-negative claim ('no patient has TMB>10') is refuted by a single valid patient above threshold; analysts may wrongly use median or mean TMB. CHECK: Report max TMB and number of patients with TMB>10 (and >=10), deduplicated by PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: Even one well-supported patient >10 mut/Mb contradicts the hypothesis (False). SOURCE: logic of the claim; FDA pembrolizumab TMB-H approval uses >=10 mut/Mb https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/fda-approves-pembrolizumab-adults-and-children-tmb-h-solid-tumors (not retrieved).

label: sample QC and joins
text: PITFALL: Mismatched samples (tumour without a matched normal) or samples missing exome data inflate or lack mutation counts, and patients with RECIST X (not evaluable) can contaminate the groups. CHECK: SOMATIC_STATUS values, missing MUTATION_LOAD, and the count of X responses; also make sure there is one sample per patient when joining the patient and sample tables. IF FOUND: exclude non-evaluable patients and samples lacking load data; rerun the test excluding unmatched samples as a sensitivity check. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: TMB denominator per panel
text: PITFALL: Recomputing TMB from data_mutations.txt with a wrong denominator (e.g. whole exome 30-38 Mb, or one panel size for all) or including silent/intronic variants gives wrong values; MSK-IMPACT panels differ in size (IMPACT341 ~0.98 Mb, IMPACT410 ~1.06 Mb, IMPACT468 ~1.14 Mb). CHECK: Prefer the provided TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS; if recomputing, count nonsynonymous coding mutations per sample divided by the sample's GENE_PANEL size and compare to the provided column. IF FOUND: Use the provided column as primary evidence. SOURCE: Zehir et al. 2017 Nat Med https://doi.org/10.1038/nm.4333 ; Samstein et al. 2019 Nat Genet https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-018-0312-8 (not retrieved).

label: confounding and power
text: PITFALL: Confounders such as M stage, LDH, prior therapy or tumour site can partly explain benefit, but in a cohort of about 110 patients multivariable models are underpowered. CHECK: whether MUTATION_LOAD differs by M_STAGE or LDH. IF FOUND: report the univariate test as primary (matching how the original-style finding is stated) and the adjusted logistic model as supporting evidence; a loss of significance after adjustment alone should not flip the label to False. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Patient vs sample level
text: PITFALL: Counting multiple samples from one patient (primary + metastasis, T01/T02) inflates counts of TMB-high patients. CHECK: Group by PATIENT_ID and take per-patient max or one sample per patient; report both. IF FOUND: State results at patient level since the hypothesis is about patients. SOURCE: standard cBioPortal sample/patient structure (web not retrieved).

label: Hypermutation biology in cervix
text: PITFALL: TMB-high outliers in cervical cancer are often driven by MSI-H/MMR deficiency, POLE mutations or APOBEC hypermutation, and an analyst might dismiss them as artefacts. CHECK: For samples with TMB>10, look at MSI_TYPE/MSI_SCORE, POLE/MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 mutations in data_mutations.txt, and TUMOR_PURITY/SAMPLE_COVERAGE. IF FOUND: Biologically explained hypermutation is real TMB-high and supports False; only exclude samples with clear QC failure. Established biology: TCGA cervical cancer (Nature 2017, https://doi.org/10.1038/nature21386, not retrieved) reports hypermutated, APOBEC-high tumors, so TMB-high cervical cancer is known to exist (KEYNOTE-158 included TMB-H cervical cases).

label: Threshold and histology checks
text: PITFALL: Threshold edge cases (>10 vs >=10) and non-cervical histologies can sway borderline counts. CHECK: Count both >10 and >=10; check CANCER_TYPE and CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED/ONCOTREE_CODE (e.g. CESC, GCEMU, adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine) to make sure the TMB-high samples are cervical primaries. IF FOUND: Report counts by histology; any cervical-cancer patient above 10 still refutes the claim. SOURCE: OncoTree https://oncotree.mskcc.org (not retrieved).

label: Purity, coverage, matched normal
text: PITFALL: Low tumor purity or low coverage underestimates panel TMB, and unmatched (tumor-only) samples overestimate it by keeping germline variants. CHECK: Inspect TUMOR_PURITY, SAMPLE_COVERAGE and SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched vs Unmatched) for TMB-high samples. IF FOUND: Treat Unmatched TMB-high samples with caution, but matched high-purity samples above 10 are solid evidence. SOURCE: Chalmers et al. 2017 Genome Med https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-017-0424-2 ; Merino et al. 2020 JITC TMB harmonization https://doi.org/10.1136/jitc-2019-000147 (not retrieved).

label: platform confounds mutation counts
text: PITFALL: The samples mix sequencing types (GENE_PANEL column has WGS and exome-type samples, IDs ICGC_MB* vs MB_Exm*), so raw mutation counts per sample are not comparable and platform can confound age. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL by sample and compare age distributions and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS across platforms. IF FOUND: use per-Mb TMB (TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS or coding-only nonsynonymous counts), test age within each platform, or adjust for platform; do not correlate raw counts from data_mutations.txt across platforms. SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable).

CHECK: plot TMB vs age, list top TMB samples and LFS samples. IF FOUND: use Spearman rank correlation as the primary test, and report results with and without LFS/hypermutator samples. SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: subgroup confounding
text: PITFALL: Medulloblastoma subgroups (WNT, SHH, Group 3, Group 4 in SUBGROUP) differ in age distribution (SHH bimodal infants+adults, Group 3 young children) so a pooled age-mutation correlation can be confounded by subgroup. CHECK: tabulate subgroup by age and TMB; compute Spearman within subgroup. IF FOUND: report pooled and subgroup-stratified/partial correlations (e.g. regression log(TMB) ~ age + subgroup); a consistent positive direction within subgroups strengthens a True call. SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: hypothesis is testable here
text: PITFALL: Background knowledge: somatic mutation burden rises with age in most cancers via clock-like (SBS1/SBS5) mutagenesis, and in medulloblastoma genome sequencing studies adults/older patients were reported to carry more somatic mutations than infants; analysts may wrongly answer Not verifiable because no explicit 'mutation rate' column exists. CHECK: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in data_clinical_sample.txt and per-sample counts in data_mutations.txt are valid mutation-rate proxies; AGE is in data_clinical_patient.txt. IF FOUND: the hypothesis is about this cohort (medulloblastoma, has age and mutations), so the label must be True or False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: counting mutations correctly
text: PITFALL: Mutation counts per sample derived from data_mutations.txt miss samples with zero mutations and may include silent/noncoding or duplicate rows, biasing rates. CHECK: join on Tumor_Sample_Barcode to the full sample list (header '#sequenced samples'), fill zeros, inspect Variant_Classification. IF FOUND: count consistently (e.g. all or nonsynonymous only) and include zero-mutation sequenced samples. SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: skew and join checks

CHECK: verify PATIENT_ID-SAMPLE_ID join count, missing AGE, units (years). IF FOUND: use Spearman or log-transformed TMB, report n, rho and p, and check direction is robust to leaving out adults (age>=18). SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: No expression data in tables
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about transcriptional output (JAK-STAT, hypoxia, immune pathways), but /biodsa-data holds only clinical, mutation (MAF) and MutSig tables, with no RNA-seq or pathway scores, so it cannot be tested directly; calling it 'Not verifiable' only for that reason goes against the benchmark convention. IF FOUND: the hypothesis is about this study's cancer, gene and cohort, so the label must be True/False, decided from established biology plus whatever proxies the tables offer. SOURCE: benchmark task text; no web source (search tool down).

label: Established PBRM1 biology
text: PITFALL: Analysts may guess the direction of the PBRM1 effect. Established biology: PBRM1 loss in ccRCC amplifies HIF/hypoxia transcription (Nargund et al. 2017 Cell Rep) and, in RNA-seq of anti-PD-1-treated ccRCC, PBRM1 loss-of-function tumours showed changed (mostly reduced) IL6/JAK-STAT3 and immune-signaling gene expression and enriched hypoxia signatures (Miao et al. 2018 Science, nivolumab ccRCC WES+RNA cohort). CHECK: see whether the clinical table describes an anti-PD-1 nivolumab ccRCC cohort (DRUG=Nivolumab, CA209 trial barcodes). IF FOUND: established biology supports 'altered' transcription in all three pathway groups. The hypothesis says 'alters', not a direction, so a direction mismatch should not turn it to False. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aan5951 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2017.03.007 (from prior knowledge, not retrieved).
