label: Define PBRM1 LOF properly
text: PITFALL: Counting every PBRM1 mutation (including silent/Splice_Region synonymous or missense VUS) as 'loss' misclassifies tumours. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification for PBRM1 in data_mutations.txt; keep nonsense, frameshift indels, canonical splice site and translation-start changes; look at allele fraction (t_alt_count/(t_ref+t_alt)) relative to PURITY to infer biallelic loss (chr3p LOH is near-universal in ccRCC). IF FOUND: define PBRM1-LOF as truncating mutations only and run missense as a sensitivity check. SOURCE: MAF spec https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/ (not retrieved).

label: Sample/patient ID mismatch and WES-only subset
text: PITFALL: The MAF uses Tumor_Sample_Barcode IDs such as RCC_20-Tumor-SM-A46EG and RCC-CA209009 normals, while the clinical table uses PATIENT_ID RCC_n, so a naive join drops or mismatches patients; also, patients with no MAF rows are not necessarily wild-type, because only sequenced samples count. CHECK: map MAF barcodes to SAMPLE_ID in data_clinical_sample and check that every sample with ALL_MUTS>0 is in the MAF; restrict to SEQUENCING_TYPE=whole-exome and to tumours that pass QC. IF FOUND: make the denominator the sequenced samples only and call PBRM1-WT only among them. label: Small-n association test

label: Endpoint: BCR is DFS columns
text: PITFALL: The endpoint is mislabelled; in these tables biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy is coded as DFS_MONTHS/DFS_STATUS (values like '0:DiseaseFree' / '1:Recurred'), not as a column named BCR, and OS_STATUS or METASTATIC_DISEASE are different endpoints. CHECK: tabulate DFS_STATUS values and confirm the event string; parse the leading digit as the event indicator. IF FOUND: use DFS_MONTHS + DFS_STATUS as the BCR time-to-event outcome; do not conclude 'Not verifiable' just because no column is literally named BCR. SOURCE: general knowledge (cBioPortal clinical-file convention); web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: CNA burden variable exists
text: PITFALL: A ready-made CNA burden variable already exists: data_clinical_sample.txt column CNA_DATA (e.g. 2.93, 0.16) is a per-sample burden score (percent genome altered type), so recomputing from data_cna.txt with ad hoc thresholds can give a different, noisier measure. CHECK: inspect the #-description lines for CNA_DATA, its range and its correlation with a fraction-genome-altered computed from data_cna_hg19.seg (|seg.mean| > ~0.2-0.3, length-weighted). IF FOUND: use CNA_DATA as the primary exposure and the seg-derived FGA as a sensitivity check. SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Use survival methods for BCR
text: PITFALL: Treating the binary recurrence status with a t-test/Mann-Whitney or logistic regression ignores censoring and unequal follow-up, and can hide or fake an association. CHECK: look at the distribution of DFS_MONTHS among non-recurrent patients (many short follow-ups => heavy censoring). IF FOUND: use Cox proportional hazards on continuous burden (and log-rank on a pre-specified split such as median or quartiles); report HR, CI, p and concordance; check proportional hazards with Schoenfeld residuals. SOURCE: general survival-analysis knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Cutpoint optimisation bias
text: PITFALL: Choosing the high/low CNA-burden cutpoint after looking at outcomes (optimal-cutpoint/minimum-p search) inflates type I error. CHECK: whether the dichotomisation threshold was chosen from the data. IF FOUND: primary test on continuous (or log/rank-transformed) burden or a pre-specified quantile split; if a cutpoint search is used, correct p-values (e.g. maximally selected rank statistics) or bootstrap. SOURCE: general knowledge (Altman et al. 1994 JNCI on optimal cutpoints); web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Skewed burden distribution
text: PITFALL: CNA burden is right-skewed with outliers; a few extreme genomes can dominate a linear Cox term, or a mostly-zero distribution can weaken power. CHECK: histogram/quantiles of CNA_DATA; count samples near zero. IF FOUND: log1p or rank-transform burden, or use quartiles; report results are robust across transforms. SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Confounding by Gleason/stage
text: PITFALL: CNA burden correlates strongly with Gleason grade, pathological stage, SVI/LNI/ECE and PSA, so a univariable association may be read as 'not independent' and wrongly labelled no-association, or a null in an overadjusted model wrongly taken as no association. CHECK: fit univariable Cox and then multivariable Cox adjusting for PATH_GLEASON_SCORE, PSA (log), PATH_T_STAGE, SVI, LNI, ECE; also check within-Gleason-7 subgroup. IF FOUND: the hypothesis is about association; a significant univariable association contradicts 'not associated' even if attenuated after adjustment; report both and watch events-per-variable (~10 events per covariate). SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: ID matching and missingness
text: PITFALL: Sample/patient ID mismatches and duplicates between data_cna.txt / seg / clinical tables, or samples lacking CNA data, silently drop or misalign patients. CHECK: verify join on PATIENT_ID/SAMPLE_ID, count samples with NaN CNA_DATA, and confirm one sample per patient. IF FOUND: restrict to matched primary samples with both CNA and DFS data and report N and event count. SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Power and null interpretation
text: PITFALL: Small event counts in single-institution prostatectomy cohorts give low power, so a non-significant p-value is not evidence of no association. CHECK: count BCR events; compute HR with 95% CI. IF FOUND: interpret a null cautiously; weigh the effect direction and CI and the well-established biology that genomic instability/CNA burden predicts BCR and metastasis in prostate cancer before labelling the hypothesis True. SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Adjuvant treatment confounding
text: PITFALL: Post-operative adjuvant radiotherapy/hormone therapy and neoadjuvant treatment alter recurrence timing and may be given preferentially to high-risk (high-CNA) patients. CHECK: tabulate ADJUVANT_HORMONE_THERAPY, RADIATION_TREATMENT_ADJUVANT, RADIATION_TREATMENT_NEOADJUVANT. IF FOUND: sensitivity analysis excluding treated patients or adjusting for treatment. SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: Race-subtype confounding; expected direction
text: PITFALL: Race is strongly confounded with histology/molecular subtype in endometrial cancer: Black patients have more serous/clear-cell, CN-high/TP53abn tumors and fewer endometrioid MMRd/MSI-H and POLE tumors, so MSI-H/TMB-high is generally expected to be LESS frequent in Black than White patients (established biology, e.g. TCGA/MSK ancestry studies). CHECK: crosstab RACE (patient file) x MOLECULAR_SUBTYPE and HISTOLOGY (sample file), Black vs White only. IF FOUND: report crude rates and also stratified by histology; a hypothesis that TMB-H/MSI-H is MORE frequent in Black patients is likely a reversed finding -> label False if data show lower/equal rates. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool unavailable); cf. https://www.cancer.gov/tcga (TCGA UCEC, Nature 2013).

label: actionability definition drives fraction
text: PITFALL: 'Clinically actionable' in mCRPC genomics papers (e.g. SU2C 2015) is defined broadly by pathway: AR (amp/mut/AR-related), PI3K (PTEN loss, PIK3CA/PIK3CB/AKT1), DNA repair (BRCA2, BRCA1, ATM, CDK12, FANCA, mismatch repair, including germline), RAF/MEK (BRAF/RAF1 fusions/muts), CDK/cyclin (CCND1 amp, CDKN2A loss), Wnt (APC, CTNNB1); a narrow OncoKB level 1 list gives a far lower fraction. CHECK: count patients with >=1 alteration in each category separately and cumulatively, with and without AR. IF FOUND: report the fraction under the study-style broad definition, since the hypothesis is the study's claim, and note sensitivity. SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26000489/

CHECK: data_clinical_sample.txt shows ONCOTREE_CODE=CHRCC (TCGA KICH cohort), so the hypothesis matches this study's cancer type and gene. label: germline missing undercount
text: PITFALL: Germline pathogenic DNA-repair variants (e.g. germline BRCA2/ATM, ~8% of mCRPC) are not in a somatic MAF, so a somatic-only count undercounts actionable cases. CHECK: look for Mutation_Status=Germline rows in data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND/absent: if germline absent, expect the computed fraction to sit a few points below the published figure and do not reject the claim on a small shortfall. SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27433846/

label: TERT is lowly expressed; normalise and compare carefully
text: PITFALL: TERT is a very low-abundance transcript, so most samples have RSEM near zero and means are dominated by a few outliers. CHECK: in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt count samples with TERT RSEM = 0 or <1 and look at the distribution (log2(x+1)). IF FOUND: report the fraction of tumours with clearly elevated TERT (e.g. outliers vs bulk) rather than a mean; 'highly elevated' in a subset is consistent with rearrangement-driven activation in a minority of tumours. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: CNA thresholds
text: PITFALL: data_cna.txt is GISTIC-style (-2,-1,0,1,2); counting -1/+1 (shallow, often arm-level) as actionable inflates to ~100%. CHECK: tabulate values for AR, PTEN, BRCA2, CDKN2A, CCND1. IF FOUND: use only -2 (deep deletion) and +2 (amplification) as aberrations. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: Compare to normals, not only within tumours
text: PITFALL: Z-scores relative to all samples only rank tumours against each other and cannot show elevation versus normal kidney. CHECK: use data_RNA_Seq_v2_expression_median_normals.txt (median normal values) or tumour vs normal comparison for TERT; note normal kidney TERT is near zero. IF FOUND: base 'elevated' on tumour/normal fold change and on the outlier subset, not on z-scores. SOURCE: cBioPortal file-format docs (https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/), not retrieved.

label: mutation filtering
text: PITFALL: Counting all mutations in a gene list (synonymous, intronic, VUS missense) inflates actionable fraction. CHECK: Variant_Classification values in data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: restrict to protein-altering (missense, nonsense, frameshift, splice site, in-frame indel), ideally known hotspots/truncating for tumour suppressors. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: denominator per patient
text: PITFALL: Denominator errors: clinical tables list ~150 samples, but CNA, mutation and SV files may profile different sample subsets, and the claim is per patient. CHECK: intersect sample IDs across data_cna.txt columns, mutation Tumor_Sample_Barcode, data_gene_panel_matrix.txt, and map to PATIENT_ID; check for patients with >1 sample. IF FOUND: denominator = patients with both mutation and CNA profiling; collapse per patient (any sample altered). SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: CNA does not capture balanced rearrangements
text: PITFALL: Using TERT copy number (data_cna.txt / GISTIC at 5p15.33) as a proxy for rearrangement; promoter rearrangements are often copy-neutral or show only small breakpoints, so absent CNA does not refute rearrangement. CHECK: inspect data_cna_hg19.seg for segment breakpoints near chr5:1,253,000-1,300,000 (hg19 TERT) in TERT-high samples. IF FOUND: a segment boundary at TERT in high-expressing tumours supports rearrangement; absence of amplification should not be read as contradiction. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: SV fusions
text: PITFALL: Structural variants (data_sv.txt, ~145 rows, mostly TMPRSS2-ERG/ETS fusions) can be over- or under-used: ETS fusions are usually not counted as actionable, but rare BRAF/RAF1 kinase fusions are. CHECK: tabulate Site1/Site2 gene pairs. IF FOUND: count only kinase fusions (BRAF, RAF1, etc.) and report ETS separately; SV file may cover only some samples. SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26000489/

label: TERT promoter mutations missed by exome
text: PITFALL: TERT promoter hotspot mutations (C228T/C250T) lie upstream of the coding region and are usually absent from exome MAFs, so their absence in data_mutations.txt is uninformative. CHECK: grep TERT in data_mutations.txt and check Variant_Classification (5'Flank/promoter). IF FOUND: do not conclude mutation status from exome; treat promoter alterations as unobserved. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: comparing to exact percentage
text: PITFALL: Exact-percentage claims (e.g. 89%) cannot be matched exactly when germline calls, AR splice variants and study-specific curation are missing; a computed value within roughly 5-10 points under the broad definition is consistent with the claim, whereas a value that is only reachable by counting shallow CNAs is not evidence. CHECK: report broad-definition fraction with CI (n~150, 95% CI about +/-5 points). IF FOUND: judge agreement against CI and known undercount sources, not exact equality. SOURCE: domain knowledge

label: Methylation is an alternative TERT activation mechanism
text: PITFALL: TERT upstream hypermethylation (THOR region) is associated with TERT expression and can confound attribution of high TERT to rearrangement. CHECK: correlate TERT probes in data_methylation_hm450.txt with TERT expression. IF FOUND: mention that some high-TERT tumours may be methylation-driven; this does not by itself contradict the hypothesis. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Sample matching and duplicates
text: PITFALL: Mismatched IDs (patient vs sample barcodes, -01 vs -11 normals) across expression, CNA and clinical tables silently drop or mix samples. CHECK: harmonise to 15-char TCGA sample IDs and confirm sample type 01 (primary tumour) before joining. IF FOUND: restrict to primaries and re-run. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: PDA hypothesis is in scope
text: PITFALL: Calling the BRAF/KRAS hypothesis 'Not verifiable'. This dataset is a PDA (PAAD) whole-exome cohort (UT Southwestern, sample IDs PDA_xxx) with a mutation MAF, so the hypothesis is about this study. CHECK: confirm that CANCER_TYPE is pancreatic adenocarcinoma and that KRAS and BRAF appear in data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: the label must be True or False, decided from KRAS/BRAF co-occurrence. SOURCE: task text and data headers (web search unavailable).

label: Oncogenic BRAF definition
text: PITFALL: Treating any BRAF variant as oncogenic. Only known activating BRAF alterations count: V600E/K, in-frame deletions in the beta3-alphaC loop (e.g. N486_P490del, V487_P492delinsA) and other class 2/3 kinase-domain hotspots. Passenger or VUS BRAF missense changes in a KRAS-mutant tumour do not break mutual exclusivity. CHECK: list the BRAF HGVSp_Short and Variant_Classification for every BRAF-mutant sample, together with that sample's KRAS status. IF FOUND: assess exclusivity only for oncogenic BRAF and report non-hotspot BRAF co-occurrences separately. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Yaeger & Corcoran 2019 BRAF classes; Foster et al. 2016 BRAF in-frame deletions in PDAC); search unavailable.

label: MIR548K absent from MAF; miRNA oncogenes act via amplification
text: PITFALL: The data contain only a mutation table (MAF, ~7,400 coding-dominated calls in 89 WGS ESCC tumours), no copy-number or expression table; MIR548K has zero rows in data_mutations.txt, and microRNA oncogenes are usually supported by focal amplification and overexpression, not point mutations, so absence of MIR548K mutations is not evidence against the claim. CHECK: grep -i MIR548K and the 11q13 region (chr11 ~69-70 Mb hg19, CCND1/FGF3/FGF4/FGF19/ORAOV1) in the MAF; confirm no CNA/expression files exist. IF FOUND (no direct variable): do not label False from missing mutations; decide by whether the hypothesis belongs to this study and by established biology, per the benchmark convention. SOURCE: general knowledge (web search unavailable; Mermel et al. 2011 GISTIC2, https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2011-12-4-r41).

label: Low power of exclusivity tests
text: PITFALL: Using a Fisher/hypergeometric p-value as the verdict. With KRAS mutated in about 90% of PDA and BRAF in about 1-3%, a cohort of around 100 samples has almost no power, so a non-significant test is not evidence against exclusivity. CHECK: count the samples that carry both oncogenic KRAS (G12/G13/Q61) and oncogenic BRAF, and the number of BRAF-mutant samples that are KRAS wild-type. IF FOUND: if oncogenic BRAF occurs only in KRAS-wt tumours (zero overlap), that supports exclusivity, whatever the p-value. Overlap in a non-hypermutated sample is evidence against it. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Canisius et al. 2016 DISCOVER, Genome Biol); search unavailable.

label: Do not default to Not verifiable for ESCC claim
text: PITFALL: Labelling 'Not verifiable' just because the tables lack the needed variable is wrong under this benchmark: hypotheses drawn from the source study are True/False even when the measurement was not deposited. This cohort is ESCC (oncotree ESCC, WGS, 89 tumours, BGI), so an ESCC hypothesis matches the study's cancer type. CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED = Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma and PLATFORM = WGS in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: treat the hypothesis as being about this study; pick True/False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention (no web source).

label: Novel-oncogene claims rest on CNV+functional data
text: PITFALL: WGS ESCC studies report noncoding and CNV drivers (e.g., focal amplifications of 11q13 containing miRNA genes) from data not deposited in cBioPortal-style tables; a novel-oncogene claim with 'novel' wording is typically a positive finding the source study reported via amplification plus functional assays (proliferation/invasion in cell lines). CHECK: look for any proxy: mutations in co-located genes (MIR548K lies at 11q13.3 near CCND1/FGF19 per standard annotation) and whether clinical outcome columns allow any test. IF FOUND: weigh established biology and study context over underpowered proxy tests. SOURCE: general knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Low cellularity KRAS false negatives
text: PITFALL: PDA has low tumour cellularity, so exome calling misses KRAS in some tumours. 'KRAS wild-type' samples can be false negatives, and a BRAF+ sample that looks KRAS-wt may hide a subclonal KRAS mutation. CHECK: inspect t_alt_count/t_ref_count (VAF) for KRAS and BRAF calls, and the VAF distribution in the KRAS-wt samples. IF FOUND: note a low-VAF BRAF call or a low-purity KRAS-wt sample as a caveat. Do not invent co-occurrence without a called KRAS variant. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Witkiewicz et al. 2015 Nat Commun; Biankin 2012); search unavailable.

label: WGS MAF filtered to coding; noncoding absence is artefact
text: PITFALL: Using somatic mutation recurrence alone to call oncogenes in WGS miss non-coding genes, because MAF exports often keep only coding/splice/UTR consequences (this MAF has only ~44 RNA and ~47 intron calls despite WGS). CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification; count non-coding (RNA, IGR, Intron) rows. IF FOUND: treat the MAF as exome-like; absence of noncoding gene calls is a filtering artefact, not biology. SOURCE: GDC MAF format docs https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/ (not retrieved).

label: Denominator from panel matrix
text: PITFALL: Wrong denominator, i.e. using only the samples present in the MAF. CHECK: take the sample universe from data_gene_panel_matrix.txt / data_clinical_sample.txt (all WXS samples), and treat samples with no KRAS row as KRAS-wt. IF FOUND: rebuild the 2x2 table on all sequenced samples. SOURCE: cBioPortal file-format conventions; search unavailable.

label: Mutation recurrence needs background model
text: PITFALL: Mutation recurrence tests for drivers must correct for gene length, replication timing and patient mutation burden (MutSigCV/dNdScv); naive counts flag long genes (TTN, MUC16) and miss small genes like miRNAs (~100 bp) that can never accumulate many mutations. CHECK: if testing any gene's recurrence, compare against background rate and length. IF FOUND: use dN/dS-style or MutSig-style background models, or do not infer oncogenicity from mutation counts. SOURCE: Lawrence et al. 2013 Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/nature12213; Martincorena et al. 2017 Cell https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.09.042 (not retrieved).

label: Filter variant classes
text: PITFALL: Counting non-functional variants. Silent, intronic, UTR, flank and splice_region rows in the MAF are not oncogenic. CHECK: filter Variant_Classification to protein-altering classes, then KRAS to codons 12/13/61 (also 146/117) and BRAF to known hotspots. IF FOUND: recompute co-occurrence on the filtered calls. SOURCE: domain knowledge; search unavailable.

label: Underpowered null is not contradiction
text: PITFALL: Survival or clinical association tests with 89 patients and a rare gene-level alteration are badly underpowered; a null result does not contradict an oncogene claim. CHECK: count carriers before any test; if fewer than ~10, report as uninformative. IF FOUND: do not use a non-significant result as evidence for False. SOURCE: general statistical guidance (web search unavailable).

label: Hypermutator confounding
text: PITFALL: Co-occurrence driven by a hypermutated (MSI/POLE) tumour, where BRAF or KRAS hits can be passengers. CHECK: check TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in data_clinical_sample.txt for any sample with both KRAS and BRAF mutations. IF FOUND: flag that sample, and judge exclusivity among non-hypermutated tumours. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Leiserson/Kim et al. weighted exclusivity tests that adjust for mutation rate); search unavailable.

label: miR-548 family naming/mapping
text: PITFALL: miR-548 family members are numerous, short, paralogous and often in repeat (MADE1 transposon) regions, so gene symbols (MIR548K vs MIR548K host/neighbour) and mapping are error-prone. CHECK: search case-insensitively for MIR548 and for genomic coordinates (hg19 chr11 ~70.1 Mb, verify) rather than only the exact symbol. IF FOUND: match by coordinates; do not conclude absence from a symbol miss. SOURCE: miRBase https://www.mirbase.org (not retrieved).

label: Do not mix CNA with mutations
text: PITFALL: Using BRAF copy-number gain from data_cna.txt as an 'oncogenic BRAF mutation'. CHECK: the hypothesis is about mutations, so use data_mutations.txt; report CNA only as a secondary analysis. IF FOUND: keep CNA out of the main exclusivity test. SOURCE: domain knowledge; search unavailable.

label: ACC MYB: capture non-fusion MYB-locus SVs
text: PITFALL: Searching only for Transcript fusion MYB-NFIB misses MYB rearrangements whose breakpoints fall downstream of MYB or in intergenic regions, which juxtapose distal enhancers (e.g. NFIB, TGFBR3, RAD51B super-enhancers) next to MYB without an in-frame fusion. CHECK: grep data_sv.txt for MYB or MYBL1 in Site1_Hugo_Symbol, Site2_Hugo_Symbol, Site descriptions and Event_Info, and also list SVs with a breakpoint on chr6 near 135.0-135.6 Mb (GRCh37, MYB at ~135.18-135.23 Mb) or chr8 near MYBL1 (~67.47 Mb). IF FOUND: count these as MYB-locus rearrangements and record partner loci (NFIB chr9p23, others). SOURCE: established ACC literature (Persson 2009 PNAS; Drier 2016 Nat Genet); no URL retrieved (search unavailable).

label: ACC MYB: truncation is activating
text: PITFALL: MYB-NFIB fusions often truncate MYB 3' exons (losing miR-15a/16 and miR-150 binding sites); an analyst may read a truncated-MYB fusion as loss of MYB rather than activation, or think overexpression requires the fusion protein. CHECK: inspect Site1/Site2_Region and exon numbers for MYB breakpoints (e.g. intron 14/15 vs downstream). IF FOUND: interpret 3' truncation and enhancer juxtaposition both as MYB-activating mechanisms; overexpression is driven by translocated enhancers in a positive feedback loop. SOURCE: Persson 2009 PNAS; Drier 2016 Nat Genet (no URL retrieved; search unavailable).

label: ACC MYB: per-sample counting and WES sensitivity
text: PITFALL: Counting SV rows instead of samples inflates MYB rearrangement frequency, because one complex translocation yields multiple breakpoint rows per sample. CHECK: count unique Sample_Id with any MYB/MYBL1-locus SV and divide by total samples in data_clinical_sample.txt (and by sample with SV profiling per data_gene_panel_matrix.txt). IF FOUND: report per-sample frequency; note WES samples have poor intergenic SV sensitivity so MYB negativity there is uninformative. SOURCE: general SV-analysis practice; no URL (search unavailable).

label: ACC MYB: include MYBL1
text: PITFALL: Some ACC lack MYB-NFIB but carry MYBL1 rearrangements (MYBL1-NFIB) or MYB copy-gain; excluding them underestimates the MYB-family activation rate and may make the hypothesis look weakly supported. CHECK: tabulate MYB, MYBL1 and NFIB involvement separately per sample. IF FOUND: report MYB and MYBL1 separately; MYB-family activation in most ACC supports the oncogene-activation claim. SOURCE: Brayer 2016 / Mitani 2016 ACC literature (no URL; search unavailable).

label: TTF column mislabeled as OS_MONTHS
text: PITFALL: In data_clinical_patient.txt the column OS_MONTHS is described in the # header as 'Time to Treatment Failure (Months)' while OS_STATUS is overall survival status; analysts may treat it as OS or miss that TTF is present. CHECK: compare the # description row against the header row column by column. IF FOUND: treat OS_MONTHS as the TTF time variable, state that the paired status column is OS_STATUS (the event indicator may not be a true TTF event), and report this ambiguity. SOURCE: data inspection of /biodsa-data headers (no web source; search tool returned 403).

label: Subset to PD-1 monotherapy cohort
text: PITFALL: The clinical tables appear to have no explicit treatment column (PD-1 monotherapy vs ipilimumab+nivolumab combination), so the hypothesis's 'PD-1 monotherapy' subset cannot be selected directly; mixing combo and mono patients can mask or create driver-class differences. CHECK: grep all columns for treatment info; note fields 'REC >=1.5% if mono tx' and 'RLC >=17.5% if mono tx' are non-NA only for monotherapy-treated patients, and ECOG/LDH/NLR are non-NA only for ICI-treated patients. IF FOUND: use non-NA REC/RLC as a proxy for the PD-1 monotherapy cohort and non-NA OS_MONTHS/NLR as the treated cohort; run the test in that subset and as sensitivity in all treated. SOURCE: data inspection (no web source; search returned 403).

label: Driver class grouping for ERK mechanism
text: PITFALL: 'Mechanism of ERK activation' maps to DRIVER_CLASS in data_clinical_sample.txt (BRAF_CLASS_1_V600E, BRAF_CLASS_1_Other, BRAF_CLASS_2_3, NRAS_Q61, RAS_OTHER, NF1, KIT_PDGFRA, Other_Driver, Unknown_Driver); collapsing classes arbitrarily (e.g. all BRAF together) can hide the effect the study reported, and tiny groups (n~14-44) give unstable estimates. CHECK: tabulate DRIVER_CLASS within the treated/monotherapy subset and count events per class. IF FOUND: run an overall multi-group log-rank plus Cox model with a reference class (e.g. BRAF V600E), and also biologically grounded groupings (RAS-dependent: BRAF class 2/3, NRAS, NF1 vs RAS-independent BRAF V600); report both the global p and key pairwise HRs. SOURCE: domain knowledge of BRAF class I/II/III signalling (Yao et al. Nature 2017); no web source retrieved.

label: TMB confounding of driver class
text: PITFALL: TMB confounds driver class: NF1-mutant and BRAF non-V600 / NRAS-wildtype 'triple wild-type' melanomas often have very high UV TMB, and high TMB predicts ICI benefit, so a driver-class TTF difference may be partly TMB-driven (and conversely acral/mucosal KIT or Unknown_Driver have low TMB). CHECK: compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS distribution across DRIVER_CLASS; fit Cox TTF ~ DRIVER_CLASS + log(TMB) + LDH/ECOG. IF FOUND: report unadjusted and adjusted results; the hypothesis is about variation by class, so an unadjusted significant difference already contradicts 'does not vary', but note the mechanism. SOURCE: domain knowledge (no web source retrieved; search returned 403).

label: Time zero and merging
text: PITFALL: Clinical-genomic cohorts (MSK-IMPACT) sequence tumours at varying times relative to treatment start, causing left truncation/immortal time bias if time zero is diagnosis; and patients with NA time must be excluded, not set to 0. CHECK: confirm the time variable starts at treatment start (TTF does by definition) and drop rows with NA time/status; check for multiple samples per patient (one per patient in this data) before merging sample to patient. IF FOUND: use treatment start as time zero; deduplicate to one sample per patient (earliest or first). SOURCE: standard survival-analysis guidance on delayed entry (no web source retrieved).

label: Power, PH and null interpretation
text: PITFALL: Failing to reject equality with a log-rank test is not evidence of no difference; with small subgroups an underpowered null can be mislabeled 'True', and non-proportional hazards (crossing curves typical of ICI) reduce log-rank power. CHECK: inspect Kaplan-Meier curves per driver class, median TTF with CIs, Schoenfeld residual test (cox.zph / lifelines check_assumptions). IF FOUND: if PH is violated use restricted mean survival time or landmark comparisons as supplementary; weigh effect sizes and the study's likely reported finding (benchmark hypotheses often are a reversed published finding) rather than p-value alone. SOURCE: standard survival methodology (no web source retrieved).

label: Prior targeted therapy confounding
text: PITFALL: Prior BRAF/MEK targeted therapy is common in BRAF V600 patients and patients who received ICI after progression on targeted therapy have worse ICI outcomes, biasing BRAF V600E vs others comparisons. CHECK: look for any line-of-therapy or prior-treatment column; if none, acknowledge as unmeasured confounder. IF FOUND: stratify or adjust by prior targeted therapy. SOURCE: domain knowledge of melanoma ICI outcomes (no web source retrieved).

label: No survival columns in clinical tables
text: PITFALL: The deposited data_clinical_patient.txt has only PATIENT_ID, CENTER, STAGE, SEX (101 patients); there are no OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS columns, so a survival test cannot be run directly and an analyst may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: grep the headers of all clinical files for OS_, DFS_, SURVIVAL, VITAL. IF FOUND (no survival variable): per the task convention, a hypothesis about this study's cancer (gallbladder) and genes (SMAD4 is on the IMPACT410 panel) is True/False, not Not verifiable; decide from what the study likely reported plus established biology and state that this was the deciding evidence. SOURCE: direct inspection of /biodsa-data headers.

label: SMAD4 alteration definition incl. deep deletion
text: PITFALL: Counting SMAD4 as mutated from data_mutations.txt alone misses homozygous deletions, which are a major SMAD4 inactivation mechanism in biliary/pancreatic cancer. CHECK: count SMAD4 -2 calls in data_cna.txt and SMAD4 entries in data_sv.txt alongside the non-silent mutations. IF FOUND: define SMAD4-altered as mutation OR deep deletion OR disruptive SV, and report both definitions. SOURCE: cBioPortal OQL/alteration conventions, https://docs.cbioportal.org (not retrieved; tool down).

label: Collapse samples to patients
text: PITFALL: The cohort has several samples per patient (sample IDs ending _P/_M, multiple P-xxxx-T0n), and two ID schemes (s_WJ_gb_* and P-000*), so a per-sample analysis double counts patients and can mis-join to the patient table. CHECK: map SAMPLE_ID to PATIENT_ID through data_clinical_sample.txt and count unique patients that carry SMAD4 alterations. IF FOUND: collapse to one status per patient (altered if any sample is altered) before any group comparison. SOURCE: standard practice for cBioPortal multi-sample studies (not retrieved).

label: Confounding by stage and center
text: PITFALL: Mutation-status survival comparisons are confounded by stage and by center/country (Chile, Japan, USA have different etiology and treatment), and SMAD4 loss may be enriched in advanced/metastatic samples. CHECK: cross-tabulate SMAD4 status against STAGE, CENTER and SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary/Metastasis). IF FOUND: adjust (Cox with stage, and center as a covariate or strata) or at least report the imbalance; an unadjusted association does not show that SMAD4 is prognostic. SOURCE: REMARK guidelines for prognostic marker studies, McShane et al. 2005 JNCI https://doi.org/10.1093/jnci/dji237 (not retrieved).

label: Left truncation in sequencing cohorts
text: PITFALL: Clinical-sequencing cohorts like MSK-IMPACT are left-truncated (patients enter at sequencing, not at diagnosis), which biases the HR of a mutation if follow-up is counted from diagnosis. CHECK: if any survival times exist, find out whether they start at diagnosis or at sequencing. IF FOUND: use delayed-entry (counting-process) Cox models or measure time from sequencing. SOURCE: Brown et al. 2022 JAMA Oncol 'Survival bias in clinicogenomic cohorts' (not retrieved; tool down).

label: Missing fusion data is not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: Concluding 'Not verifiable' because the tables have no fusion or drug-response variable. CHECK: data_clinical_sample.txt shows a breast cancer cohort (IDC, ER/PR/HER2 status, WXS matched tumour-normal), and data_mutations.txt has no Fusion rows (Variant_Classification counts: Missense 3094, Silent 1133, Nonsense 233, etc.; grep for AKT3 or Fusion returns 0 lines). IF FOUND: under the benchmark convention, a hypothesis about this study's genes and cancer type gets True/False even when the measurement was not deposited, so decide from established biology. SOURCE: task label convention; library web search was unavailable.

label: Low power / multiple testing
text: PITFALL: With about 100 patients and few SMAD4-altered cases (often 10-20%), log-rank tests have low power; a non-significant p-value is not evidence against a worse-survival claim, and picking the best of many genes inflates false positives. CHECK: report the number of SMAD4-altered patients, number of events, HR with 95% CI, and how many genes were screened. IF FOUND (few events): read the direction and the CI rather than p alone, and do not call False just because p>0.05. SOURCE: general survival-analysis guidance, e.g. REMARK https://doi.org/10.1093/jnci/dji237 (not retrieved).

label: Filter to damaging SMAD4 variants
text: PITFALL: Silent and non-functional variants (and possible germline calls in unmatched samples; SOMATIC_STATUS=Unmatched exists here) inflate the SMAD4-mutant group. CHECK: filter data_mutations.txt Variant_Classification to non-synonymous types and look for SMAD4 hotspots/truncations (e.g. R361). IF FOUND: restrict to likely-damaging alterations. SOURCE: MSK-IMPACT/cBioPortal driver-annotation conventions (OncoKB, https://www.oncokb.org; not retrieved).

label: Inhibitor class vs fusion domain structure
text: PITFALL: Treating ATP-competitive and allosteric AKT inhibitors as the same thing. Allosteric inhibitors such as MK-2206 need the PH domain to lock AKT in its inactive conformation. ATP-competitive inhibitors such as GSK690693, ipatasertib and capivasertib bind the kinase-domain ATP pocket. CHECK: work out which AKT3 domains the fusion keeps. MAGI3-AKT3 fusions are reported to keep the AKT3 kinase domain and lose the PH domain, which makes them PIP3-independent and constitutively active. IF FOUND: base the mechanistic argument on whether the inhibitor's binding site survives in the fusion, not on generic 'AKT inhibitor resistance'. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable); verify against established AKT pharmacology.

label: SMAD4 prognostic biology (unverified)
text: PITFALL: Answering from memory without stating it. Established biology (from my background knowledge; I could not verify it with web search): SMAD4 inactivation is widely reported to go with aggressive disease and poorer survival in pancreatic and biliary tract cancers, but gallbladder-specific results vary between cohorts. CHECK: the reasoning should say explicitly whether the label came from the data or from prior biology. IF FOUND (no direct test possible): say that the label rests on prior biology and the study context. SOURCE: background knowledge only; the search tool returned HTTP 403.

label: Check for reversed-finding hypotheses
text: PITFALL: Reading the absolute wording 'cannot be abolished' without checking for a reversed finding. Benchmark hypotheses are often a published finding with its direction flipped. CHECK: compare the hypothesis with the expected study finding, e.g. whether the original study reported the fusion as sensitive to an ATP-competitive AKT inhibitor. IF FOUND: if the claim is the negation of the reported result, the label is False, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention.

label: Point mutations are not fusion proxies
text: PITFALL: Using AKT3 point mutations or PI3K-pathway mutation frequencies in data_mutations.txt as a stand-in for the fusion or for inhibitor sensitivity. CHECK: confirm that no column in the tables measures fusion status or drug response. IF FOUND: treat pathway-mutation co-occurrence analyses (PIK3CA/PTEN/AKT1 vs. ER/PR/HER2 status) only as context, and let established mechanism decide the label. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: TNBC subtype ties fusion to cohort
text: PITFALL: Missing the subtype context. MAGI3-AKT3 fusions were described mainly in triple-negative (ER-/PR-/HER2-) breast cancer. CHECK: tabulate ER_STATUS, PR_STATUS and HER2_STATUS in data_clinical_sample.txt to confirm the cohort includes TNBC cases, which ties the hypothesis to this study. IF FOUND: treat the hypothesis as being about this study (so True/False), not about another cohort. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: TERT promoter is 5'Flank
text: PITFALL: TERT promoter mutations are non-coding (5'Flank, chr5 ~1,295,228 C228T and ~1,295,250 C250T in GRCh37) and are dropped if the analyst filters to coding/nonsynonymous variants or counts TERT only by protein change. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt select Hugo_Symbol==TERT and Variant_Classification in {5'Flank,5'UTR}; list Start_Position values (about 138 5'Flank TERT rows exist). IF FOUND: define TERT-promoter status per sample from these 5'Flank hotspot rows, not from coding mutations. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: TERT denominator
text: PITFALL: Samples with no TERT row are not automatically wild-type unless the promoter was assayed in all samples; WXS normally misses the TERT promoter, so absent rows may mean not sequenced. CHECK: compare the set of samples in data_clinical_sample.txt/data_gene_panel_matrix.txt with samples carrying any TERT 5'Flank row, and check whether 5'Flank calls exist for other genes (targeted promoter genotyping vs capture). IF FOUND: state the denominator explicitly; if promoter genotyping covered all samples treat absence as wild-type, otherwise restrict to assayed samples. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: Missing phospho data is not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: Answering 'Not verifiable' because the tables contain no phosphoproteomic data; this dataset (SCB-MERiC Basel HCC biopsy cohort, clinical + mutations only) is from a proteogenomic HCC study, and the benchmark convention says hypotheses from the source publication are True/False even when the needed measurement was not deposited. CHECK: confirm cancer type is HCC and CTNNB1 is mutated in the MAF (Hugo_Symbol==CTNNB1). IF FOUND: the hypothesis is about this study; choose True/False from established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention (web search unavailable).

label: Early event interpretation
text: PITFALL: 'Early event' is a claim about timing; a cross-sectional frequency-by-stage comparison only tests it indirectly. An early event predicts similar (high) frequency in early stages (BCLC 0/A, small tumors, well-differentiated, classic HCC) as in advanced ones, NOT enrichment in late stage; a significant increase with stage would argue for a late event. CHECK: tabulate TERT-promoter frequency across BCLC_STAGE, TUMOR_SIZE, DIFFERENTIATION, DISEASE_STAGE, VASCULAR_INVASION. IF FOUND: interpret flat-and-high frequency in early stages as consistent with early event; also check clonality (VAF high vs other drivers) as more direct timing evidence. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: VAF clonality timing
text: PITFALL: Clonality evidence for timing: an early (truncal) mutation should have VAF similar to or higher than other clonal drivers; low VAF suggests subclonal/late. Promoter VAFs are confounded by tumor purity and copy number. CHECK: compute t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count) for TERT 5'Flank rows if counts are filled, compared with per-sample median VAF of other mutations. IF FOUND: use relative VAF within sample (normalises purity) rather than absolute VAF. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: Stage test power
text: PITFALL: Stage-by-mutation tests on ~100-300 tumours with ordinal stages have low power; a non-significant p-value is not evidence of 'no association', and sparse cells break chi-square. CHECK: cell counts per BCLC stage group. IF FOUND: use Fisher exact or Cochran-Armitage trend test on ordered stages, merge sparse categories (e.g. 0/A vs B/C), report proportions with CIs. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: Negated hypothesis likely reversed finding
text: PITFALL: Treating the negated hypothesis ('not associated') as default-true because no data can test it; hypotheses in this benchmark are often a reported finding reversed. CHECK: ask whether the publication-style finding would be a positive association (CTNNB1-mutant HCC shows distinct phosphorylation of actin-cytoskeleton/cell-adhesion proteins). IF FOUND: established biology (beta-catenin is an adherens-junction protein bridging cadherins to the actin cytoskeleton via alpha-catenin; CTNNB1-mutant HCC is a distinct molecular class with altered signaling) favours an association, i.e. label False. SOURCE: domain knowledge; e.g. Schulze et al. 2015 Nat Genet; Ng et al. proteogenomic HCC (unverified, search down).

label: Sample dedup and merge
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient or non-HCC samples (e.g. other ONCOTREE codes, mixed HCC-CCA) inflate or bias frequencies. CHECK: count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID and ONCOTREE_CODE / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED values; BCLC_STAGE is in the patient table and must be merged via PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: one sample per patient, restrict to HCC. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: Etiology confounding
text: PITFALL: Etiology confounds TERT promoter frequency (lower in HBV-related HCC where HBV integration into TERT activates it instead; higher in HCV/alcohol), and etiology may differ by stage. CHECK: cross-tab ETIOLOGY by stage and TERT status. IF FOUND: stratify or adjust (logistic regression with etiology) before attributing a stage trend. SOURCE: background knowledge (search tool unavailable).

label: No methylation data - do not default to Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: The tables contain no DNA methylation or chromatin data (only clinical, CNA, FPKM expression, mutations), so analysts may wrongly answer 'Not verifiable'; but the hypothesis concerns this very cohort (CRPC-NE vs CRPC-Adeno, DISEASE_CODE column), so per the benchmark convention it must be True/False. CHECK: confirm DISEASE_CODE has CRPC-NE and CRPC-Adeno groups and that no methylation file exists. IF FOUND: test with the closest proxies (expression of epigenetic regulators such as EZH2, DNMT1/3A/3B, TET, SOX2, and mutations/CNAs in chromatin modifiers) and fall back on established biology (NEPC is reported to have distinct, largely hypermethylated DNA-methylation profiles and EZH2 up-regulation). SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable (Exa HTTP 403).

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: Several patients contribute multiple samples (e.g. WCMC0 has samples _1,_5,_6,_8,_9,_10; WCMC159 several), which inflates n and p-values (pseudoreplication). CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID within each DISEASE_CODE group. IF FOUND: collapse to one sample per patient (or average) or use a patient random effect before testing group differences. SOURCE: general statistical guidance; web search unavailable.

label: Define CTNNB1 activating mutations
text: PITFALL: Counting all CTNNB1 variants as activating; only exon-3 hotspot missense/in-frame deletions (codons 32-45, e.g. S33, S37, T41, S45, D32, G34) and large exon 3-4 in-frame deletions stabilise beta-catenin. CHECK: tabulate CTNNB1 HGVSp_Short and Variant_Classification; exclude Silent/intronic/UTR. IF FOUND: define mutant group as exon-3 hotspot/in-frame deletions; report counts. SOURCE: domain knowledge (COSMIC CTNNB1 hotspots), search unavailable.

label: Transform FPKM before testing
text: PITFALL: The zscores file is standardized against all samples, and FPKM is unlogged and right-skewed; t-tests on raw FPKM are driven by outliers. CHECK: inspect distributions of FPKM for candidate genes. IF FOUND: use log2(FPKM+1) with Wilcoxon or limma-style tests, and FDR correction across genes. SOURCE: general RNA-seq guidance (limma/voom, Law et al. 2014 Genome Biol); web search unavailable.

label: Purity and site confounding
text: PITFALL: Group labels may be confounded by tumour purity (CLONET_PURITY) and tissue site (TUMOR_TISSUE_SITE, e.g. liver vs bone), which change bulk expression of any gene, including epigenetic regulators. CHECK: compare purity and site distributions between CRPC-NE and CRPC-Adeno. IF FOUND: adjust for purity/site in a regression or check the effect holds within strata. SOURCE: general tumour-genomics guidance; web search unavailable.

label: Count patients not rows
text: PITFALL: Counting KRAS mutation rows instead of mutated patients inflates frequency when a patient has multiple KRAS calls or multiple samples. CHECK: collapse data_mutations.txt to unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode, then map to PATIENT_ID via data_clinical_sample.txt; count distinct patients with >=1 qualifying KRAS mutation. IF FOUND: use per-patient binary mutated/not, denominator = all sequenced patients in each PREVIOUS_TREATMENT group (including patients with zero mutations of any gene). SOURCE: standard practice (web search unavailable).

label: Validate NE vs Adeno labels
text: PITFALL: Mixed/intermediate pathology (PATHOLOGY_CLASSIFICATION codes) can blur the NE vs Adeno contrast; also verify group labels with marker genes. CHECK: tabulate PATHOLOGY_CLASSIFICATION vs DISEASE_CODE and check AR, KLK3 (low in NE) and SYP, CHGA, ASCL1 (high in NE). IF FOUND: run the analysis on clear-cut groups and as sensitivity with mixed cases excluded. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search unavailable.

label: Multiple biopsies per patient
text: PITFALL: Multi-region sampling - several patients have more than one biopsy (e.g. SCB-MERiC-0004 has C457b and C457c), so sample-level tests double count patients. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt and CTNNB1 status per sample. IF FOUND: collapse to patient level (mutant if any sample mutant) or use one sample per patient / mixed models. SOURCE: standard practice for multi-region cohorts.

label: Denominator from clinical table
text: PITFALL: Denominator built only from samples appearing in the MAF drops sequenced patients with no mutations, biasing frequencies. CHECK: compare number of samples in data_clinical_sample.txt vs unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode in MAF. IF FOUND: denominator is clinical-sample list (all were sequenced in this study), unmutated = absent from KRAS rows. SOURCE: standard practice (web search unavailable).

label: Use a predefined epigenetic gene panel with FDR
text: PITFALL: Testing only one epigenetic gene, or many without correction, gives fragile conclusions. CHECK: predefine a panel of epigenetic regulators (EZH2, DNMT1, DNMT3A/B, TET1-3, KDM, SMARCA, CBX2) and/or do unsupervised clustering / genome-wide DE between groups. IF FOUND: report FDR-adjusted results and whether global expression separates groups; a coherent separation (e.g. EZH2 higher in NE) supports 'distinct epigenetic profiles'. SOURCE: general guidance; web search unavailable.

label: Filter non-silent KRAS
text: PITFALL: Including Silent/intronic/UTR KRAS variants counts non-functional calls as mutations. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification for KRAS rows. IF FOUND: restrict to nonsynonymous (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame indels); report hotspot (G12/G13/Q61/A146) counts as sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: standard cBioPortal/MAF convention (web search unavailable).

label: Sequenced-sample denominator
text: PITFALL: Samples absent from the MAF or unmatched (SOMATIC_STATUS not Matched) get misclassified as wild-type or contain germline variants. CHECK: compare Tumor_Sample_Barcode set to SAMPLE_ID list and check SOMATIC_STATUS values. IF FOUND: restrict denominator to sequenced samples; treat unmatched-sample calls cautiously. SOURCE: cBioPortal MAF conventions.

label: Treatment variable NA
text: PITFALL: PREVIOUS_TREATMENT may contain NA/Unknown values; dropping or merging them wrongly shifts group frequencies. CHECK: value_counts of PREVIOUS_TREATMENT including NA. IF FOUND: exclude NA from the comparison and report n per group. SOURCE: standard practice (web search unavailable).

label: Small-sample significance and direction
text: PITFALL: With modest group sizes (~200 patients, KRAS ~20-25%), a direction difference may be non-significant; a p>0.05 does not by itself mean False under this benchmark's convention. CHECK: 2x2 Fisher exact test plus the proportions and odds ratio in treated vs untreated. IF FOUND: decide on direction and magnitude together with the significance; if treated freq clearly higher, supports True, if equal or lower, False. Biology: RAS mutations are reported more often in relapsed/pretreated myeloma (clonal selection), and the original Broad MM sequencing study reported KRAS enrichment in previously treated patients as a finding, so hypothesis comes from this study. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: TMB confounding
text: PITFALL: Hypermutated or high-TMB samples, more common after treatment (e.g., alkylator exposure), can raise mutation frequency in any gene nonspecifically. CHECK: compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS between treatment groups. IF FOUND: as sensitivity, a logistic regression of KRAS status on treatment adjusted for log TMB. SOURCE: standard practice (web search unavailable).

label: Proxy variables are not phosphorylation
text: PITFALL: Using a proxy (e.g. mutations in actin-organization genes, TMB, Edmondson grade, immunophenotype) as if it measured phosphorylation; a null proxy result does not show 'no association' with phosphorylation. CHECK: state explicitly that no phospho variable exists. IF FOUND: let established biology decide the label and say so in reasoning; mention proxy results only as secondary. Note CTNNB1-mutant HCC is known to be enriched for Immune-Excluded/desert phenotypes (immune exclusion), a useful sanity check of mutant calls. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Pinyol/Sia et al. on CTNNB1 immune exclusion).

label: Matched normal status
text: PITFALL: Matched vs unmatched (tumor-only) samples differ in germline contamination of calls. CHECK: SOMATIC_STATUS column in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: KRAS hotspot calls are robust, but rerun restricted to Matched samples as sensitivity. SOURCE: standard practice (web search unavailable).

label: Lauren join and denominators
text: PITFALL: Lauren histology is in data_clinical_patient.txt (PATHOLOGY_LAUREN) while mutations are keyed by Tumor_Sample_Barcode; failing to join on PATIENT_ID=SAMPLE_ID or dropping unmatched samples changes denominators. CHECK: confirm every sample in the sample table maps to one patient and list PATHOLOGY_LAUREN value counts including mixed/unknown/NA. IF FOUND: use as denominator all sequenced samples of each Lauren type (from the clinical table, not only those with any mutation row); report mixed/indeterminate separately. SOURCE: none (search tool unavailable; domain knowledge).

label: RHOA frequency denominator
text: PITFALL: Counting mutated tumours only among samples present in data_mutations.txt underestimates the denominator (wild-type samples have no RHOA row) and samples with zero mutations may be missing entirely. CHECK: denominator = number of samples per Lauren group in data_clinical_sample.txt; numerator = unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode with a non-silent RHOA call. IF FOUND: recompute frequency as unique mutated samples / all sequenced samples of that subtype. SOURCE: none (domain knowledge).

label: RHOA mutation filtering
text: PITFALL: Including silent/intronic/UTR RHOA variants or counting multiple RHOA mutations in one tumour twice inflates frequency. CHECK: tabulate Variant_Classification and HGVSp for RHOA; RHOA driver hotspots in diffuse gastric cancer cluster at Y42, R5, G17, L57 (switch/GTP-binding regions). IF FOUND: count unique samples with non-synonymous (missense/nonsense/frameshift/splice/in-frame) RHOA variants; report hotspot vs other separately. SOURCE: none (domain knowledge; Wang et al. 2014 Nat Genet and Kakiuchi et al. 2014 Nat Genet reported RHOA in diffuse-type GC).

label: Two-part claim check
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis has two parts (about 14.3% in diffuse AND absent in intestinal); a single RHOA mutation in an intestinal or mixed tumour, or a diffuse rate far from 14.3%, can decide the label. CHECK: report exact counts k/n for diffuse and intestinal (and mixed), with exact binomial CI; check whether 14.3% equals a simple fraction like 1/7 of the diffuse count. IF FOUND: if diffuse rate matches roughly and intestinal has 0, supports True; if intestinal tumours carry RHOA mutations at a similar rate, consider False. Note published discovery-cohort figures may differ from deposited subset. SOURCE: none (domain knowledge).

label: MSI hypermutator passengers
text: PITFALL: Hypermutated MSI-high tumours (mostly intestinal) carry many passenger mutations, so a stray RHOA passenger in an MSI-H intestinal tumour can be misread as contradicting 'not in intestinal'. CHECK: cross-tab RHOA-mutant samples with MSI_STATUS and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS; check whether variant is a known hotspot. IF FOUND: report whether intestinal hits are non-hotspot passengers in hypermutated tumours; weigh against the original study's likely framing (driver mutations). SOURCE: none (domain knowledge).

label: Hypothesis is on-topic
text: PITFALL: This dataset (center pfizer_uhongkong, GRCh37, Lauren and EBV/H. pylori fields) is a gastric adenocarcinoma WES study, so a RHOA-in-diffuse-gastric hypothesis is on-topic and should not be labelled Not verifiable. CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED is stomach adenocarcinoma and PATHOLOGY_LAUREN exists. IF FOUND: answer True or False from the counts, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: none (benchmark convention in task text).
