label: No drug data but on-study
text: PITFALL: The tables contain no drug-response variable (no IC50/AUC/viability), so analysts may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: grep all files for drug/IC50/AUC/response columns; confirm cohort is bladder cancer organoids (SCBO-*, Oncotree BLCA, Sample Class Organoid). IF FOUND: the hypothesis matches this study (bladder organoids + MSK-IMPACT mutation profiles), so per the benchmark convention the label must be True or False, decided from established biology/the study's known framing, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention (web search unavailable).

label: Partial correlation is the typical finding
text: PITFALL: Treating 'partial correlation' as requiring a strong, comprehensive genotype-drug link; organoid pharmacogenomic studies typically report that some drug responses track mutations (e.g., FGFR3, ERBB2, PIK3CA, TSC1, KDM6A/ARID1A, TP53/RB1) while others do not. CHECK: confirm organoids carry recurrent actionable bladder alterations (FGFR3, PIK3CA, ERBB2, TP53, RB1, KDM6A, ARID1A, STAG2) with heterogeneity across lines. IF FOUND: heterogeneous actionable genotypes across organoid lines are consistent with partial genotype-response correlation; weigh toward True unless evidence contradicts. SOURCE: general pharmacogenomics knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Pseudo-replication across passages
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (Organoid P1/P7/P11 passages, Parental, Xenograft, CellLine) inflate n and create pseudo-replication. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID and per SAMPLE_CLASS (45 Organoid, 32 CellLine, 18 Resection, 15 Xenograft etc.). IF FOUND: collapse to one organoid per patient (or per tumor line) before any association; use passage comparisons only to assess genomic stability. SOURCE: standard statistical practice (search unavailable).

label: Sample class labeling
text: PITFALL: Sample Class labels are inconsistent (e.g., SCBO-1_Organoid_P1 labeled CellLine while P11 labeled Organoid). CHECK: compare SAMPLE_ID suffix against SAMPLE_CLASS. IF FOUND: define organoid samples by SAMPLE_ID pattern '_Organoid' rather than only SAMPLE_CLASS. SOURCE: direct header inspection.

label: Gene panel coverage
text: PITFALL: Gene panel (MSK-IMPACT410/468) limits which genes can be called mutated; absence in MAF is not wild-type for genes off-panel. CHECK: data_gene_panel_matrix.txt for panel per sample. IF FOUND: restrict genotype features to genes on all panels used. SOURCE: cBioPortal data conventions (search unavailable).

label: Small n power
text: PITFALL: With ~20 organoid lines, any genotype-drug test is badly underpowered and multiple-testing across genes x drugs yields false positives. CHECK: number of unique patients with organoids and mutation frequency per gene. IF FOUND: do not treat non-significance as contradiction; report effect sizes, use FDR, and rely on biology for the label. SOURCE: standard statistical practice (search unavailable).

label: Concordance is indirect evidence
text: PITFALL: Organoid-vs-parental concordance is a different claim from genotype-drug correlation; teams may substitute it. CHECK: concordance of mutations between Parental and Organoid samples of the same patient can support that organoids retain mutational profiles, a prerequisite for genotype-response links. IF FOUND: use concordance as supporting evidence only, stating it is indirect. SOURCE: general practice (search unavailable).

label: PIK3CA mutation-only data
text: PITFALL: The data have only a mutation table (no CNA file), so PIK3CA 'alterations' from mutations alone leave out PIK3CA amplification/3q26 gain, which is common in HPV-related squamous cancers. CHECK: confirm there is no data_cna/gistic file, and count samples with any non-silent PIK3CA mutation. IF FOUND: report the frequency as mutations only. Missing amplification data does not make the claim Not verifiable: the cohort and gene match this vulvar SCC study, so the label must be True or False. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable); general cBioPortal practice.

label: No subtype column is not Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: The tables (31 UTUC samples, sample clinical + MAF) contain no methylation data and no EpiC subtype column, so an analyst may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: grep the clinical file headers for subtype/cluster/methylation columns. IF FOUND absent: the hypothesis is still about this study's cohort (UTUC, FGFR3), so per the benchmark convention answer True/False from the study's reported finding and established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention (web search unavailable).

label: Count samples, nonsynonymous only
text: PITFALL: Counting mutation rows instead of unique samples, or including Silent/Intron/UTR/Flank variants, inflates the PIK3CA frequency. CHECK: filter Hugo_Symbol==PIK3CA and Variant_Classification in {Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site, Nonstop}, then count unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode. IF FOUND: use unique altered samples as the numerator. SOURCE: none (search unavailable); cBioPortal altered-sample convention.

label: Check subtype name vs methylation direction
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis may be a reversed version of the study finding (swapping EpiC-high vs EpiC-low). CHECK: reason about which label is biologically consistent: a hypermethylated cluster is by naming convention 'EpiC-high' (high epigenetic/CpG methylation), so attributing hypermethylation to 'EpiC-low' is internally suspicious. IF FOUND: weigh whether the claim's subtype name matches its described methylation state; a name/phenotype mismatch suggests a reversed (False) hypothesis. SOURCE: general CIMP-naming convention, no web source (search returned HTTP 403).

label: Denominator from clinical table
text: PITFALL: The denominator should be all sequenced samples in data_clinical_sample.txt, not only samples that appear in the MAF; a sample with zero mutations listed is still unaltered. CHECK: compare the sample count in clinical_sample with the unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode in the MAF. IF FOUND: use the clinical sample count (the VSCC cohort) as N. SOURCE: none (search unavailable).

label: FGFR3 biology proxy
text: PITFALL: FGFR3-mutant urothelial tumours are typically luminal-papillary, low-grade, low-TMB and in UTUC have been associated with a hypermethylated/CIMP-like epigenetic cluster; analysts can confuse which cluster carries FGFR3. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt count FGFR3 hotspot mutations (R248C, S249C, G370C, Y373C, K650E) per sample and compare their TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS with non-mutants as a proxy for the low-grade luminal phenotype. IF FOUND: use this only as supporting proxy evidence; it cannot by itself identify EpiC clusters. SOURCE: established urothelial biology (no web source; search unavailable).

label: Small-N binomial CI
text: PITFALL: With a small cohort (tens of samples), the observed PIK3CA frequency has a wide 95% CI, and a point estimate near 40% (e.g. 30-50%) is compatible with the claim. CHECK: compute a Wilson/exact binomial CI for k/N and see whether it contains 0.40. IF FOUND: if 40% is inside the CI and the estimate is close, lean True; if the estimate is far below (e.g. <20%) with a CI that excludes 40%, lean False. Also keep in mind that the paper may have counted amplifications as well. SOURCE: none (search unavailable).

label: Small n low power
text: PITFALL: With n=31 any proxy test (e.g. FGFR3 mutant vs TMB, or hypermutated samples) has very low power, and non-significance is not evidence against the hypothesis. CHECK: report counts and Fisher/Wilcoxon exact p-values with effect sizes. IF FOUND non-significant: do not convert this into False; decide from study-level biology. SOURCE: general small-sample statistics guidance (no web source).

label: Exact-number hypotheses
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis says '40%'. Benchmark hypotheses are usually either the paper's reported number or a reversed/altered one, so an exact number differing from the data may be a deliberately changed figure. CHECK: compute the exact mutation frequency, and also the frequency in HPV-positive vs HPV-negative subgroups (HPV_STATUS in the patient table). IF FOUND: if the mutation-only frequency is roughly 40%, label True; if it is clearly different (e.g. ~10-20%) and nothing else in the tables could add alterations, label False. SOURCE: none (search unavailable).

label: Cohort is vulvar SCC
text: PITFALL: The cohort is labelled ONCOTREE VSC 'Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Vulva/Vagina' and CANCER_TYPE 'Vaginal Cancer', which might wrongly suggest the data are not vulvar. CHECK: sample IDs are VSCC*, the cohort is Korean, and HPV status is recorded. IF FOUND: treat this as the vulvar SCC study the hypothesis refers to, and do not answer Not verifiable. SOURCE: none.

label: MAF mutation status derivation
text: PITFALL: Counting FGFR3 mutants from the MAF can be inflated by silent/intronic variants or deflated by not deduplicating per sample. CHECK: filter Variant_Classification to nonsynonymous classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame), count unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode, and denominate by all 31 samples in data_clinical_sample.txt (samples with no mutations still count). IF FOUND: use filtered per-sample mutation status. SOURCE: MAF format conventions (no web source).

label: Hotspots and FFPE artefacts
text: PITFALL: PIK3CA hotspot mutations (E542K, E545K helical; H1047R kinase) are enriched in HPV-positive/APOBEC-driven squamous tumours, and FFPE artefacts (C>T at low VAF) can create false calls. CHECK: list PIK3CA HGVSp_Short and VAF (t_alt_count/(t_ref+t_alt)); flag calls with VAF <5% or alt reads <5. IF FOUND: report the frequency both with and without low-support calls, and say whether the label depends on this. SOURCE: none (search unavailable).

label: Hypermutated outliers
text: PITFALL: UTUC cohorts can include hypermutated/MSI (Lynch syndrome) tumours, which skew TMB and mutation-frequency comparisons between groups. CHECK: inspect TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS distribution for outliers (e.g. >10/Mb) and MSH2/MLH1/MSH6 mutations. IF FOUND: exclude or analyse separately in any proxy comparison. SOURCE: general UTUC/Lynch knowledge (no web source).

label: Identify classifier variable
text: PITFALL: The classifier output is not one obvious column; the sample table has PRED_CATEGORY (Biliary class / Biliary-aligned / HCC-aligned / HCC class, NaN for ~793 samples) and the patient table has a numeric BILIARY_SCORE, so analysts may test the wrong variable or silently drop NaN rows. CHECK: cross-tab PRED_CATEGORY and non-missing BILIARY_SCORE by SUBGROUP; confirm which IHC patients have a prediction. IF FOUND: restrict to SUBGROUP=='IHC' with a non-missing prediction, test both the score (continuous) and HCC-like vs biliary-like groups (e.g. HCC class+HCC-aligned vs Biliary class+aligned), and report n/events. SOURCE: general practice (web search unavailable).

label: Independence requires multivariable Cox
text: PITFALL: 'Independent of FGFR2 and IDH1' needs a multivariable Cox model; a univariable log-rank on the classifier alone does not test independence, and FGFR2 fusions sit in data_sv.txt, not data_mutations.txt. CHECK: build FGFR2 status from data_sv.txt (FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, Site1 or Site2) plus FGFR2 mutations/amplification, and IDH1 from mutations (hotspot R132); see whether they are associated with classifier group (biliary-like tumours enrich for FGFR2/IDH1). IF FOUND: fit Cox OS ~ classifier + FGFR2 + IDH1 (optionally stage/age/surgery) and judge on the adjusted HR and its CI. SOURCE: general Cox modelling practice (web search unavailable).

label: Left truncation in sequencing cohorts
text: PITFALL: Survival from clinical sequencing cohorts (MSK-IMPACT) is left-truncated: patients enter the risk set only at sequencing, often months after diagnosis, while OS_MONTHS is measured from diagnosis, so naive KM/Cox gives immortal-time bias. CHECK: look for any sequencing-time or delayed-entry column; if none, note that the bias is likely non-differential across classifier groups. IF FOUND: use delayed-entry Cox (entry=time to sequencing); otherwise run the standard analysis and state the limitation without letting it alone flip the label. SOURCE: Brown et al. JAMA Oncol 2022 on left truncation in genomic cohorts (not retrieved).

label: PTEN LoF definition union
text: PITFALL: PTEN loss-of-function in this kind of data arises from truncating/missense mutations AND homozygous deletion (CNA -2) AND sometimes structural variants; counting only data_mutations.txt undercounts PTEN-altered patients. CHECK: union PTEN nonsynonymous truncating/known-hotspot mutations, data_cna.txt PTEN == -2, and data_sv.txt PTEN rows, per patient. IF FOUND: define PTEN-LoF as the union and test against outcome. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: Event coding
text: PITFALL: OS_STATUS is a string like '1:DECEASED'/'0:LIVING'; parsing it wrong flips the event coding and reverses the HR. CHECK: value_counts of OS_STATUS; check that the event fraction is plausible and that the median OS is in the expected range for IHC. IF FOUND: event = status startswith '1'; drop rows with missing OS_MONTHS. SOURCE: cBioPortal file format docs (not retrieved).

label: baseline vs acquired PTEN
text: PITFALL: Samples include pre-treatment tumor (MSK-IMPACT/Sequenom/Foundation) and cfDNA (Guardant) at pre-, on- and post-treatment timepoints; PTEN alterations that emerge on/post-treatment are acquired resistance and must not be mixed with baseline predictors of primary resistance. CHECK: tabulate PTEN events by SAMPLE_COLLECTION_TIMEPOINT and compare pre vs post cfDNA within patients. IF FOUND: analyse baseline PTEN vs clinical benefit/weeks on study, and separately report new post-treatment PTEN alterations as acquired resistance evidence. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Restrict to IHC; confounders
text: PITFALL: Mixed cohorts: the dataset holds HCC, gallbladder, EHC, biphenotypic and IHC samples; pooling them confounds classifier with tumour type. Metastatic vs primary samples and differing treatment (curative surgery) also confound OS. CHECK: filter SUBGROUP=='IHC' (one sample per patient, 1370 unique); tabulate CURATIVE_INTENT_SURGERY, METASTASIS, TUMOR_STAGE by classifier group. IF FOUND: adjust for or stratify by surgery/stage in a sensitivity Cox model; the primary claim is about IHC only. SOURCE: general practice (web search unavailable).

label: panel coverage of PTEN
text: PITFALL: Sequenom and Guardant panels may not cover PTEN or detect deletions, so absence of a PTEN call is not wild-type. CHECK: data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and platform per sample; restrict denominators to samples whose panel profiles PTEN (CNA only from MSK-IMPACT columns in data_cna.txt). IF FOUND: exclude non-profiled samples rather than counting them as PTEN-WT. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Power, EPV, PH assumption
text: PITFALL: Small classifier groups (e.g. few HCC-like IHCs) give few events, unstable HRs and wide CIs; underpowered non-significance gets read as 'contradicts'. CHECK: events per group and events per covariate (aim >=10 EPV); check the Cox PH assumption with Schoenfeld residuals. IF FOUND: limit covariates, collapse categories (HCC class+aligned), use Firth/penalized Cox if events are very sparse; read the HR direction plus CI rather than p alone. SOURCE: Peduzzi 1995 EPV; Grambsch-Therneau 1994 (not retrieved).

label: cancer type confounds signatures
text: PITFALL: Signature-response associations in pan-cancer ICB cohorts are confounded by cancer type (UV SBS7 = melanoma, smoking SBS4 = lung, APOBEC SBS2/13 = bladder/head-neck), and response rates differ by cancer type. CHECK: tabulate CANCER_TYPE vs response and each signature's exposure by CANCER_TYPE. IF FOUND: adjust for cancer type (stratified test or logistic regression with cancer type) or test within melanoma/NSCLC separately. SOURCE: Alexandrov et al. Nature 2020 (doi:10.1038/s41586-020-1943-3); not retrieved, search tool down.

label: Label convention
text: PITFALL: Under the benchmark convention, a hypothesis that reproduces the source paper's finding is labelled True even when the deposited data test it weakly; the variables here (BILIARY_SCORE/PRED_CATEGORY, FGFR2 SV, IDH1 mutation, OS) are all present, so 'Not verifiable' is very unlikely to be right. CHECK: confirm the hypothesis's cancer type (IHC), genes and endpoint all exist in the tables. IF FOUND: choose between True and False on whether the adjusted classifier HR stays in the same direction and significant (or near it) after FGFR2/IDH1 adjustment. SOURCE: task instructions.

label: small n, absence of evidence
text: PITFALL: With only ~50 patients and few PTEN-altered cases, a non-significant Fisher test is underpowered and does not support a 'no association' claim; absence of significance is not evidence of absence. CHECK: count PTEN-LoF patients and compare clinical benefit rate / weeks on study descriptively (all PTEN-altered vs WT). IF FOUND: weigh effect direction and established biology (PTEN loss reactivates PI3K signalling via PI3Kbeta and is a well-established cause of PI3Kalpha-inhibitor resistance) rather than p-value alone. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Juric et al. Nature 2015 PTEN loss in alpelisib resistance).

label: TMB confounds signatures
text: PITFALL: Signatures such as UV (SBS7) and smoking (SBS4) raise tumor mutational burden, so an apparent signature-response link may just be TMB. CHECK: correlate signature exposures/fractions with TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and fit response ~ signature + log(TMB). IF FOUND: report whether signature stays associated after TMB adjustment; distinguish absolute counts (TMB-driven) from relative fractions. SOURCE: Samstein et al. Nat Genet 2019 (doi:10.1038/s41588-018-0312-8); not retrieved.

label: restrict to PIK3CA-mut HR+
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is restricted to PIK3CA-mutant HR+ patients; including PIK3CA-WT or HER2+ patients dilutes or confounds the PTEN effect. CHECK: filter on PIK3CA_PRE_TREATMENT_TUMOR / mutation and BREAST_CANCER_SUBTYPE in data_clinical_patient.txt. IF FOUND: run the PTEN vs outcome comparison within the PIK3CA-mutant HR+ subset (and report all-patients as sensitivity). SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: No read counts in MAF
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt (9846 rows, WGS DLBCL, about 40 tumours with matched normals) has empty t_ref_count/t_alt_count/n_ref_count/n_alt_count columns, so you cannot compute VAF or cancer cell fraction and cannot run any direct clonal or subclonal reconstruction. CHECK: count the non-empty values in t_alt_count and t_ref_count. IF FOUND: do not call it Not verifiable just because VAF is missing. The hypothesis is about DLBCL, the cancer type of this study, so under the benchmark convention the label must be True or False and should rest on established biology plus whatever indirect proxies exist. SOURCE: local inspection of /biodsa-data (web search unavailable).

label: MSI not annotated; exclude hypermutators
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis says microsatellite-stable tumors, but the tables have no MSI column; MSI/MMR-deficient tumors have very high TMB and signatures SBS6/15/20/26/44 and respond strongly to ICB, which can drive associations. CHECK: flag hypermutators (e.g. TMB far above cohort distribution) and samples with high MMR-signature fraction or indel-heavy profiles; check MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2/POLE mutations. IF FOUND: exclude putative MSI/POLE samples and re-run. SOURCE: Le et al. Science 2017 (doi:10.1126/science.aan6733); not retrieved.

label: toxicity discontinuation confound
text: PITFALL: Patients who stopped for toxicity (OFF_STUDY_REASON) have short WEEKS_ON_STUDY unrelated to tumour resistance; using raw time on study conflates toxicity with resistance. CHECK: tabulate OFF_STUDY_REASON by PTEN status. IF FOUND: censor or exclude toxicity discontinuations, and use CLINICAL_BENEFIT / progression-driven endpoints. SOURCE: domain knowledge.

label: Not verifiable trap
text: PITFALL: answering Not verifiable because the tables have no clonality variable. The benchmark reserves Not verifiable for hypotheses about a different disease or cohort, and this one concerns DLBCL, which is the study's own disease (WGS, GCB/ABC subtypes, tumour cellularity columns). CHECK: confirm that CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE are DLBCL subtypes (GCB/ABC). IF FOUND: choose True or False. Established literature (bulk WGS/WES studies of DLBCL using ABSOLUTE/PyClone-style CCF analysis, for example Chapuy 2018 Nat Med and Morin 2013 Blood) reports subclonal mutations in most DLBCL tumours, which supports True unless the data clearly contradict it. SOURCE: domain knowledge; web search failed (HTTP 403), so unverified.

label: Purity vs allele-frequency cellularity
text: PITFALL: heterogeneity can be conflated with impurity. Low VAF reflects normal-cell contamination as well as subclonality. CHECK: data_clinical_sample has both EST_TUMOR_CELLULARITY (pathology) and ALLELE_FREQUENCY_CELLULARITY (VAF-derived). Compare them per sample. A VAF-derived cellularity well below pathology cellularity, or a broad VAF distribution, hints at subclonal structure. IF FOUND: describe it only as an indirect proxy for subclonality, and do not treat pathology purity alone as evidence. SOURCE: standard CCF method (Carter 2012 ABSOLUTE, Nat Biotechnol; Roth 2014 PyClone, Nat Methods); unverified, search unavailable.

label: signature fitting at low counts
text: PITFALL: Per-sample signature fitting (deconstructSigs/SigProfiler/MutationalPatterns) is unreliable at low mutation counts (<~50 SNVs) and gives spurious exposures. CHECK: count SNVs per Tumor_Sample_Barcode; build 96-trinucleotide context from GRCh37 reference (or from the codon/context column if present). IF FOUND: exclude or flag low-count samples, use a restricted signature set (e.g. SBS1,2,4,5,7,13,6/MMR), and normalise exome trinucleotide frequencies (deconstructSigs tri.counts.method='exome'). SOURCE: Rosenthal et al. Genome Biol 2016 (doi:10.1186/s13059-016-0893-4); not retrieved.

label: PTEN variant LoF classification
text: PITFALL: Not every PTEN mutation is loss-of-function; synonymous, intronic or VUS missense calls in unmatched (tumor-only) samples may be germline/passenger. CHECK: Variant_Classification and any oncogenicity annotation; prioritise truncating, splice, known hotspot (e.g. R130, R173) and biallelic events. IF FOUND: classify LoF strictly and run sensitivity with a broad definition. SOURCE: domain knowledge (OncoKB conventions).

label: Coverage limits subclone detection
text: PITFALL: at about 30x WGS (TUMOR_GENOME_COVERAGE is roughly 28-40), subclonal mutations below about 10-15% VAF are mostly undetected, so the absence of low-VAF calls underestimates heterogeneity and cannot be read as evidence of clonality. CHECK: TUMOR_GENOME_COVERAGE per sample. IF FOUND: do not answer False because the subclonal signal looks weak. Low depth biases towards apparent clonality. SOURCE: general sequencing-sensitivity principle (e.g. Griffith 2015 Cell Systems on deep validation); unverified.

label: response endpoint definition
text: PITFALL: Response definition choice changes results: the patient table has RECIST_RESPONSE, RECIST, VA_RESPONSE and ROH_RESPONSE (clinical benefit vs no clinical benefit) plus PFS/OS; mixing them or treating SD inconsistently shifts associations. CHECK: tabulate each response column and missingness; pick one primary binary endpoint (e.g. clinical benefit vs no benefit, or CR/PR vs PD) prespecified. IF FOUND: report primary result and sensitivity with alternate definitions; exclude intermediate/missing rather than coding as non-response. SOURCE: Eisenhauer et al. Eur J Cancer 2009 RECIST 1.1; not retrieved.

label: label convention in-scope
text: PITFALL: The benchmark label convention: this hypothesis is in-scope (alpelisib, PIK3CA-mutant HR+ breast cancer cohort with PTEN data), so 'Not verifiable' is almost certainly wrong; established biology holds PTEN loss confers resistance to PI3Kalpha inhibitors, so a claim of 'no association' is likely the reversed finding. CHECK: confirm cohort matches (alpelisib arms, HR+ breast). IF FOUND: answer True/False from data plus biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention + Juric et al. Nature 2015.

label: Copy number confounds VAF
text: PITFALL: VAF clusters at 0.25 or 0.75 can come from copy-number changes or LOH rather than subclones, so clustering without copy-number correction overcalls heterogeneity. CHECK: there is no CNA table here, only SV fusions. IF FOUND: any VAF-based inference has to be caveated, and the decision should lean on literature and biology. SOURCE: PyClone/ABSOLUTE methodology; unverified.

label: multiple testing
text: PITFALL: Testing many signatures across many cancer types without correction yields false positives. CHECK: count number of signature x subgroup tests. IF FOUND: apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR and emphasise the pan-cohort test; mutational signatures that consistently associate (e.g. smoking/UV via TMB, APOBEC) should be reported with q-values. label: Proxy evidence for heterogeneity

IF FOUND: a single bulk sample cannot show multi-region heterogeneity, but heterogeneity remains the established default in DLBCL (subclonal driver mutations, divergent evolution at relapse). Base the label on biology and state that this decided it. SOURCE: domain knowledge (e.g. Juskevicius 2016 Nat Commun on relapsed DLBCL clonal evolution); unverified.

IF FOUND: dedupe to one sample per patient, include synonymous SNVs for signature context, exclude DNP/indels from SBS-96. label: No translocation column - not grounds for Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: The tables (data_clinical_sample.txt: IDs, oncotree, TMB only; data_mutations.txt: MAF) contain no BCL2/IGH translocation or structural-variant column, so analysts may wrongly answer 'Not verifiable'. CHECK: grep all column headers for translocation/SV/fusion/t(14;18)/BCL2 status. IF FOUND absent: per the benchmark convention the hypothesis is about this study's genes (DLBCL cohort, BCL2 is mutated in the MAF), so decide True/False from the closest variables plus established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task text; web search unavailable (Exa HTTP 403).

label: Scope: CLL WES study
text: PITFALL: Treating 'not verifiable' as the answer because the tables lack a driver/significance column; this dataset is a CLL whole-exome cohort (ONCOTREE CLLSLL, WXS, matched normals) so a hypothesis about CLL genes is about this study and must be labeled True/False. CHECK: confirm CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED is CLL/SLL in data_clinical_sample.txt and that RPS15 and IKZF3 appear in Hugo_Symbol of data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: decide True/False from mutation recurrence plus established biology. SOURCE: task convention; library web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: BCL2 mutations co-occur with t(14;18) via aSHM
text: PITFALL: Treating BCL2 mutations and BCL2/IGH t(14;18) as mutually exclusive alternatives (like KRAS/BRAF). Established biology: BCL2 point mutations in lymphoma arise from AID-driven somatic hypermutation targeting the translocated BCL2 allele juxtaposed to the IGH enhancers, so BCL2 mutations are strongly ENRICHED in t(14;18)-positive FL and GCB-DLBCL (DLBCL genetic-subtype papers group BCL2 mutations with BCL2 SVs in the same cluster, e.g. C3/EZB). CHECK: whether BCL2-mutated samples co-occur with other EZB/GCB markers (EZH2, KMT2D, CREBBP, TNFRSF14, many BCL2 hits per sample). IF FOUND: co-occurrence evidence contradicts a 'never co-occur' claim. SOURCE: established literature (Schuetz/Morin/Chapuy 2018 Nat Med, Schmitz 2018 NEJM); web search unavailable.

label: Low-frequency drivers vs background
text: PITFALL: Judging 'involvement' by raw mutation frequency alone; CLL drivers like RPS15 and IKZF3 are low-frequency (~2-5%) so a few percent of patients can look negligible. CHECK: count unique patients with non-silent mutations (exclude Silent, Intron, UTR, Flank, IGR) in RPS15 and IKZF3 and compare against an expectation given gene length and cohort-wide nonsynonymous rate (TMB is in clinical table). IF FOUND: a gene recurrently mutated far above background in a small protein (RPS15 is ~145 aa) is evidence of driver involvement, contradicting a 'not involved' claim. SOURCE: MutSigCV rationale, Lawrence et al. Nature 2013 (from prior knowledge; search unavailable).

label: BCL2 silent/UTR mutations = SHM signature
text: PITFALL: Counting BCL2 mutation rate only from nonsynonymous calls underestimates SHM; in this MAF BCL2 has ~34 Silent, 29 Missense, ~60 5'UTR/5'Flank calls - a hallmark of AID aberrant somatic hypermutation (clustered within ~2 kb of the TSS), which in BCL2 is characteristic of the translocated allele. CHECK: tabulate BCL2 Variant_Classification and count mutations per sample (multiple hits per sample = SHM pattern). IF FOUND: interpret many-hits-per-sample BCL2 as translocation-associated SHM, not independent driver mutations. SOURCE: Pasqualucci 2001 Nature (aSHM); web search unavailable.

label: Hotspot clustering RPS15 IKZF3
text: PITFALL: Missing hotspot/positional clustering evidence; IKZF3 in CLL carries a recurrent hotspot (L162R) and RPS15 mutations cluster in a short C-terminal region (roughly codons 130-145), which is strong driver evidence even at low frequency. CHECK: tabulate HGVSp_Short / protein position for RPS15 and IKZF3 non-silent mutations and look for repeated identical changes or tight clustering. IF FOUND: treat recurrent identical missense changes in unrelated patients as driver evidence (contradicts hypothesis). SOURCE: Landau et al. Nature 2015; Ljungstrom et al. Blood 2016 (prior knowledge; search unavailable).

label: Universal negative claim, decide via biology
text: PITFALL: Applying a 'absence of evidence' logic: one cannot show zero co-occurrence without translocation calls, and a definite universal claim ('do not occur') is contradicted by known co-occurrence in the literature. CHECK: whether any variable proxies BCL2 rearrangement (none in these tables). IF FOUND absent: decide from established biology, and state in reasoning that biology (not a direct test) decided the label. SOURCE: task label convention; web search unavailable.

label: Patient-level dedup
text: PITFALL: Counting mutations instead of patients, or double counting multiple samples per patient, inflates recurrence. CHECK: map Tumor_Sample_Barcode to PATIENT_ID and deduplicate; check whether any patients have more than one tumor sample. IF FOUND: report patient-level frequency. SOURCE: general MAF analysis practice (prior knowledge).

label: Sample QC for mutation counts
text: PITFALL: Low TMB or tumor-only/unmatched samples and hypermutated samples can inflate or deflate per-gene mutation counts. CHECK: SOMATIC_STATUS column (Matched vs Unmatched) and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS outliers; dedupe by Tumor_Sample_Barcode. IF FOUND: report BCL2 results with and without unmatched/hypermutated samples. SOURCE: general MAF QC practice; web search unavailable.

label: Expression is secondary evidence
text: PITFALL: Using expression (TPM / z-scores) to argue a gene is not involved; driver involvement of RPS15 and IKZF3 is via somatic mutation, and ubiquitous RPS15 expression or unremarkable IKZF3 z-scores do not argue against involvement. CHECK: use data_mutations.txt as primary evidence; expression only secondary (e.g. mutant vs wild-type). IF FOUND: do not flip the label based on null expression differences in small mutant groups (low power). SOURCE: general practice (prior knowledge).

label: Artifact / VAF check
text: PITFALL: Germline or artifact calls masquerading as somatic recurrence, or low-VAF calls. CHECK: SOMATIC_STATUS is Matched in clinical table; inspect t_alt_count/t_ref_count for RPS15/IKZF3 calls. IF FOUND: drop low-support calls but expect genuine subclonal drivers in CLL to have modest VAF; do not discard just for VAF<0.2. SOURCE: general practice (prior knowledge).

label: Power and established biology
text: PITFALL: Concluding absence of association with outcome or IGHV status means 'not involved'. CHECK: if testing clinical links, note small mutant counts (likely <30 patients) give very low power. IF FOUND: rely on recurrence/hotspot evidence for involvement; established literature names RPS15 and IKZF3 as recurrently mutated CLL driver genes, so the 'not involved' hypothesis is expected to be False. SOURCE: Landau et al. Nature 2015 (prior knowledge; search unavailable).

CHECK: denominator = all samples listed as profiled in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt (about 97-98 BLCA samples), not unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode in the MAF. IF FOUND: compute fraction = samples with >=1 qualifying alteration / all profiled samples. SOURCE: general cBioPortal practice (web search tool unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: Actionable gene set definition
text: PITFALL: 'Actionable' depends on the gene list; including TP53 or RB1 (not druggable) inflates it, while omitting PI3K/mTOR or RTK/RAS genes deflates it. CHECK: report the fraction under a pathway-based definition (PI3K/AKT/mTOR: PIK3CA, PIK3R1, PTEN, TSC1, AKT1, AKT3; RTK/RAS/RAF: FGFR3, KRAS, BRAF; optionally CDKN2A as CDK4/6 target) and a sensitivity variant with and without CDKN2A. IF FOUND: base the label on the definition that matches the study's pathway framing (PI3K/mTOR + RTK/RAS), and state whether the conclusion survives across definitions. SOURCE: OncoKB levels of evidence, https://www.oncokb.org/levels (not retrieved; tool down).

Mutation-only counts underestimate. CHECK: confirm no CNA file exists; mRNA z-scores (diploid-reference file) can proxy amplification (e.g., z>2) or deep loss for those genes. IF FOUND: report mutation-only as a lower bound and mutation+expression-proxy as an upper bound; per the benchmark convention, missing CNA does NOT make the claim Not verifiable since the cohort is bladder cancer from the same study. SOURCE: general knowledge (tool down).

The clinical tables have only OS/DFS and BLCA codes, but the cohort is a bladder urothelial carcinoma series (MSKCC_BLCA panel), i.e. the study the claim comes from. label: Use CI, not exact equality, against 61%

CHECK: compute Wilson CI for the actionable fraction under each definition. IF FOUND: call True if 61% lies within the CI for the study-consistent definition (PI3K/mTOR + RTK/RAS, mutations, with CNA lower-bound caveat); call False only if the fraction is clearly far (e.g. >15 points) from 61% under all reasonable definitions. label: Cohort mismatch: lung data, thyroid hypothesis
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about anaplastic vs other thyroid cancers, but this dataset is an MSK lung cancer cfDNA/tumour study (2539 of ~2620 samples are Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer; panels ctDx_lung_panel, ACCESS129, IMPACT; patient columns include SMOKING_STATUS, SUCCESSFUL_CTDX_LUNG, METABOLIC_TUMOR_VOL). IF FOUND (no thyroid tumours): per the benchmark convention the hypothesis comes from a different publication and the correct label is 'Not verifiable'; do not test lung subgroups as a proxy and do not count a metastatic site as tumour type. SOURCE: direct inspection of /biodsa-data headers (web search unavailable).

label: Signatures from panel data overfit
text: PITFALL: Mutational signatures (SBS96 decomposition) are unreliable from targeted panels: a few hundred kb gives typically <10 SNVs per sample, so refitting overfits and assigns spurious signatures. CHECK: count SNVs per sample in data_mutations.txt and the panel size per GENE_PANEL. IF FOUND (<~20-50 SNVs/sample): pool by group, restrict to dominant signatures (e.g. SBS4 smoking, SBS2/13 APOBEC, SBS1 ageing) or compare simple spectra (C>A fraction, TMB), and use bootstrapped refitting. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1943-3 ; https://github.com/AlexandrovLab/SigProfilerAssignment (not retrieved; search down).

label: Missing fusion data is not Not-verifiable
text: PITFALL: The tables may hold no fusion calls at all (no data_sv/data_fusions file; MAF may only hold SNVs/indels), so a team may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: grep data_mutations.txt Variant_Classification and Hugo_Symbol for RSPO2/RSPO3 and any 'Fusion'/'SV' classes; list all files. IF FOUND (no fusions): per the task convention, a claim about this study's cancer type and genes is still True/False; decide from APC status in the MAF plus established biology, not Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention; cBioPortal file formats docs https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: CHIP contamination in cfDNA
text: PITFALL: cfDNA panels (ctDx, ACCESS) capture clonal haematopoiesis (CHIP) variants (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, TP53) that are not tumour-derived and distort mutation spectra and burden. CHECK: look for CHIP genes at low VAF in cfDNA samples, and whether matched-WBC filtering was applied. IF FOUND: exclude CHIP genes/low-VAF calls or analyse tumour-tissue samples separately. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-019-0652-7 (Razavi et al. 2019; not retrieved).

label: RSPO fusions vs APC biology
text: PITFALL: Established biology: RSPO2/RSPO3 fusions (e.g. EIF3E-RSPO2, PTPRK-RSPO3) activate Wnt signalling upstream and were reported to be mutually exclusive with APC mutations in colorectal cancer, the opposite of co-occurrence. CHECK: if RSPO fusion samples can be identified, tabulate their APC status (truncating vs none) vs the rest. IF FOUND: mutual exclusivity (RSPO-fusion tumours APC wild-type) contradicts a 'frequently co-occur' claim. SOURCE: Seshagiri et al. Nature 2012, doi:10.1038/nature11282 (from prior knowledge; web search unavailable)

label: Panel heterogeneity confound
text: PITFALL: Pooling samples sequenced on different panels (ctDx_lung_panel, ACCESS129, IMPACT341/410/468/505) confounds group comparisons of TMB or spectra because footprint and gene content differ. CHECK: cross-tabulate group vs GENE_PANEL via data_gene_panel_matrix.txt. IF FOUND: restrict to genes common to all panels, normalise per Mb, or stratify by panel. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1136/jitc-2019-000147 (TMB harmonisation; not retrieved).

label: Define APC mutation as truncating
text: PITFALL: Counting any APC variant as 'APC mutant' (silent, intronic, missense of unknown significance, subclonal low-VAF calls) inflates APC-mutant rates, especially in hypermutated/MSI tumours, and can create false co-occurrence. CHECK: restrict APC to protein-truncating (Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site) calls, check t_alt_count/VAF, and compare rates in MSS vs MSI samples. IF FOUND: base co-occurrence on truncating/driver APC calls only. SOURCE: standard MAF practice; Cancer Genome Atlas Network Nature 2012 doi:10.1038/nature11252

label: Repeated samples per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (tissue + cfDNA, serial draws) inflate n and duplicate mutations in group comparisons. CHECK: count SAMPLE_IDs per PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: collapse to one sample per patient (or use patient-level mixed models) before testing. SOURCE: general statistical practice (search unavailable).

label: Hypermutation biases co-occurrence
text: PITFALL: Hypermutated/MSI tumours carry mutations in almost every gene, so co-occurrence tests across all samples are biased toward co-occurrence (and away from mutual exclusivity). CHECK: split by MSI_STATUS and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS (e.g. >10-20 mut/Mb) and repeat the cross-tab in MSS only. IF FOUND: report the MSS-only result or use a rate-aware test (DISCOVER) rather than plain Fisher. SOURCE: Canisius et al. Genome Biol 2016 doi:10.1186/s13059-016-1114-x

label: Few fusion carriers, low power
text: PITFALL: Small counts: RSPO fusions occur in ~5-10% of CRC, so only a handful of carriers; a Fisher test will be underpowered and a non-significant p is not evidence of co-occurrence. CHECK: report the 2x2 table counts and odds ratio with CI, not just a p-value. IF FOUND: judge direction from the counts (e.g. how many fusion carriers are APC-mutant) and established biology. SOURCE: general statistical guidance; Canisius et al. 2016 doi:10.1186/s13059-016-1114-x

label: Compare against APC baseline rate
text: PITFALL: 'Co-occur' must be judged against the baseline: APC is mutated in ~70-80% of CRC, so carriers of any alteration will often be APC-mutant by chance; a claim of co-occurrence requires enrichment above baseline, and depletion means mutual exclusivity. CHECK: compare APC-truncation rate in RSPO-fusion carriers vs non-carriers (also check CTNNB1 and RNF43 for Wnt-exclusivity context). IF FOUND: depletion supports False. SOURCE: Leiserson et al. (WExT) Bioinformatics 2016 doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btw462

label: Sample ID harmonisation
text: PITFALL: Sample ID mismatch: mutation Tumor_Sample_Barcode may differ in format from clinical SAMPLE_ID (numeric ids, multiple samples per patient), so samples with zero APC calls get silently dropped or wrongly treated as wild-type. CHECK: verify every clinical SAMPLE_ID appears in the MAF and that samples absent from the MAF are counted as profiled wild-type only if they were sequenced. IF FOUND: harmonise IDs and use the clinical table as the denominator. SOURCE: cBioPortal file formats https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/

label: left truncation
text: PITFALL: In MSK-IMPACT cohorts, sequencing often happens months or years after diagnosis, so survival measured from diagnosis without delayed entry gives immortal-time/left-truncation bias, which favours genotypes sequenced late. CHECK: Inspect OS_MONTHS_DIAG_TO_COLL (sample table) and compare it with OVERALL_SURVIVAL_MONTHS / OS_MONTHS_DIAGNOSIS_TO_FU; see how many patients have a large diagnosis-to-sequencing gap. IF FOUND: Fit Cox with delayed entry (start=time diag->collection, stop=OS from diagnosis; lifelines entry_col / R Surv(start,stop,event)) or measure OS from sequencing, and report whether the SMAD4/STK11 hazard ratios change. SOURCE: Brown S et al., JCO Clin Cancer Inform 2022 (left truncation in real-world genomic cohorts), not retrieved because search was unavailable.

label: Hypothesis is in-scope for this HCC dataset
text: PITFALL: Treating the question as 'Not verifiable' because the tables lack a mutational-signature column; the cohort is HCC with a CHRONIC_HEPATITIS_ANY_TYPE field (HBV/HCV/NBNC) and a MAF with Reference_Allele/Tumor_Seq_Allele2, so the hypothesis is about this study. CHECK: confirm sample IDs prefixed HB/HC/NBNC and the hepatitis column. IF FOUND: answer True/False, deriving the 6-class substitution spectrum (C>A,C>G,C>T,T>A,T>C,T>G, pyrimidine-collapsed) per sample from the MAF. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: multiple survival columns
text: PITFALL: The clinical tables hold several OS definitions (patient OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS, OS_MONTHS_DMT/OS_STATUS_DMT, CRDB_SURVIVAL_STATUS, sample OVERALL_SURVIVAL_MONTHS, OS_MONTHS_DIAGNOSIS_TO_FU), and many are blank, so choosing the wrong one silently drops patients or mismatches event and time. CHECK: Count non-missing values for each time/status pair, and make sure the status column you pair with a time column describes the same follow-up. IF FOUND: Use the most complete pair that is consistent from diagnosis (or from sequencing, with truncation handled); state which one you used, and run a sensitivity analysis with the other pair. SOURCE: cBioPortal clinical data format docs (https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/), not retrieved.

label: Low power and signature overfitting
text: PITFALL: Very small cohort (about 21 sequenced tumours, roughly 9 HBV, 9-10 HCV, 2 NBNC) with few exome mutations each, so per-sample signature refitting (deconstructSigs/SigProfiler) overfits and p-values are underpowered; non-significance is not evidence against the hypothesis. CHECK: count mutations per sample and per group; if many samples have <50 SNVs signature fitting is unreliable. IF FOUND: pool SNVs by etiology group and compare 6-class (or 96-context) spectra with chi-square/Fisher test, report effect sizes, and weigh descriptive differences together with established biology rather than only a p-value. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: one sample per patient
text: PITFALL: Patients can have several sequenced samples (T01, T02, primary and metastasis), so analysing at sample level counts a patient's survival more than once. CHECK: Compare the number of unique PATIENT_IDs with SAMPLE_IDs. IF FOUND: Collapse to one row per patient (a patient counts as altered if any sample carries the alteration, or take the first sample), then fit survival at patient level. SOURCE: general survival-analysis independence assumption (Therneau & Grambsch 2000), not retrieved.

label: Multi-region sample duplication
text: PITFALL: Multi-region samples from one patient (e.g. HC3-1/HC3-2, HC7-1) double-count shared mutations and inflate one group's spectrum. CHECK: list Tumor_Sample_Barcode values with -1/-2 suffixes and map to PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: deduplicate per patient (union of unique variants or keep one region) before group comparisons. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Hypermutator dominance in pooled spectra
text: PITFALL: Pooling mutations across samples lets one hypermutated tumour dominate the group spectrum. CHECK: compare per-sample mutation counts and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS; look for outliers. IF FOUND: compare per-sample proportions (e.g. Wilcoxon on fraction of each substitution class) instead of, or in addition to, pooled counts. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: define metastatic subset
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is about METASTATIC gallbladder carcinoma, but the cohort probably mixes resected/localized and metastatic disease, and stage is a strong confounder of both mutation frequency and survival. CHECK: Identify the metastatic patients via TUMOR_STAGE_COLLECTION (stage 4), SAMPLE_TYPE=Metastasis, or METASTATIC_SITE, and check that CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED is gallbladder. IF FOUND: Run the primary analysis in the stage IV/metastatic subset, and in the full cohort adjust for stage; report both. SOURCE: standard confounding guidance (Hernán & Robins, Causal Inference), not retrieved.

label: Spectrum construction errors
text: PITFALL: Not collapsing substitutions to the pyrimidine reference strand (G>T counted separately from C>A) and including indels/DNPs in SNV spectra distorts the comparison; also strand-specific patterns (e.g. T>C transcribed-strand bias) need Strand info. CHECK: Variant_Type=SNP only; complement purine-ref changes. IF FOUND: recompute spectrum after filtering and collapsing. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: independence needs multivariable model
text: PITFALL: 'Independently associated' means each gene stays significant in a multivariable Cox model that includes the other gene and the clinical covariates (stage, age, sex, etc.); a univariable log-rank test alone does not show independence. CHECK: Fit Cox OS ~ SMAD4 + STK11 + stage (+age), check events per variable (EPV>=10) and the proportional-hazards assumption (cox.zph / Schoenfeld residuals). IF FOUND: If STK11 is altered in very few patients (expect <5%), the estimate is unstable; use Firth-penalized Cox or report it as underpowered rather than as a null effect, and judge both genes separately. SOURCE: Peduzzi et al., J Clin Epidemiol 1995 (EPV); Heinze & Schemper 2001 (Firth Cox), not retrieved.

label: Confounding of etiology
text: PITFALL: Etiology confounded by alcohol, age and sex (e.g. ALCOHOL column; HCV patients typically older), so spectral differences may not be due to virus. CHECK: cross-tabulate ALCOHOL, AGE, SEX by hepatitis group. IF FOUND: state the confounding in reasoning; stratify descriptively if possible. Established HCC literature reports etiology-associated differences in mutation spectra and driver frequencies (e.g. TP53 R249S with aflatoxin/HBV regions, HBV integration events, distinct substitution patterns between HBV and HCV tumours). SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: alteration definition incl CNA
text: PITFALL: SMAD4 is often inactivated by homozygous deletion (CNA=-2) and STK11 by deletion or truncation, so counting only data_mutations.txt undercounts alterations; including silent or VUS missense variants adds noise. CHECK: Combine nonsynonymous mutations (Variant_Classification excluding Silent/Intron/UTR) with data_cna.txt -2 calls (and data_sv.txt fusions/rearrangements) for each gene; tabulate the counts for each source. IF FOUND: Define 'altered' as oncogenic mutation OR deep deletion, run a sensitivity analysis with mutation-only, and confirm the conclusion does not depend on that choice. SOURCE: cBioPortal OncoKB annotation / Chakravarty et al. JCO PO 2017, not retrieved.

label: Gene-level vs spectrum-level tests
text: PITFALL: Comparing only driver-gene frequencies (TP53, CTNNB1, AXIN1, ARID1A) with tiny counts gives no significance and is misread as 'no influence'; mutation pattern also means substitution spectrum. CHECK: test both gene-level frequencies (Fisher) and substitution spectra by group. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on the full pattern; HCC etiology–mutation pattern links are established biology and the source publication likely reported a difference. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: panel coverage
text: PITFALL: Samples were sequenced on different MSK-IMPACT panels (IMPACT341/410/468), and an unprofiled gene is not the same as a wild-type gene. CHECK: Use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and the panel gene lists to confirm that SMAD4 and STK11 are on every panel used (both are on IMPACT341+). IF FOUND: Exclude samples whose panel lacks the gene instead of coding them wild-type. SOURCE: Cheng et al., J Mol Diagn 2015 (MSK-IMPACT), not retrieved.

label: label convention
text: PITFALL: Under the benchmark convention, a hypothesis about gallbladder cancer on an MSK gallbladder cohort with mutation + OS data is about this study, so 'Not verifiable' is almost certainly wrong; the label is True or False. CHECK: Confirm CANCER_TYPE is gallbladder, that SMAD4/STK11 appear in the data, and that OS columns exist. IF FOUND: Decide True or False from the stage-appropriate multivariable Cox result; if only one gene, or neither, is independently significant in the metastatic subset, that argues for False on a joint claim. SOURCE: task instructions.

label: No fusion-negative comparator
text: PITFALL: The cohort may contain only TRK fusion-positive patients (clinical columns like POS_ARCHER/POS_IMPACT/ANY_LINE_NTRK suggest a fusion-selected series), so there may be no internal fusion-negative comparator and the analyst may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: tabulate fusion status per sample from data_sv.txt and the POS_* columns; count samples with no NTRK1/2/3 fusion. IF FOUND (no negatives): the study is still about TRK fusions and has a TMB variable, so per the benchmark convention answer True/False from the study's comparison vs an external fusion-negative reference and established biology: in pan-cancer series kinase-fusion-driven tumours, including TRK fusion cancers, generally have low TMB and lack canonical drivers, with the notable exception of MSI-high colorectal cancers. SOURCE: domain knowledge (research tool returned HTTP 403; unverified).

label: TMB assay comparability
text: PITFALL: TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is not comparable across assays: samples with suffix -AS (Archer RNA fusion panel) have no DNA mutation calls, and MSK-IMPACT versions IM3/IM5/IM6/IM7 cover different megabases. CHECK: group TMB by sample-ID suffix and by data_gene_panel_matrix.txt; note panel matrix labels everything WXS, which may be wrong. IF FOUND: exclude Archer-only samples from TMB analysis (treat their TMB as missing, not zero) and use panel-normalised mutations/Mb. SOURCE: domain knowledge; Friends of Cancer Research TMB harmonization (Merino et al., JITC 2020, https://jitc.bmj.com/content/8/1/e000147) - unverified, research tool down.

label: Duplicate samples per patient
text: PITFALL: Multiple samples per patient (e.g. T01 and T02) inflate n and double count. CHECK: count SAMPLE_ID per PATIENT_ID in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient (first/primary IMPACT DNA sample) before comparing. SOURCE: domain knowledge (research tool unavailable).

label: Skew and MSI-H outliers
text: PITFALL: TMB is extremely right-skewed and a few MSI-high/hypermutated tumours (notably colorectal NTRK fusions, which are enriched for MSI-H/MLH1 silencing) dominate the mean and can make fusion-positive look higher. CHECK: inspect TMB distribution, flag TMB>20 mut/Mb and colorectal/MSI cases. IF FOUND: use medians and Mann-Whitney / log-TMB, and report results with and without MSI-H/colorectal outliers. SOURCE: domain knowledge (research tool unavailable).

label: Cancer-type confounding
text: PITFALL: Cancer type confounds TMB (e.g. melanoma/lung high, sarcoma/thyroid/salivary/pediatric tumours low; TRK fusions are enriched in rare low-TMB histologies such as secretory carcinoma, infantile fibrosarcoma, papillary thyroid). CHECK: cross-tab fusion status by CANCER_TYPE and age. IF FOUND: compare within cancer type (stratified Wilcoxon / regression on log TMB with cancer-type term) rather than a pooled comparison. SOURCE: domain knowledge (research tool unavailable).

label: Fusion status definition

CHECK: verify NTRK is the 3' partner with kinase domain retained and in-frame, and reconcile with POS_ARCHER/POS_IMPACT/POS_METHOD. IF FOUND: define fusion-positive by the study's clinical confirmation columns and run a sensitivity analysis. SOURCE: domain knowledge (research tool unavailable).

IF FOUND: pool SNVs across the cohort or subgroup into one 96-channel profile and fit to COSMIC signatures, or restrict per-sample calls to high-count samples; treat low-count per-sample results as noise. label: no trinucleotide context
text: PITFALL: The MAF lacks trinucleotide context columns, so naive 96-channel classification is impossible without a reference genome; using only the 6 substitution classes misattributes signatures. CHECK: confirm whether a GRCh37 FASTA is available offline; if not, the strongest feasible proxy for clock-like SBS1 is the fraction of C>T at CpG, which needs context; the HGVSc/Codons field (e.g. cGg/cAg) gives the flanking bases for coding SNVs. IF FOUND: derive context from the Codons column (the uppercase base is mutated, lowercase are neighbours, but only within the codon, so edge positions lack one flank) or label the analysis as 6-class only and interpret conservatively. SOURCE: https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/sbs/ (COSMIC SBS; not fetched).

label: aging vs SBS17 in EAC
text: PITFALL: The 'aging' (clock-like) signatures are SBS1 (C>T at CpG via 5mC deamination) and SBS5; in esophageal adenocarcinoma the hallmark is SBS17a/b (T>G at CTT context), plus SBS2/13 (APOBEC) and SBS3 (HRD), so dominance of C>T alone is not proof of aging. CHECK: compute the cohort-level substitution spectrum and specifically the T>G (A>C) fraction and the C>T fraction at CpG versus non-CpG. IF FOUND: a high T>G fraction indicates SBS17 contributes substantially; call aging dominant only if CpG C>T (SBS1) plus SBS5 exceed the other signatures. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3659 (Secrier et al. 2016, EAC signatures; not fetched).

label: hotspot bias
text: PITFALL: Targeted panels are biased toward cancer hotspots (e.g. TP53 R175H, R248, R273 CpG C>T; PIK3CA, KRAS G12), so recurrent selected driver mutations inflate CpG C>T and mimic SBS1. IF FOUND: base the signature conclusion on the hotspot-excluded spectrum; a large drop in CpG C>T means the aging signal was driven by selection. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-11037-8 (not fetched).

label: cHCC-ICC: which patients are testable
text: PITFALL: Only Separate-type patients (6 patients, ~14 samples incl. multi-nodule Sep cases with C1H/C1I/C2H/C2I) have two independently sampled components; Combined-type patients split into those with LCM-paired H and I samples (41) and those sampled whole as T (15); Mixed-type (59) have a single T sample only, so their clonality cannot be tested from pairs. CHECK: tabulate ALLEN_AND_LISA_TYPE x TUMOR_SAMPLES in data_clinical_patient and count samples per patient. IF FOUND: assess clonality per patient only where >=2 component samples exist; for single-sample Mixed/Combined T tumours, a single tumour sample cannot show multiclonality directly, so the claim that they are all monoclonal must rest on paired Combined H&I patients plus established biology (study framing), not on absent evidence. SOURCE: no web access (search returned HTTP 403); derived from data headers and standard multi-region practice.

label: Shared-mutation clonality call
text: PITFALL: Calling two components clonally related from any single shared mutation produces false 'monoclonal' calls, since shared germline leakage, recurrent hotspots (TERT promoter, TP53 R249S in HBV/aflatoxin) or artefacts can be shared by independent tumours; conversely calling 'multiclonal' because few mutations are shared ignores branching evolution. CHECK: per patient compute shared vs private non-silent+silent somatic mutations (same chr, position, alt) between H and I samples; compare to the background expected for unrelated pairs (e.g. shared counts across samples from different patients). IF FOUND: define monoclonal as multiple shared truncal mutations well above the inter-patient background (unrelated pairs should share ~0); define multiclonal (collision) as zero/near-zero private-only overlap, as in the convention of clonal-relatedness tests (e.g. Ostrovnaya et al. Clonality method). SOURCE: no web access; standard method (Ostrovnaya I, Begg CB, Clonality R/Bioconductor package).

label: Purity/coverage false private calls
text: PITFALL: Mutations absent in one sample may be present below calling threshold (low purity or LCM low DNA input), making a monoclonal pair look multiclonal. CHECK: for mutations private to one component, look at t_ref_count/t_alt_count in data_mutations; check whether the other sample has coverage at that site (if only called mutations are listed, compare depth/VAF distributions and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS per sample). IF FOUND: treat pairs with low-VAF/low-depth samples as uncertain, not as multiclonal; weight decision on high-VAF (clonal) mutations. SOURCE: no web access; general multi-region WES practice.

label: Expected biology Separate vs Combined
text: PITFALL: Separate-type cHCC-ICC (spatially distinct HCC and ICC nodules) is classically considered to include both collision tumours (multiclonal, independent origin) and intrahepatic spread of one clone (monoclonal); Combined/Mixed (intermingled/transitional) types are generally reported as monoclonal. A claim negating this ('Separate are not of both origins, Combined/Mixed not all monoclonal') is the reversed form of the usual finding. CHECK: for each Separate patient (including each nodule pair C1/C2 in multi-nodule cases) classify shared vs no shared mutations; for each Combined H&I pair check shared mutations. IF FOUND: if Separate patients show a mixture of shared and non-shared pairs and all Combined pairs share mutations, the data contradict the hypothesis. SOURCE: no web access; established literature on cHCC-ICC classification (Allen & Lisa 1949; WHO 2019).

label: A>C at AA equals T>G at TT
text: PITFALL: A>C at AA and T>G at TT are the same mutation class on opposite strands (pyrimidine-collapsed notation used by COSMIC SBS); counting only Reference_Allele=A & alt=C undercounts by about half and misreads the context. CHECK: count SNPs with (ref A, alt C, 3' or 5' neighbour A) plus (ref T, alt G, neighbour T) together, after reverse-complementing purine refs. IF FOUND: always report strand-collapsed T>G with flanking T (the COSMIC SBS17-like CTT/TTT peak). SOURCE: https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/sbs/ (not fetched; search tool down)

label: Multi-nodule pairwise comparisons
text: PITFALL: Multi-nodule Separate cases (sample codes C1H, C1I, C2H, C2I, CH, CI, H) contain several nodules; comparing only one H/I pair, or merging nodules, misses that one patient can have both related and unrelated nodules. CHECK: list all sample IDs per Separate patient and do all pairwise shared-mutation comparisons. IF FOUND: report clonality per nodule pair; a single patient with both a related and an unrelated pair still evidences both origins within Separate type. SOURCE: no web access; multi-region practice.

label: Match variants by coordinate
text: PITFALL: Matching mutations by gene name or protein change instead of genomic coordinate and allele inflates sharing (different mutations in the same driver gene e.g. TP53 do not prove common origin). CHECK: match on Chromosome+Start_Position+Reference_Allele+Tumor_Seq_Allele2. IF FOUND: use exact-variant matching; treat same-gene-different-variant as evidence of independent origin (convergent), not shared. SOURCE: no web access; standard practice.

label: No context column in MAF
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt (exome MAF, ~28k SNPs, 152 samples) has NO trinucleotide/ref_context column, so dinucleotide context cannot be read directly. CHECK: look for a reference FASTA (likely none); otherwise use the Codons / codon_change / Codon_Change columns, where the mutated base is uppercase inside a lowercase codon in VEP format (e.g. aAg/aCg), and take the neighbouring codon base on the transcript strand, mapping back to genome strand via Transcript_Strand/Strand. IF FOUND: limit the context analysis to coding SNPs whose neighbour lies inside the codon (positions 1-2 or 2-3), state the restriction, and do not claim genome-wide numbers. SOURCE: https://www.ensembl.org/info/docs/tools/vep/vep_formats.html (not fetched)

label: SV sharing as support

label: Normalize context to opportunity
text: PITFALL: a raw count of A>C at AA is not evidence of a signature, because AA/TT dinucleotides are very common in the genome and exome. CHECK: compare the fraction of A>C (strand-collapsed T>G) SNPs with an A/T neighbour against that fraction for other A>N/T>N substitutions in the same samples, or against the exome's background ApA/TpT frequency; test enrichment with a Fisher or binomial test. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on enrichment relative to that background, not on absolute counts. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12477 (Alexandrov 2013 signatures; not fetched)

label: SBS17 is EAC hallmark
text: PITFALL: in the EAC literature, A>C (T>G) transversions at AA/TT, i.e. COSMIC SBS17a/b at CTT, are a well-known hallmark mutational signature of oesophageal adenocarcinoma, linked to acid/oxidative damage (8-oxo-dGTP), and are one of the defining features of EAC exome studies. A hypothesis that this is NOT a signature in EAC therefore runs against established biology. CHECK: see whether A>C/T>G is a large share of transversions (the EAC literature reports it as one of the most frequent classes, unusually high compared with other tumour types). IF FOUND: if the data show this enrichment, it contradicts the negated claim. SOURCE: https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/sbs/sbs17b/ (not fetched)

CHECK: compute the A>C share per sample (TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS / NONSILENT_PER_MB exist in the sample table), look at the distribution and the fraction of samples above the background expectation, and redo the analysis without the top-mutated samples. label: MAF SNP cleaning

label: PIK3R1 biology direction
text: PITFALL: Deciding direction of a drug-sensitivity claim from genomics alone without stating the biology. Established biology: PIK3R1 encodes p85alpha, the regulatory subunit that restrains p110 PI3K; loss or truncating/iSH2 mutations relieve inhibition, raise PI3K/AKT signalling and destabilise PTEN, so PIK3R1-altered models are generally expected to be MORE dependent on and sensitive to PI3K/AKT inhibition (cf. Cheung et al., Cancer Discovery 2011 and Cancer Cell 2014; some PIK3R1 mutants also signal via ERK). CHECK: in the data, test whether PIK3R1 loss co-occurs with or is mutually exclusive with PTEN loss/PIK3CA/AKT1 alterations (mutual exclusivity supports PIK3R1 as an alternative PI3K-activating driver). IF FOUND: weigh a 'decreased sensitivity' claim against this mechanistic expectation; the hypothesis may be the study's finding reversed. SOURCE: background knowledge (search unavailable), e.g. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Cheung+PIK3R1+mutations+cancer+discovery+2011

label: library search unavailable
text: NOTE: The library's web search tool failed (HTTP 502/403) on every call, so the pitfalls below come from established field knowledge, not from retrieved documents; the cited references were not re-checked online.

label: no control group in tables
text: PITFALL: The tables appear to contain only cancer patients (124 patients with breast, NSCLC or prostate cancer, each with a cfDNA sample and a tumour sample, matched to a WBC normal). There are no non-cancer control samples, so 'controls' cannot be tested directly, and an analyst may wrongly answer Not verifiable. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS/CANCER_TYPE in data_clinical_sample.txt and look for any healthy or non-cancer group. IF FOUND (no controls): the benchmark convention says a hypothesis about this study's own finding is True/False even when a variable is missing. Measure CH in the patients' cfDNA, then decide from established biology: CH-derived cfDNA variants are well documented in non-cancer individuals, especially older ones. SOURCE: Genovese et al. NEJM 2014; Jaiswal et al. NEJM 2014; Hu et al. Clin Cancer Res 2018 (general literature, not retrieved).

label: use WBC alt counts to flag CH
text: PITFALL: If cfDNA variants are called without matched white-blood-cell (WBC) sequencing, clonal hematopoiesis variants look like tumour-derived mutations. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt, cfDNA rows (Tumor_Sample_Barcode ending _cfdna) are paired with Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode ending _wbc. Use n_alt_count/n_depth to find cfDNA variants that are also present in the WBC (n_alt_count>0 or WBC VAF comparable to cfDNA VAF). IF FOUND: classify those variants as CH-derived (WBC-matched), not tumour-derived, and report what fraction of cfDNA variants they make up. SOURCE: Razavi-style matched cfDNA–WBC designs; Hu et al. Clin Cancer Res 2018 (not retrieved).

label: three-way origin of cfDNA variants
text: PITFALL: Treating any cfDNA variant absent from the tumour biopsy as CH overcounts CH: tumour heterogeneity and biopsy sampling also produce cfDNA-only variants. CHECK: split cfDNA variants three ways: also in the tumour sample of the same patient (tumour-matched); in the WBC (n_alt_count>0, WBC-matched); or in neither (VUSo/unknown). IF FOUND: attribute to CH only the WBC-supported variants, and report the unexplained category separately.

label: CH gene spectrum and age
text: PITFALL: CH variants concentrate in specific genes, and their presence in cfDNA scales with age. CHECK: tally WBC-supported cfDNA variants by gene (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, TP53, JAK2, CHEK2, ATM, SF3B1, SRSF2, GNAS, CBL, KMT2D), and correlate the per-patient count with AGE in data_clinical_patient.txt. IF FOUND: a gene spectrum dominated by DNMT3A/TET2/PPM1D plus a positive age association is the hallmark of CH, which supports CH as a cfDNA mutation source in general, including in people without cancer. SOURCE: Jaiswal NEJM 2014; Genovese NEJM 2014 (not retrieved).

label: therapy-related CH in driver genes
text: PITFALL: TP53, ATM, CHEK2 and PPM1D CH variants are enriched after chemotherapy or radiotherapy, and they are also cancer driver genes, so they are easily misassigned to the tumour. CHECK: for cfDNA TP53/PPM1D/ATM/CHEK2 calls, compare cfDNA VAF with WBC VAF and with tumour presence. Check TUMOR_TYPE for treatment status (untreated vs progressive). IF FOUND: count WBC-supported driver-gene variants as CH, and do not count them as tumour mutations. SOURCE: Coombs et al. Cell Stem Cell 2017; Bolton et al. Nat Genet 2020 (not retrieved).

label: low-VAF CH and WBC depth
text: PITFALL: Low-VAF CH (VAF<2%, below the classic CHIP threshold) dominates in ultra-deep cfDNA panels, and WBC depth may be lower than cfDNA depth, so WBC support can be missed. CHECK: look at the n_depth distribution and the cfDNA VAF (t_alt_count/t_depth). Look for variants at hotspot CH positions (e.g. DNMT3A R882, JAK2 V617F) with n_alt_count of 0 or 1 at low n_depth. IF FOUND: do not restrict to VAF>=2%. Report the CH fraction both with and without low-VAF variants, and treat weak WBC support (n_alt>=2 or significant by binomial test) as evidence of CH. SOURCE: general CH/cfDNA error-model practice (not retrieved).

label: check whether CH calls were filtered out
text: PITFALL: The patient-level mutation file may hold only cfDNA and tumour rows, with WBC-matched variants either filtered out upstream or kept with nonzero n_alt_count. If the CH calls were filtered out, the counts will understate CH. CHECK: count cfDNA rows with n_alt_count>0, and note whether any mutation rows carry a WBC barcode. IF FOUND (no WBC-positive rows): CH can't be quantified from the file. Fall back on the study design (matched WBC sequencing was done precisely to remove CH) and on established biology.

text: The hypothesis concerns transcriptional output (JAK-STAT, hypoxia, immune pathways), but the provided tables are only clinical, mutation (MAF) and MutSig files, with no RNA-seq or pathway scores. Under the task's label convention, a missing measurement alone does not make a hypothesis 'Not verifiable'; that label is reserved for hypotheses about a disease, cohort or data type the study does not cover. First check whether the cohort is ccRCC (ONCOTREE_CODE / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED) and whether PBRM1 is mutated and prominent in data_mutsig.txt, then decide which label category applies.

reason: No expression data exist, so the teams have to rely on established biology. They need the correct published direction and context, and they need to know the claim has no direction, so they do not guess or misread it.
text: Published biology on PBRM1 in ccRCC (from the library's prior knowledge; not retrieved online): Nargund et al. 2017 (Cell Reports) reported that PBRM1 loss amplifies HIF/hypoxia transcription. In RNA-seq of anti-PD-1 (nivolumab)-treated ccRCC, Miao et al. 2018 (Science) reported that PBRM1 loss-of-function tumours showed altered (largely reduced) IL6/JAK-STAT3 and immune-signalling gene expression, along with differences in hypoxia signatures. Check whether the clinical table describes a nivolumab-treated ccRCC cohort (e.g. drug fields, CA209 trial identifiers). The hypothesis says 'alters' and gives no direction, so judge it on whether a change happens, not on which way it goes.

reason: Treating every PBRM1 call as loss misclassifies tumours, and that would weaken any proxy comparison.
text: Define PBRM1 loss as truncating mutations only (nonsense, frameshift indels, canonical splice site, translation start). Exclude silent and splice-region synonymous calls, and treat missense calls only as a sensitivity analysis. Allele fraction relative to PURITY can indicate biallelic loss (chr3p LOH is almost universal in ccRCC).

reason: The task's grading treats a wrong Not verifiable as wrong. Teams need to decide scope correctly before they analyse.
text: Scope check before labelling: confirm in data_clinical_sample.txt that the cancer type is prostate and that data_mutations.txt supports per-gene sample frequencies. The library describes the data as a pooled prostate cancer exome (WXS) cohort of about 1000 primary and metastatic samples, with mutations, CNA and SV. If that is confirmed, a claim about the distribution of significantly mutated genes in prostate cancer concerns this study. Under the benchmark convention the label must then be True or False, decided by the analysis, and not Not verifiable.

reason: This defines the test of the hypothesis. Without an explicit definition, teams may reach arbitrary visual judgements.
text: Make 'long tail' operational and quantitative; do not judge it by eye. In the sense used for cancer genes (Lawrence et al. 2014, Nature), a long tail means a few genes mutated at high frequency and many significant genes each mutated in only about 1-3% of tumours, which are detectable only in large cohorts. Compute the fraction of samples with a nonsynonymous mutation in each gene and rank-order the genes. Report how many candidate driver/significant genes are above 5%, how many are at 1-5% and how many are below 3%. Optionally, compare the fit of an exponential decay with a heavy-tailed or power-law fit.

reason: The hypothesis is about significantly mutated genes, not the most frequently mutated genes. Passenger long genes would distort the shape of the distribution.
text: Raw mutation frequency is not significance. Long genes (TTN, MUC16, CSMD3, LRP1B, olfactory-receptor genes) and late-replicating, low-expression genes are mutated by chance, and they swamp a raw frequency ranking. Use only nonsynonymous coding variants (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site, In_Frame indels). Normalise by gene length and background rate, or use a MutSigCV-like binomial test against the per-sample mutation rate, to pick the significant genes before you examine their frequency distribution. As a sanity check, compare the top genes with known prostate drivers (SPOP, TP53, FOXA1, PTEN, AR, KMT2C/D, CTNNB1, PIK3CA, ATM, BRCA2, APC, CDK12, RB1, ZMYM3). Do not count TTN-type genes as SMGs.

reason: Without in-data comparison groups, teams may wrongly default to 'Not verifiable'.
text: The tables appear to hold only breast adenoid cystic carcinomas (about 12 samples), with no salivary AdCC or conventional TNBC samples to compare against directly. Confirm this by tabulating CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED / ONCOTREE_CODE in the clinical tables. Under the benchmark convention, 'Not verifiable' applies only when the hypothesis concerns a disease or cohort the tables do not cover. A hypothesis about this cohort's own tumours (breast AdCC) must be labelled True or False, even though the comparison groups are absent. Compare the in-data features of breast AdCC with established literature profiles of salivary AdCC and of TNBC, and say in the reasoning that literature supplied the comparison groups.

reason: These give the teams the external reference profiles and the feature set they need, because the data contain only one group.
text: Judge similarity on the defining genomic features, not on overlap of individual gene names. Literature reference profiles: salivary AdCC has very low TMB (about 0.3 mutations/Mb), MYB-NFIB or MYBL1 rearrangements, rare TP53 mutations, few copy-number alterations, and recurrent hits in chromatin remodellers (KDM6A, ARID1A, SMARCA2, CREBBP/EP300), NOTCH1/FBXW7 and the PI3K pathway. Conventional TNBC has TP53 mutations in about 80% of cases, high genomic instability with many CNAs, PIK3CA mutations and higher TMB. Per sample, compute nonsynonymous mutation count/TMB, TP53 mutation status, high-level CNA burden, MYB/MYBL1 rearrangement status and hits in chromatin/NOTCH/PI3K genes. Then judge which reference profile the cohort matches.

reason: Hypermutators can change which genes look recurrent and how the frequencies are distributed.
text: A few hypermutated samples (MMR-deficient/MSI or POLE, common in metastatic CRPC, with TMB above about 10-20/Mb) can dominate per-gene counts and inflate the apparent set of SMGs. Inspect the per-sample nonsynonymous mutation count or the TMB column, and flag samples above about 10 times the median. Count each gene per sample (mutated yes/no), not per mutation. Repeat the distribution analysis with hypermutators excluded to check that its shape is robust.

reason: Using smoking history as a stand-in for the mutational profile is the most likely way to reach the wrong conclusion.
text: The hypothesis concerns a mutational profile, not self-reported smoking. Compute per-sample SNV spectra from data_mutations.txt and judge how many tumours show a tobacco-like (SBS4-like: C>A-dominant, with transcriptional strand bias) profile. Use clinical smoking variables (TOBACCO_SMOKING_HISTORY_INDICATOR, pack-years) only as context. If the two disagree, base the label on the mutation data and say which evidence decided it. Note that in head and neck cancer SBS4 is reported to be much weaker than in lung cancer, even in heavy smokers (Alexandrov et al. 2016, Science).

reason: The operational definition of 'consistent with tobacco' decides the majority call, so fix it in advance and show both versions.
text: HNSCC exome spectra are often dominated by APOBEC (SBS2/SBS13: C>T and C>G at TCW) and clock-like (SBS1/SBS5) signatures. For each sample, report the fractions of the six substitution classes and classify it as tobacco-like (high C>A), APOBEC-like or clock-like. Before looking at results, decide whether 'consistent with tobacco' means dominant or merely detectable. Report both counts against a 50% threshold.

reason: Affects which method is feasible and how strongly the results can be stated.
text: data_mutations.txt has no trinucleotide-context column, so a full 96-channel SBS fit needs a reference genome (hg19), which may not be available offline. If it is not, use the pyrimidine-collapsed 6-class spectrum plus transcriptional strand (Strand/transcript strand columns). As the tobacco proxy, use C>A fraction with strand bias: tobacco adducts cause excess G>T on the non-transcribed strand. Do not claim exact SBS4 exposures.

reason: This is a confounder of any group comparison the teams run.
text: Tumour purity and necrosis (e.g. PRIMARY_PURITY, PRIMARY_NECROSIS, if present) can differ between metastatic and non-metastatic primaries and confound omics comparisons, because stromal content drives mesenchymal, metastasis-linked signal. Compare them between the groups (Wilcoxon) and adjust for purity if they differ.

reason: Low mutation counts and artifacts can inflate or deflate the tobacco call.
text: HNSCC exomes often carry only about 50-300 SNVs per sample, so per-sample signature fitting overfits. SBS4 can be confused with flat signatures (SBS5/SBS40) and with C>A artifacts or oxidative signatures (SBS18, SBS45). Count SNVs per sample across all variant classifications, flag samples with fewer than 50, and fit only a restricted signature set (SBS1, SBS2, SBS13, SBS4, SBS5, SBS18). Require a minimum exposure, for example at least 10-20% and at least 10 mutations. Check for low-VAF C>A excess as a sign of artifact, and report how robust the majority call is.

reason: Cohort composition can shift the majority; stratification makes the result interpretable without changing the target population.
text: HPV-positive HNSCC (mostly oropharynx) has lower smoking rates and is more APOBEC-driven. Tabulate the HPV columns (HPV_ISH/HPV_PCR/HPV_PATHSEQ) and TUMOR_TISSUE_SITE, and report the tobacco-profile fraction in the whole cohort and in the HPV-negative subset. The hypothesis is about HNSCC cases overall, so take the label from the whole cohort and use the stratification to explain it.
