text: In data_mutations.txt, cfDNA rows (Tumor_Sample_Barcode ending _cfdna) are paired with Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode ending _wbc. Sort each cfDNA variant into one of three groups: (a) also present in the same patient's tumour sample (tumour-matched); (b) supported in the WBC (n_alt_count>0, or WBC VAF from n_alt_count/n_depth comparable to the cfDNA VAF), i.e. CH-derived; (c) in neither (unexplained). Attribute only WBC-supported variants to CH, report group (c) separately, and give the fraction of cfDNA variants in each group.

reason: Upstream filtering could make CH look absent when it was only removed. That would mislead the conclusion.
text: Check whether WBC-supported variants were kept in the mutation file at all: count cfDNA rows with n_alt_count>0 and see whether any rows carry a WBC barcode. If WBC-positive variants were filtered out upstream, the file will understate CH. In that case, rely on the study design (matched WBC sequencing done to identify CH) and established biology rather than reading an absence of CH from the file.

reason: A VAF cut-off or a strict n_alt rule changes how much CH is detected.
text: CH in ultra-deep cfDNA panels is mostly low-VAF (<2%), and WBC depth may be lower than cfDNA depth, so WBC support can be missed. Look at the n_depth and cfDNA VAF (t_alt_count/t_depth) distributions and at CH hotspots (e.g. DNMT3A R882, JAK2 V617F) with n_alt_count 0–1 at low n_depth. Do not restrict to VAF>=2%. Report the CH fraction both with and without low-VAF calls, and treat n_alt>=2 or a significant binomial test as WBC support.

reason: Misassigning these driver-gene CH variants to the tumour would bias the CH estimate downward.
text: TP53, PPM1D, ATM and CHEK2 are both cancer drivers and common CH genes, and CH in them is enriched after chemo- or radiotherapy. For cfDNA calls in these genes, compare cfDNA VAF with WBC VAF and with presence in the tumour. Count WBC-supported calls as CH, not as tumour mutations. Check the treatment-status field (e.g. TUMOR_TYPE untreated vs progressive) where available.

reason: With no controls, the gene spectrum and age dependence are the closest in-data evidence for whether CH is a cancer-independent source of cfDNA variants.
text: Tally WBC-supported cfDNA variants by gene (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, TP53, JAK2, CHEK2, ATM, SF3B1, SRSF2, GNAS, CBL, KMT2D), and correlate the per-patient count with AGE from data_clinical_patient.txt. A canonical CH gene spectrum and an age association are the features that mark the variants as haematopoietic in origin rather than tumour- or cancer-specific. Use them when reasoning about whether the finding carries over to non-cancer individuals.

label: FINDING
text: FINDING: Without gene lengths/covariates, the best simple option is a dN/dS-style test: per gene, compare the nonsynonymous count to the synonymous count scaled by the cohort-wide nonsyn:syn ratio (binomial/Poisson test, or Fisher test of gene vs rest). The synonymous count acts as a proxy for gene length and local mutation rate. Known biases: per-gene synonymous counts are sparse, so it is noisy and has low power for small genes. Long, late-replicating, lowly expressed genes (TTN, MUC16, CSMD3, LRP1B, RYR2, USH2A, OR genes) still leak in when a single global rate is used, because their background rate is higher than average (Lawrence 2013). Naive frequency or a global-rate binomial greatly inflates false positives for these genes. dNdScv (Martincorena 2017) uses trinucleotide context plus a negative-binomial gene-rate model with synonymous counts and is reported to control false positives well. Practical fallback: require significance under both syn-scaling and a global-rate test, and exclude a blacklist of known long/FLAGS genes. Web gateway failed (HTTP 403), so not re-read; confidence medium. QUESTION: Simple background models without gene lengths for SMG false-positive control and long-gene biases. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.09.042 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12213 (not retrieved).

From domain knowledge, OncoKB gives fusion-based Level 1-3 assignments (ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK1-3, FGFR2/3 fusions and so on) only to fusions that have a partner gene, which in practice means in-frame, functional fusions. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Which COSMIC SBS signatures are classed as clock-like or aging-related, and which signatures usually dominate oesophageal and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma? ANSWER: Clock-like/aging: SBS1 (spontaneous deamination of 5-methylcytosine, C>T at CpG) and SBS5 (flat, unknown aetiology); both accumulate with age (Alexandrov et al. 2015). In oesophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma the hallmark, often dominant signature is SBS17a/b (T>G at CTT context, associated with gastric acid reflux/oxidative damage); SBS1 and SBS5 are present in nearly all tumours (and on panel data SBS1 C>T at CpG frequently ranks first), while Secrier et al. 2016 split EAC into SBS17-dominant (C>A/T>G), HRD/BRCA-like (SBS3) and APOBEC (SBS2/13) subgroups. So an 'aging-dominant' call for an EAC cohort is plausible but not the textbook characteristic; SBS17 is. CAVEAT: the research gateway returned HTTP 502/403 on every call, so no page was fetched; this answer is from prior knowledge and the web did not settle it. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/signatures/sbs/ (not fetched), https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3441 (not fetched), https://doi.org/10.1038/ng.3659 (not fetched).

QUESTION: When a VEP- or Oncotator-annotated MAF has no reference-context column, is estimating dinucleotide context from codon strings known to bias substitution-context frequencies, and what standard corrections exist? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB (gateway HTTP 403, no pages read). From background knowledge: yes, it gives a restricted and biased sample. Context is known only when the neighbour falls in the same codon, so codon-position-3 SNPs have no 3' neighbour and position-1 SNPs have no 5' neighbour. As a result, 5' and 3' flank tests use different SNP subsets, and codon-position and amino-acid composition distort which contexts appear. Standard corrections: (1) take the true flanking bases from the reference genome (hg19/hg38 FASTA via pyfaidx/BSgenome, or tools such as SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, MutationalPatterns or deconstructSigs, which do this automatically); (2) normalise context counts by exome trinucleotide opportunity (e.g. deconstructSigs tri.counts.method='exome2genome'); (3) compare the A>C/T>G context fraction with other substitution classes drawn from the same codon positions, so that both share the same bias. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How does dNdScv (or MutSigCV) define a significantly mutated gene, and what minimum cohort size and mutation counts are needed for it to have power in a small, highly UV-hypermutated whole-exome cohort? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 502 (Exa 403) on all 3 calls, so no page was read. From background knowledge: dNdScv calls a gene significant when its global dN/dS test has q<0.1 (qglobal_cv). That test compares missense and truncating mutations against synonymous ones, with a negative-binomial background adjusted for covariates. MutSigCV calls genes significant at q<=0.1 against a background that is specific to each patient, gene and sequence context. Neither tool sets a fixed minimum cohort size. Power is limited in small, very high-TMB UV cohorts of a few tens of tumours. Even so, TP53 usually still reaches significance in cSCC cohorts of about 30-40 tumours because of its strong excess of truncating and missense mutations; CDKN2A may not. Running dNdScv is feasible, but a non-significant result at this cohort size is not evidence against recurrence. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

QUESTION: In mutual-exclusivity analyses of cancer driver mutations, how should samples with no called mutations at all be handled: as wild-type, or excluded as possibly unprofiled? How does that choice affect a Fisher exact test of exclusivity? ANSWER: The web search failed (all 3 gateway calls returned HTTP 502 / Exa 403), so this answer comes from domain knowledge and no page was read. Convention (e.g. cBioPortal): a sample listed as profiled/sequenced (gene panel matrix, sequenced case list) but with no mutation records counts as wild-type. Exclude it only if there is evidence it was not profiled. Including such samples only adds to the double-negative cell. QUESTION: How is 'fraction of genome altered' or 'percent genome altered' conventionally computed from segmented copy-number data (log2 thresholds, segment-length weighting, sex chromosomes), and how do common portals derive the sample-level value? ANSWER: The web did not settle this: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on every call, so no pages were read. From general knowledge: cBioPortal-style FGA is the summed length of segments with |seg.mean| >= about 0.2 (log2 ratio), divided by the total length of all profiled segments. QUESTION: Is expression of DNA-methylation and Polycomb regulators (EZH2, DNMT1, UHRF1) an accepted proxy for global DNA-methylation differences between tumour subtypes, and how strongly do the two correlate in published work? ANSWER: The web did not settle this: every research call failed (Exa HTTP 403), so no page was read. From domain knowledge only: regulator expression is not an accepted quantitative proxy for global methylation. EZH2, DNMT1 and UHRF1 are E2F/proliferation-linked genes, so their expression largely tracks cell-cycle activity, and in my recollection correlations with global methylation are weak or inconsistent. Regulator expression can only be supportive context. The decisive evidence for the hypothesis is the established finding that NEPC has distinct, largely hypermethylated DNA-methylation profiles compared with CRPC-Adeno, together with EZH2 up-regulation. OncoKB Level 1 means FDA-recognised, Level 2 standard care, Level 3A clinical evidence in this tumour type, Level 3B evidence in another tumour type. Tumour-agnostic Level 1 calls include MSI-H, TMB-H (>=10 mut/Mb), and NTRK1/2/3 fusions. Endometrial-relevant Level 1-3 calls include ERBB2 amplification (trastuzumab in serous EC, Level 2), PIK3CA oncogenic mutations (3B), BRCA1/2 oncogenic mutations (3B for PARP inhibitors), KRAS G12C (3B), and possibly POLE. MSK cohort studies usually call a tumour 'clinically actionable' if it carries at least one OncoKB Level 1-3 (sometimes 1-3B) alteration. Composite actionability can stay similar across races even when MSI-H/TMB-H is lower in Black patients, because ERBB2 amplification in serous EC offsets the drop. QUESTION: Which alterations count as OncoKB Level 1-3 actionable in endometrial cancer, and how is 'clinically actionable' defined in cohort studies? question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How do background-adjusted driver-gene tests (MutSigCV, dNdScv, OncodriveCLUST) combine gene length, per-sample mutation rate and positional clustering? What minimum number of recurrent identical missense hits in a cohort of several hundred exomes is generally treated as significant? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on every call (3 used), so no page was read. From prior knowledge: MutSigCV models a gene-specific background from per-patient mutation rate, gene coding territory (length and sequence context), local synonymous/noncoding rate and covariates (expression, replication timing, chromatin state), then tests for an excess of nonsilent mutations. MutSig2CV adds clustering (CL) and conservation (FN) components. dNdScv estimates the expected synonymous rate per gene with trinucleotide context, gene length and a negative-binomial regression on covariates, then tests for an excess of missense and truncating mutations (dN/dS > 1). OncodriveCLUST ignores mutation rate and scores how tightly missense mutations cluster by position, against a background built from how synonymous mutations cluster. No universal hit threshold exists, because significance depends on gene length and the background rate. At CLL-like rates (~0.5-1 coding mutation/Mb) in several hundred exomes, the expected count at any one codon is far below 0.01. So 3 or more identical missense hits in unrelated patients is conventionally a significant hotspot (for example under binomial hotspot methods such as Chang et al. 2016 at q<0.01). This means recurrent hotspot or tightly clustered hits in a small gene (RPS15 C-terminus, IKZF3 L162R) are adequate informal evidence of driver involvement. HOW SURE: medium (prior knowledge only; not web-verified). SOURCES: none given.

HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

QUESTION: In studies of mutational signatures and immune checkpoint blockade response, is a signature-response association usually reported as a marginal association, or does it count only when it is independent of tumor mutational burden? Is TMB usually treated as a confounder or as a mediator of signature exposure? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: every call to the research gateway returned HTTP 502 / Exa 403, so no page was read. From background knowledge: genomic ICB cohort papers usually report signature-response links as marginal (univariate) associations, sometimes with a secondary check of whether they hold after TMB adjustment. Signatures produce mutations, so TMB is generally treated as lying on the causal path (a mediator), not a confounder. Under that convention the marginal association is the test of the claim, and the adjusted result shows whether the effect works only through TMB. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Without an MSI status column, what are the accepted ways to identify microsatellite-unstable or POLE-hypermutated tumors from whole-exome mutation calls alone (e.g., indel fraction, MMR signature fractions, TMB thresholds)? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED (gateway down). From background knowledge: MSI-H/MMRd tumors are marked by a high indel count and fraction (especially 1-bp homopolymer indels), high MMR signature fractions (SBS6/14/15/20/21/26/44; ID1/ID2), high TMB (often >=10-20 mut/Mb) and MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 alterations. POLE-hypermutated tumors are marked by exonuclease-domain hotspots (P286R, V411L, S297F, A456P, S459F), SBS10a/b, ultra-high TMB (>100 mut/Mb) and a low indel fraction. Read-based callers (MSIsensor, MANTIS, mSINGS) need BAMs. Cutoffs vary from study to study; the usual practice is to flag extreme outliers and run the analysis with and without them. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In immunotherapy cohorts, how do 'clinical benefit' definitions (e.g., RECIST CR/PR/SD of at least 6 months versus durable clinical benefit or mixed-response categories) usually differ, and which is the standard endpoint for association tests of genomic features? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED (gateway down). From background knowledge: Rizvi 2015 and Snyder 2014 define durable clinical benefit as CR/PR or SD lasting >6 months, against no durable benefit (PD within 6 months). Van Allen 2015 defined clinical benefit as CR/PR or SD with OS >1 year, with a separate intermediate/mixed category. Objective response (CR/PR vs SD/PD) is stricter and puts long-term SD with non-responders. For association tests of genomic features, the usual primary endpoint is binary clinical benefit vs no benefit with intermediate cases excluded; ORR and PFS/OS are used as sensitivity endpoints. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: Yes (from field knowledge, web NOT retrieved; gateway returned HTTP 403 on all 4 calls). Studies that sequenced plasma cfDNA alongside matched WBC DNA found CH-derived variants in the cfDNA of non-cancer controls, and found them often: most cfDNA variants in healthy/non-cancer controls matched WBC and sat in CH genes (DNMT3A, TET2, PPM1D, ASXL1, TP53), with frequency rising with age. Healthy controls in matched cfDNA-WBC studies such as Hu et al. Clin Cancer Res 2018 and the large deep-sequencing cfDNA screening cohorts showed this. So the established biology contradicts the claim that CH is not a source of cfDNA mutations in controls. ANSWER: Non-CR/Non-PD is the RECIST 1.1 overall response for patients with only non-target (non-measurable) disease when that disease persists, or tumour markers stay above normal, without clear progression. QUESTION: In whole-genome sequencing studies of lung adenocarcinoma in never smokers, how are copy-number-based subtypes usually related to tumour mutational burden and to histology (e.g. carcinoids)? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY THE WEB: the research gateway refused all 3 calls (HTTP 502 / Exa 403), so no page was read. From background knowledge only: copy-number-quiet tumours usually also carry fewer point mutations. SCNA burden tends to rise with TMB, TP53 mutation and genomic instability. So a quiet copy-number subtype would be expected to have LOWER TMB, not higher. Carcinoids are a separate histology with low TMB and few copy-number changes. They are usually excluded or analysed on their own, because they would pile into a quiet cluster and pull its TMB down. Teams should run the comparison with and without carcinoids. HOW SURE: low. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In published hepatocellular carcinoma genomic studies, what is the reported relationship between focal FGF19/CCND1 (11q13.3) amplification and CTNNB1 or AXIN1 mutation: co-occurrence, mutual exclusivity, or no association? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY WEB: every research call failed with Exa HTTP 403. From recollection only: focal FGF19/CCND1 amplification (about 5-6% of HCC; Sawey 2011, Schulze 2015, TCGA LIHC 2017) is linked to the proliferative, TP53-associated subclass. CTNNB1 and AXIN1 mutations mark other classes: CTNNB1 the non-proliferative class, while AXIN1 falls in the proliferative class but without beta-catenin activation. I recall no published report that FGF19 amplification is significantly enriched in CTNNB1/AXIN1-mutant tumours. My lean is no association or a tendency to exclusivity, which would make the hypothesis the reversed form of a reported finding. Do not treat this as established. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (study finding): The cohort (40 DLBCL WGS tumours with matched normals plus 13 cell lines) is the source study; I assume it reported, from mutation allele frequencies, evidence of subclonal mutation populations in many tumours, i.e. heterogeneity described as common. The tables cannot confirm whether the paper said 'common' or 'a subset'; a reversal to 'rare' would contradict established DLBCL biology (subclonal mutations in most tumours by CCF analysis). Keeps True; confidence lowered slightly.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (Mutation_Status): somatic=757 calls, all in tumours; valid=256, all in cell lines; known_somatic=1 (RG040); blank=8832 (2666 tumour, 6166 cell line). The flag marks the subset of calls confirmed/validated per sample type (enriched for missense/nonsense driver genes). There are no read counts in any subset, so restricting to it changes no check; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (Mutation_Status, SVs): Mutation_Status is blank on 8832 of 9846 rows; 757 are 'somatic', 256 'valid' and 1 'known_somatic'. Annotated rows per sample range from 0 to 62. t_ref/t_alt counts and Validation_Status are empty. data_sv.txt has 56 fusions in 29 samples, all RNA-only (DNA_Support=No). Neither has allele-fraction or clonality information, so the method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (cellularity sign): Of 39 tumours with both values, 11 differ by >15 points, but 9 have AF-based cellularity ABOVE pathology and only 2 (RG008 -23, RG075 -23) below; 12/39 below at all, median diff +7.5. The direction subclonality could produce is rare, so the proxy gives no support for heterogeneity and I no longer cite it as supporting evidence. Label still rests on established DLBCL biology and the source-study finding; True kept.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (signed cellularity difference): Of the 40 primary tumours, 39 have both cellularity values. AF-cellularity minus pathology cellularity has a median of +7.5. Only 2 of 39 tumours are below pathology by more than 15 points (-23.3, -22.6); 9 are above by more than 15. The earlier '11/39 discordant' overcounted, because only the 'below' direction could reflect subclonality. The proxy gives essentially no support for heterogeneity and is dropped as evidence. The label still rests on study identity and established biology.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (reading of 'common'): The reading is 'many or most tumours carry subclonal mutation populations', which is intratumoral. The earlier reasoning did not use between-patient variation in burden or genes as support. The only data-based support was the cellularity proxy, which the Q2 check refutes. The tables contain no direct intratumoral evidence: read counts are empty. The label True rests on this being the study's DLBCL WGS cohort and on the published and established finding that subclonal mutations are frequent in DLBCL.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (codings): I had not fitted the four-level PRED_CATEGORY. In IHC (n=527, 331 deaths), the four-level classifier adjusted for FGFR2+IDH1 is strongly prognostic (LRT 3 df p=0.0003; p=2e-5 when also stratified by curative surgery). Strict Biliary class (n=122, 88 events, median OS 13.6 mo) is worst; other levels have adjusted HR 0.56-0.77. Biliary class vs the rest: adjusted HR 0.58 (0.46-0.75), p=2e-5. The omnibus four-level test uses the classifier's own output with no grouping choice, so my HCC-like vs biliary-like collapse hid the signal. Changes method: yes, revised to True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (FGFR2/IDH1 wild-type subgroup): in IHC with neither FGFR2 nor IDH1 altered (n=318, 211 deaths), the four-level classifier still separates OS (log-rank p=0.0018), and non-Biliary-class vs Biliary class HR is 0.57 (0.42-0.77), p=0.0002. This supports independence from FGFR2/IDH1. The HCC-like collapse is null (HR 0.91), so it was the wrong coding.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on library findings: REMARK-style advice favours a prespecified coding. The four-level variable is the classifier's native output, and its adjusted omnibus test (p=0.0003) involves no post-hoc grouping. That result is robust to age, to surgery stratification and to the wild-type subgroup, so the conclusion does not rest on picking a coding.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (survival columns): patient OS_MONTHS equals sample OS_MONTHS_DIAGNOSIS_TO_FU exactly for all 100 patients that have both (so OS is from diagnosis). CRDB_SURVIVAL_STATUS disagrees with OS_STATUS: 6 patients are CRDB Alive but OS_STATUS deceased, and 0 the reverse, so CRDB is an older snapshot and pairing it with the latest follow-up time is inconsistent. Patients without OS_STATUS have no consistent status, so a larger consistent n is not available. The inconsistent CRDB pair (n=68 stage IV) gave SMAD4 HR 1.56 and STK11 HR 1.96, both above 1 but not significant. No method change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (STK11 leave-one-out): STK11 is altered in 13 stage IV patients, 10 of them with OS; all stage IV, 9 adenocarcinoma and 1 mixed adeno-neuroendocrine; 9 mutations and 1 deep deletion; 7 events, mostly deaths within 1-9 months. In leave-one-out Cox the STK11 HR ranges from 2.09 to 3.33 and p from 0.009 to 0.13; dropping any early-death patient makes p>0.05. SMAD4 HR is stable at 2.08-2.24 (p<=0.013). STK11 direction is robust but its significance is fragile. No method change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (histology): in the stage IV OS cohort, 85 of 99 are adenocarcinoma. Restricted to adenocarcinoma: SMAD4 HR 2.05 (1.07-3.93, p=0.03), STK11 HR 3.75 (1.51-9.33, p=0.004). Adjusted for adenocarcinoma vs other: SMAD4 HR 2.09 (p=0.012), STK11 HR 2.21 (p=0.083). Both effects persist; no method change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (other drivers): STK11 co-occurs with KRAS in only 1 of 10 patients. Adjusted for TP53, KRAS, ERBB2 and CDKN2A: SMAD4 HR 2.13 (p=0.013), STK11 HR 2.15 (p=0.09). Adding log TMB and purity: SMAD4 HR 2.34 (p=0.007), STK11 HR 2.33 (p=0.064). Drivers plus TMB with delayed entry: SMAD4 HR 2.30 (p=0.007), STK11 HR 1.79 (p=0.21). SMAD4 is independent and robust; STK11 HR stays around 1.8-2.3 but is underpowered. No evidence contradicts the claim; label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY library findings: on delayed entry, only 2 of 10 STK11-altered OS patients were sequenced after diagnosis (3.4 and 13.8 months), and the delayed-entry STK11 HR of 1.79-1.87 is still above 1. On the events-per-variable rule, STK11 has 7 events among carriers, so it is underpowered; under the library's own note a non-significant result does not show there is no effect. The study's cancer type and genes match, so the label is True or False; the direction supports the claim, so True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to PH/adjustment/coding question: In IHC (n=527, 331 deaths) Biliary class vs rest satisfies PH (Schoenfeld rank test p=0.13) and survives adjustment: HR 1.95 (1.52-2.49) with age and strata by curative surgery, HR 1.88 (1.44-2.47) with age, surgery, metastasis, differentiation and FGFR2/IDH1 (n=476). The coding choice is justified without p-values by using the classifier's own 4-category output (PRED_CATEGORY) as primary: its 3-df likelihood-ratio test adjusted for FGFR2/IDH1 gives p=3.4e-4, and with clinical covariates p=2.0e-4. HCC-like vs biliary-like collapse (HR 0.96) and continuous score (HR 1.45, p=0.11) are null or weak because the signal sits only in the highest-score Biliary class (top score quartile has median OS 13.6 vs 17-20 mo). Does not change the label (True).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to broader driver question: With FGFR2 = fusion+nonsilent mutation+amplification (n=89) and IDH1 = any nonsilent mutation (n=128), the classifier is associated with drivers (FGFR2 alt 7% in Biliary class vs 37% in HCC class; IDH1 28% vs 3%), but Biliary class vs rest stays prognostic: adjusted HR 1.71 (1.34-2.19, p<1e-4); FGFR2 HR 0.85 and IDH1 HR 0.84 not significant. Does not change the method or label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to library findings: Collapsing to HCC-like vs biliary-like gives HR 0.96-0.99 (null) and continuous BILIARY_SCORE HR 1.35-1.45 (p 0.11-0.17), so significance depends on coding. But the prespecified full 4-category classifier output is significant independent of FGFR2/IDH1 (3-df LRT p=3.4e-4; p=2e-4 with age, surgery, metastasis, grade), so the evidence is not just from a cherry-picked cutpoint. Label kept True, confidence moderate.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (CNA-missing samples, FGFR3 fusions): The premise does not hold in this data. data_cna.txt and data_cna_hg19.seg both hold the same 105 samples, so no sample is missing CNA. All 4 FGFR3 fusions (3 FGFR3-TACC3 in P-0005966 HGT1, P-0001453 HGT1 and P-0003677 LGTa, plus FGFR3-TNIP2 in P-0006429 HGT1) have no ERBB2 mutation and no ERBB2 amplification. A segment scan with seg.mean>0.5 at both loci flags only P-0002166 (HGT1, FGFR3 missense). Its ERBB2 change is a broad 17q arm gain (seg 0.51 over 29-80Mb) with discrete CNA 0, which is not an amplification. No co-altered high-grade sample is added, and the method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (hotspot-only and all-variant versions): The Hotspot column in data_mutations.txt is 0 for all 1609 calls, so a hotspot-only version reduces to amplifications plus SVs: high-grade has 0 both, 2 ERBB2-only, 4 FGFR3-only and 76 neither (uninformative). The all-variant version, including silent and UTR calls, gives high-grade 0 both, 20 ERBB2-only, 33 FGFR3-only and 29 neither (p<0.001), the same as the non-silent default. The overlap stays at zero and the method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (scope): For HG Ta/T1 TURBT only, the counts are 0 both, 14 ERBB2-only, 29 FGFR3-only and 22 neither (p=0.0001). For high-grade with CONCOMITANT_CIS=1 (n=39), they are 0 both, 13 ERBB2-only, 6 FGFR3-only and 20 neither (two-sided p=0.08). For the whole cohort of 105, they are 0 both, 21 ERBB2-only and 52 FGFR3-only. Zero overlap holds in every scope, so the scope definition does not change the method or the label False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on library findings: The CNA convention finding has no effect, because all 105 samples are CNA-profiled and amplification is CNA=2. On 'mutually exclusive': the data are exclusive both literally (0 co-altered of 82 high-grade) and statistically (Fisher p<0.001), so the 'not mutually exclusive' hypothesis is contradicted either way. The label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to Q1 (all ERBB2/FGFR3 variants with VAF in high-grade samples): all 57 ERBB2/FGFR3 mutation records in the 82 HG samples are missense; the Hotspot column is 0 for every row, so it carries no information. No HG sample has a variant in both genes at any VAF, including low-VAF calls such as ERBB2 S310F at 3-6% and FGFR3 S249C at 3%. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to Q2 (2x2 tables): (i) HG Ta/T1 TURBT only, n=65: both=0, ERBB2-only=14, FGFR3-only=29, neither=22, expected both 6.25, Fisher p=1e-4. (ii) HG ERBB2 mutation vs FGFR3 mutation, n=82: both=0 vs 6.4 expected, p=1.5e-4. (iii) ERBB2 amplification vs any FGFR3 alteration, n=82: both=0, 2 vs 33, expected 0.8, p=0.51. Overlap is zero under every definition. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (status columns): OS_MONTHS equals sample OS_MONTHS_DIAGNOSIS_TO_FU exactly for all 100 patients with OS_STATUS, so OS_STATUS+OS_MONTHS is one consistent time/status pair. CRDB_SURVIVAL_STATUS disagrees in 6 of 40 overlapping patients (OS_STATUS deceased, CRDB alive), so CRDB is stale. With only the consistent pair (n=100, 65 events, which includes all 97 metastatic-sample patients), the Cox model with SMAD4+STK11 gives SMAD4 HR 2.13 p=0.009 and STK11 HR 2.49 p=0.04. The metastatic subgroup is unchanged (2.12/2.35). This strengthens, and does not change, the label True; the primary analysis now uses only OS_STATUS.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to Q3 and library CNA finding: no samples are missing from data_cna.txt. It has all 105 samples, including 6 s_DS_nmibc_* samples that my earlier script wrongly dropped by keeping only columns starting with P-. Corrected calls: ERBB2 amp in P-0003681 and P-0003832; FGFR3 amp in P-0003823 and s_DS_nmibc_008_P (seg log2 1.20). None of these samples carries an alteration in the other gene. Segment data show only low-level ERBB2 gains (log2 0.5-0.9, discrete 0) in a few FGFR3-mutant samples, e.g. s_DS_nmibc_011 and P-0006124 (FGFR3 G803S, not a hotspot); these are not amplifications. Corrected HG any-alteration table: both=0, ERBB2 20, FGFR3 33, expected 8.05, p=8e-6. Label False unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (full-cohort adjusted Cox): adjusting for stage at collection, sample type and CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED (penalizer 0.01) with the consistent OS_STATUS pair (n=100) gives SMAD4 HR 2.12 p=0.015 and STK11 HR 5.35 (unstable, sparse histology). Adjusting for stage and sample type only gives SMAD4 2.16 p=0.009 and STK11 2.44 p=0.046. With the mixed CRDB status (n=151) the HRs are 1.41 and 1.98, ns. The direction is always HR>1. The 100-patient OS_STATUS cohort is effectively the metastatic cohort, so the cohort definition stays the same.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to library finding on 'mutually exclusive' usage: whether the term is read literally or statistically, the data meet both readings. There are 0 co-altered samples, against about 8 expected, with Fisher p<1e-5. So the hypothesis 'not mutually exclusive' is contradicted, and the label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (SV / mutation-only): data_sv.txt has 2 SMAD4 intragenic SVs and no STK11 SVs. Adding them reclassifies one patient (SMAD4 altered 59 to 60) and gives metastatic-subgroup SMAD4 HR 2.21 p=0.006 and STK11 2.25 p=0.067. Counting mutations only, with no deep deletions, weakens the result (SMAD4 1.44 p=0.30, STK11 1.82 p=0.21), but the direction stays the same. Deep deletion of a tumour suppressor is a real loss-of-function event, so the alteration definition is kept; the method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (left truncation): in the metastatic subgroup, a delayed-entry Cox (entry=OS_MONTHS_DIAG_TO_COLL) gives SMAD4 HR 1.81 p=0.045 and STK11 HR 1.80 p=0.19. OS from collection gives 1.92 p=0.026 and 1.77 p=0.195. In the 100-patient OS_STATUS cohort: SMAD4 1.82 p=0.039, STK11 1.95 p=0.14. Correcting shrinks the HRs, and STK11 loses significance (only 10 carriers and 6 events), but both stay at HR about 1.8. This weakens the evidence for STK11 but does not reverse it. The label stays True, with lower confidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (PAIRED_STATUS): The groups are roughly balanced. Blood reference is 61/70 metastatic vs 67/76 non-metastatic; remote normal is 9 vs 9. In the blood-referenced subset (60 vs 66 with mutations) TMB has MWU p=0.072, SMAD4 is 12 vs 5 with Fisher p=0.066, and APC, TP53 and KRAS are null. The weak mutation signal shrinks further, but the label never rested on it, so the method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (metastasis definition): METASTATIC_STATUS means synchronous metastasis at surgery. DISTANT_LM=Yes occurs only in metastatic cases (43/70) and never in non-metastatic ones. 14/76 non-metastatic patients progressed later, so they are metachronous cases. The study's comparison and the hypothesis are about synchronous status. A metachronous reading would still be about this cohort's metastasis question and would not change True/False vs Not verifiable. The label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (SMAD4): SMAD4 does not survive BH-FDR across 735 genes mutated in at least 8 samples. All samples: 14/67 vs 5/75, p=0.015, q=0.28. Excluding pre-treated samples: p=0.034, q=0.35. No gene has q<0.19. Mutations do not robustly separate metastatic from non-metastatic primaries. That is consistent with the study's premise that proteomics, not genomics, separates them. The label rested on the study context (a CRC synchronous liver-metastasis proteogenomic cohort; no proteomic tables deposited) and on the reversed-finding convention, not on SMAD4. Label stays False; I removed the SMAD4 support claim from the reasoning.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY library finding (proteomics distinguishes metastatic CRC primaries): The data cannot check this, because no proteomic or phosphoproteomic tables are deposited. It agrees with the study design (70 synchronous-metastatic vs 76 non-metastatic primaries, profiled proteogenomically). It is low-confidence prior knowledge and does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (variant classes/hotspots): 177 non-silent of 254 mutations; Hotspot column is 0 for all 254. Chromatin/NOTCH hits: KMT2D frameshift (AdCC9T), KMT2C and NOTCH1 are Silent (should not have been counted), FBXW7 D642G and SF3B1 R625H missense, MYB missense x2; no PI3K-pathway or TP53 mutations at all. Restricting to functional mutations removes NOTCH1/KMT2C support but leaves a quiet, TP53/PIK3CA-free genome that still matches salivary AdCC, not TNBC. Label unchanged (True).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (CNA): MYB_NFIB_CNA field holds arm-level CNA text. 17q gain in 3/12 (AdCC4T, AdCC10T, AdCC11T), 17p loss in 2/12 (AdCC4T, AdCC10T; TP53 deep-loss call only there, ERBB2 gain too); 12q12-q14.1 loss (AdCC-associated) in 5/12; 9q loss in AdCC5T; 3 samples have no CNA. Fraction of CNA-table genes altered: 0-0.72, but table only holds 1849 genes in altered regions, so genome-wide burden is low in 9/12. A TNBC-like 17q/17p subset of 2-3 samples exists but no TP53 mutation accompanies it; does not change method or label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (intervals): references (unsourced background, low certainty): salivary AdCC ~0.3 nonsyn mut/Mb, TP53 <=5%, few CNAs; TNBC ~1-2+ mut/Mb, TP53 ~80%, extensive CNAs. Observed TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS mean 0.48 (95% t-CI 0.36-0.60, range 0.20-0.77), all 12 below 1/Mb. TP53 0/12 mutated, Clopper-Pearson 95% CI 0-26.5%, excludes 80% TNBC. Conclusion holds with 12 samples. Label True kept.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (fusion reconciliation): the premise is partly wrong: data_sv.txt DOES have an AdCC32T row (last line, no trailing newline), so SV rows = 10 samples (all except AdCC11T, AdCC12T), matching MYB_MYBL1_FUSION column. AdCC5T is FISH-negative but SV row says DNA+RNA support (WGS/RT-PCR); FISH-positive count is 9/12. MYB-NFIB frequency 9-10/12 (95% CI ~0.52-0.98) either way, typical of salivary AdCC and absent in TNBC. Weight unchanged; FUSION_STATUS column says YES for all 12 and is uninformative.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (mini PDX): Including the 3 'Metastatic, mini PDX done' untreated samples (metastatic n=45 vs non-metastatic n=73, PRETHERAPY=No) leaves purity (median 80 vs 80, Wilcoxon p=0.59), necrosis (10 vs 10, p=0.73) and TMB (3.27 vs 4.4, p=0.13) unchanged in conclusion; does not change method or label (False).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (progression): Of 73 untreated Non-Metastatic CCRC patients, 14 later progressed; 3 to liver, about 7 to distant sites (liver 3, lung 2, lung+bone 1, widespread 1), plus 3 'progression' rows that are other primary cancers. Group definition stays synchronous metastasis (METASTATIC_STATUS = TNM M); the few metachronous cases would dilute, not create, a difference, so the label (False) is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (metastasis tissue): METASTATIC_PURITY/NECROSIS are non-missing in 28 samples, all in metastatic groups (19 with DISTANT_LM=Yes), none in non-metastatic; so the study also profiled matched liver-metastasis tissue for a subset. The study compared primaries with vs without metastasis (and primaries vs matched metastases); this supports, not weakens, the reconstruction that it reported metastasis-associated proteomic/phospho differences. Label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (denominator): panel matrix and clinical sample table both list 97 samples (no mismatch); 64 samples have >=1 mutation call (63 non-silent) and 33 have none; expression z-scores cover only 58 of the 97. label: REPLY

text: REPLY Q(mutation-only fraction): Using C>A fraction alone with criteria fixed in advance against the 9 never-tobacco tumours, 63/74 (85%) exceed the never-smoker median (0.080), 56/74 (76%) exceed the never-smoker upper quartile (0.099), 39/74 (53%) have C>A>=0.15, and 31/74 (42%) exceed the never-smoker maximum (0.172). label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q(subsets/strand): The tobacco-like fraction (C>A above the never-smoker Q3) is 100% in larynx, 75% in hypopharynx, 74% in oral cavity and 45% in oropharynx; 83% in HPV-negative vs 43% in HPV-positive; and 4/4 recurrences. The signal is broad across HPV-negative sites, not driven by the 4 recurrences. Transcriptional strand bias: C>A with G on the coding (untranscribed) strand outnumbers C on the coding strand 1003 vs 740 (binomial p~3e-10), while the C>T control is near even (2107 vs 1971). That is the tobacco-adduct signature, so it supports True.

text: REPLY Q(synonymous/DNP): Synonymous-only C>A is lower (pooled 14% vs 20% nonsynonymous; median 22 silent SNVs/sample), still higher in ever- vs never-tobacco (median 0.11 vs 0.07, MWU p=0.10, underpowered with n=9 never), and 59% of tumours exceed the never-smoker synonymous Q3. label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q2 (denominator pitfalls): Samples 587236 and 587326 have no mutation rows and TMB NA, so they were never in the APC denominator (72 sequenced). label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q3 (APC recounts): APC non-silent 29/72 (40%); truncating-only (nonsense/frameshift) 27/72 (38%); VALIDATED non-silent calls only 20/72 (28%); by MSI: MSI 7/15 non-silent (5/15 truncating), MSS 22/57 (22/57 truncating). text: REPLY Q1 (matched denominators): of 97 panel samples only 58 have expression z-scores. In those 58, druggable-gene non-silent mutations (PI3K/AKT/mTOR + RTK/RAS/RAF + CDKN2A) hit 25/58 = 43% [Wilson 31-56%], versus 15/39 = 38% in the 39 without expression, so the subsets are similar. The diploid-reference |z|>2 CNA proxy adds 13 samples, giving 38/58 = 66% [53-76%]. The earlier 55% mixed a proxy that was only possible in 58 samples with a 97-sample denominator, so the method changes to matched denominators. The label does not change: 61% lies inside the matched CI.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (proxy validation): for ERBB2, CCND1, MDM2, EGFR, CDKN2A, E2F3 and PTEN, diploid-reference and all-samples z-scores correlate at r>=0.997, and most samples flagged at |z|>2 are flagged in both (e.g. MDM2 4/4, EGFR 4 vs 5, ERBB2 2 vs 4). The fraction on the 58 samples is threshold-sensitive: with the diploid reference, union = 78/66/62/55% at |z| 1.5/2/2.5/3; with the all-samples reference, 66/64/48/47%. The proxy is rough, but at the moderate thresholds (2-2.5) both files give about 48-66% and the CIs include 61%. The label still holds as True; the proxy brackets the claim rather than proving it.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (hotspot-level): counting only known activating hotspots (FGFR3 S249C/R248C/G370C/S371C/Y373C, PIK3CA E542K/E545K/Q546P/H1047R, AKT1 E17K, KRAS G12, BRAF V600E/K601E) plus truncating TSC1/PTEN drops the mutation-only count from 40/97 (41%) to 34/97 (35%). label: REPLY

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (379 samples with no mutation rows): they were kept in the denominator. 143 of them have SV calls and 111 have nonzero CNA. label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (breakdown): of 10,194 samples, 28.4% have an actionable mutation, 9.1% EGFR, 3.4% fusions with a partner and 8.3% amplifications (4.5% ERBB2/MET only). label: REPLY

As a result TMB>=10 flagged only 12 samples. Recomputing TMB over a 1.5 Mb panel raises the overall rate to 41.7%, so the original figure was conservative. By sample type the rates are 40.0% metastatic, 36.6% primary and 31.8% recurrent. Treatment-naive patients (n=7695) are at 37.1%. text: REPLY Q1 (denominator/purity): 1013 samples in clinical table, 1012 in mutations (TCGA-CH-5743 has no mutation rows); 995 after removing 18 hypermutators. label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (passenger check): TTN/CSMD3/LRP1B have syn-scaled ns/s ratios of 1.4-1.9. Keeping only significant genes with ns/s ratio>=5 or truncating fraction>=0.3 leaves 19 genes: 5 above 5% (TP53, SPOP, FOXA1, KMT2D, KMT2C) and 14 at 1-5% (PTEN, ATM, CDK12, APC, CTNNB1, KDM6A, BRCA2, ZMYM3, USP28, CHD6, etc.), 11 of them below 3%. Several marginal tail genes (DNAH9/11, PCDH17, KRTAP13-3) look like passengers, but the long-tail shape holds among the strict set. The method does not change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (data source): about 10 marginal tail genes (DNAH11, CACNA1H, KRTAP13-3, UNC13A, MYEOV, HCN4, etc.) come >60% from PCF_SU2C metastatic samples, which are 28% of the cohort. With leave-one-source-out, the significant-gene counts are 13-44, and every run has 3-5 genes above 5% and most genes at 1-5%. Dropping source-dominated genes does not change the head/tail shape or the label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (subsampling): with hypermutators and TTN/CSMD3/LRP1B excluded, the mean number of significant genes at 25/50/75/100% of the 995 samples is 2.8/13/22.4/46. It rises roughly linearly and does not saturate, which matches the Lawrence 2014 long-tail inference that larger cohorts find more low-frequency SMGs. This supports the label True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the literature-list question: a data-driven caller found 42 genes after removing 18 hypermutators (N=995). It selects genes with truncating enrichment against missense+silent (BH q<0.05) or a missense hotspot in at least 4 samples. Their frequencies show a long tail: TP53 18% is the only gene above 10%, 8 genes are at 3-10% and 33 are under 3%. A stricter syn-scaled dN/dS-style binomial test is underpowered and called only 5 genes (TP53, SPOP, FOXA1, KMT2D, PTEN at 18-4%). This does not change the method or the True label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the strata question: across the 42 data-called SMGs, the few-frequent/many-rare pattern holds in every stratum. Primary (674): 2 genes above 10%, 35 under 3%. Metastasis (321): 2 above 10%, 26 under 3%. TCGA: 2 above 10%, 35 under 3%. PCF_SU2C: 3 above 10%, 26 under 3%. AAPC, Broad/Cornell and Nelson: 0-2 above 10%. NEPC (n=26) is the most top-heavy, with 6 genes above 10%. Pooling does not create the pattern. TP53 is much higher in metastases (33% vs 11%).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the denominator question: the clinical table has 1013 samples and 1012 of them have mutation calls. 1011 was a wording slip for the non-silent-mutated set. After removing 18 hypermutators, N=995. Restricting to purity >=0.2, >=0.3 or >=0.4 (971/789/631 samples) or to tumour coverage at or above the median raises tail-gene frequencies only slightly. Even at purity >=0.4, 28 of the 42 genes stay under 3%. The method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the curve-fit question: on the pooled rank-frequency curve of the 42 data-called SMGs, a power-law (log-log) fit beats an exponential (semi-log) fit, R2 0.977 vs 0.892 and SSE 0.59 vs 2.73. This agrees with the long-tail judgement. On the 5-gene strict set the discrete MLE could not separate the two forms. Within single strata the comparison is mixed because of small n. The pooled result does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to the library findings: the operational definition of a long tail (a few genes at high frequency and many significant genes at 2-20% or lower) is met by data-called genes. Truncating and hotspot recurrence select real drivers (CDK12, APC, KDM6A, BRCA2, RB1, IDH1, AKT1) along with a few likely false positives (ZNF and KRTAP genes). Those false positives also sit in the tail, so excluding them would not change the shape.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (fusions/treatment/sample type): My code already skipped Intragenic SV rows. 42 samples carried Intergenic (no-partner) calls in ALK/ROS1/RET/NTRK/FGFR2, against 325 with true partnered fusions. Dropping the partnerless-only samples moves L1-3 from 35.9% to 35.5%. Treatment-naive samples (n=7695) are 35.9% L1-3 actionable, chemo-only 27.7%, prior targeted therapy about 50%. By sample type: primary 35.1%, metastasis 39.0%, recurrent 27.7%. None of these changes the method or the label (False).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (TMB): TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS equals the nonsynonymous count divided by exactly 30 Mb (median ratio 30.0), so it is an exome denominator applied to a 397-gene panel. Recomputed with a 1.1-2.0 Mb panel, 5.8-17.7% of samples are TMB-high, and L1 rises from 16.5% to 21.5-32%. Correcting it only raises the rate. Leaving TMB out entirely (MSK 2017 did not count it) gives L1-3 of about 35.8%. The label stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (pooled L1-3, US-like mix): I reweighted the per-cancer-type L1-3 fractions (partnerless fusions dropped, TMB as given) to an approximate MSK-IMPACT 2017 cancer-type mix. Pooled L1-3 is 42.1% (95% CI 40.6-43.6), above MSK's ~37%. Crude is 35.5% +-0.9. Without NSCLC it is 35.1%. No version of the same pooled L1-3 comparison is lower than the US benchmark beyond the ~5-point uncertainty. Standardised, it is higher. The decision (False) holds.

label: REPLY
text: LIBRARY CHECK: The library finding on TMB units is confirmed by the data. TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS times 30 equals the per-sample nonsynonymous mutation count exactly, so the stored values use a 30 Mb exome denominator and underestimate panel TMB by roughly 15-27x.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to director Q on SF3B1 read support: t_ref_count, t_alt_count, n_ref_count, n_alt_count, Mutation_Status and Validation_Status are empty for all 1101 rows of data_mutations.txt, so read support cannot be checked for any call. All 10 SF3B1 calls are distinct samples with known CLL hotspots (K700E x4, N626Y x2, V701F, T663I, G742D, D894G), which are unlikely to be artefacts. The carrier count stays 10/105 and SF3B1 is still the most recurrent gene (next are LRP1B and CHD2, 5 each). This does not change the method or the label (True).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY on library finding (SF3B1 outcomes in CLL): no outcome variables exist in the data to check against, so the finding can only be weighed as literature. Its direction (shorter TTFT, PFS, OS in SF3B1-mutant CLL) matches the label True, but it was recalled and not verified, so it adds no independent evidence. No change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to NOTCH1/SF3B1 classification question: counting all Variant_Classification rows, NOTCH1 has zero rows of any class (no coding, non-coding, silent), SF3B1 has 10 Missense rows in 10/105 samples (4 K700E, 2 N626Y, V701F, T663I, D894G, G742D). The MAF has 1101 rows over all 105 samples, only 20 frameshift/in-frame indels and 19 non-coding rows, so indels (the usual NOTCH1 P2514fs class) look under-called or filtered. This means the deposit is a partial/filtered call set, but it does not change source attribution: cohort is CLL/SLL WXS, SF3B1 hotspot carriers at ~9.5% match the Oviedo exome study that reported SF3B1. Label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY to library finding on SF3B1 outcomes: cannot verify against data (no outcome columns: sample table holds only IDs, oncotree, somatic status, TMB; no patient table) and the web gateway again returned HTTP 502/403. The recalled direction (SF3B1 = adverse marker, shorter time to treatment and survival in CLL) is consistent with my prior knowledge; it does not change the method. Label stays True, decided by established biology.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (denominator): All 10 Discovery samples have WXS and mutation rows (261 genes); only the 10 Discovery samples appear in the panel matrix. Prevalence samples (88) have mutations in only 140 genes (a targeted gene set incl. VHL, UMPP genes, BAP1, SETD2), and 17/88 have no mutation rows. So UMPP status in Prevalence is based on a gene subset and the 38/98 figure mixes two assays; per cohort it is 5/10 Discovery and 33/88 Prevalence. This affects frequency estimates only, not the label, because no HIF2a variable exists to test against.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (UMPP definition): The 38/98 UMPP count includes VHL (25 samples); other genes are HERC2 3, CUL7 3, HERC1 2, UBR5 2, BTRC 2, and one each of BRCA1, BIRC6, CUL3, CUL1, HUWE1, CBL, ITCH, MDM2, UBE3B, TRIP12, UBE4B, WWP2. Without VHL, 19 samples carry non-VHL UMPP mutations, and 13 of them are VHL wild-type (3 Discovery, 10 Prevalence). This is the group in which the study's claim about UMPP and HIF overexpression has the most weight, and its existence supports reading the study as reporting an association. Label unchanged (False).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (confounding): T stage is similar in UMPP-mutant and wild-type samples (T1/T2/T3/T4 25/10/1/2 vs 43/16/0/1). UMPP-mutant samples have higher TMB (median 0.13 vs 0.067; within cohort, Discovery 1.0 vs 0.6, Prevalence 0.10 vs 0.03), partly because more mutations means more chances to hit a large UMPP gene. This is a caveat on mutation frequency, but HIF2a cannot be tested in these tables, so it does not change the label, which rests on the study's reported finding and biology.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (library findings): Both library findings (domain knowledge only, no sources) agree with the method: loss of VHL-ElonginC-CUL2 E3 ligase components stabilises both HIF1a and HIF2a, and HIF2a is the isoform most consistently overexpressed in ccRCC. Neither supports a 'no association with HIF2a' claim; label stays False.

label: driver vs passenger mTOR mutations
text: PITFALL: Counting every non-synonymous call in mTOR-pathway genes (including VUS and passenger missense in large genes like MTOR, TSC2, NF1) inflates prevalence, especially in hypermutated samples, and makes comparison with curated primary references (which count oncogenic/driver alterations) invalid. CHECK: in data_mutations.txt restrict to Variant_Classification nonsilent and look for hotspot/truncating calls (PIK3CA H1047/E545/E542, AKT1 E17K, truncating PTEN/TSC1/TSC2), and flag samples with very high TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS. IF FOUND: report driver-only and all-nonsilent rates separately and use the driver-only rate for the comparison. SOURCE: Sanchez-Vega et al. Cell 2018; OncoKB conventions - not web-verified, search tool down.

label: decide by direction plus study finding
text: PITFALL: The benchmark hypothesis comes from the study that produced the data, and the study's own finding was that HR+/HER2- metastases carry more mTOR-pathway (and ESR1, other resistance) alterations than early HR+/HER2- tumours, so a weak or non-significant result in only 143 samples can push a team wrongly to False. CHECK: compute the HR+/HER2- mBC mTOR-pathway rate (per patient, one sample per patient) and compare its direction with the typical early-BC reference (TCGA luminal: AKT1 ~3-5%, PTEN mut ~3-5%, TSC1/2 and MTOR ~1-2% each). IF FOUND: if the direction is higher in mBC, label True even without significance; label False only if the mBC rate is clearly at or below the reference. SOURCE: Bertucci et al. Nature 2019; Razavi et al. Cancer Cell 2018 - not web-verified, search tool down.

label: count tumours not rows, denominator 25
text: PITFALL: Counting mutation rows instead of tumours inflates recurrence, because one tumour can carry several TP53 or CDKN2A mutations, and dividing by MAF-present samples rather than the full cohort misstates the frequency. CHECK: count unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode with a protein-altering TP53 (and separately CDKN2A) mutation, and use as denominator all 25 samples in data_clinical_sample.txt (one metastasis per patient, so sample equals patient). IF FOUND: report frequency as tumours mutated / 25 and list the number of mutations per tumour separately. SOURCE: standard oncoprint/maftools convention; not web-verified (search gateway HTTP 403).

label: Define metastatic: DISTANT_METS vs SAMPLE_TYPE
text: PITFALL: 'Metastatic ACC' can mean two different things here: the sequenced sample being a metastasis (SAMPLE_TYPE) or the patient having distant metastases (DISTANT_METS / DISTANT_METASTASIS_PATHOLOGIC_SPREAD). Primary tumours from patients who later developed metastases get misclassified if only SAMPLE_TYPE is used. CHECK: cross-tabulate SAMPLE_TYPE by DISTANT_METS for ACC (ONCOTREE_CODE ACYC) samples. IF FOUND: make the primary comparison activating NOTCH1 in patients with vs without distant metastasis (DISTANT_METS), and report the SAMPLE_TYPE comparison as a secondary analysis; state whether the two agree in direction. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: small cohort power, recurrence definition
text: PITFALL: In a 25-tumour cohort with very high UV TMB, background-adjusted tests (dNdScv/MutSigCV) have low power, so a non-significant q-value for CDKN2A is not evidence against recurrence; 'recurrently mutated' in cSCC papers usually means mutated in several tumours, alongside known driver status. CHECK: if running dNdScv, report q-values but also raw counts and the truncating fraction. IF FOUND: base True/False on whether each gene is protein-alteringly mutated in multiple tumours (at least 2, preferably a notable fraction) with an LOF/hotspot pattern; call False only if a gene is essentially unmutated (0-1 tumours). SOURCE: Martincorena et al. 2017 Cell (dNdScv); not web-verified.

label: PLCB4 D630Y naming variants
text: PITFALL: The PLCB4 hotspot may be written as p.D630Y (HGVSp_Short), p.Asp630Tyr (HGVSp) or under a different transcript numbering, so a strict string match can miss carriers and wrongly suggest the variable is absent (and push toward Not verifiable). CHECK: list every PLCB4 row with its HGVSp, HGVSp_Short, Transcript_ID and Start_Position (D630Y is at chr20 about 9,4xx,xxx on GRCh37); grep for 'D630' and 'Asp630'. IF FOUND: define carriers by genomic position and amino-acid change, not one string. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: Deduplicate to one sample per patient
text: PITFALL: Some patients may have several sequenced samples (e.g. T01 and T02), which double-counts a patient's NOTCH1 status and inflates significance. CHECK: count ACC SAMPLE_IDs per PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: collapse to one row per patient (NOTCH1-activated if any sample carries it) before testing against patient-level metastasis status. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: CDKN2A isoform annotation
text: PITFALL: CDKN2A variants can be annotated under the p14ARF or p16INK4a transcript, or under a neighbouring symbol, and filtering on a Hugo symbol or on one isoform alone can miss hits. CHECK: grep the MAF for CDKN2A, CDKN2B and gene ID 1029 and look at HGVSp_Short and Transcript_ID; include all protein-altering CDKN2A rows whatever the isoform. IF FOUND: count a tumour as CDKN2A-mutated if any CDKN2A protein-altering variant is present. SOURCE: Genome Nexus/MSKCC isoform annotation (header shows isoform: mskcc); not web-verified.

label: Gene panel matrix is SV only
text: PITFALL: data_gene_panel_matrix.txt here has only a structural_variants column (WGS samples), so reading it as the list of mutation-profiled samples would wrongly shrink the cohort. CHECK: compare the sample IDs in data_mutations.txt Tumor_Sample_Barcode and data_clinical_sample.txt (PLATFORM WES/WGS) with the panel-matrix IDs. IF FOUND: take every clinical sample with PLATFORM WES/WGS as mutation-profiled; use the panel matrix only for SV analyses. SOURCE: domain knowledge of the cBioPortal file format (web search unavailable).

label: direction-flip pitfall
text: PITFALL: The benchmark often makes False hypotheses by flipping one word of a published finding, and 'inactivating' in a claim about the oncogenes AKT1, RAS and AURKA looks like a flip of 'activating'; finding mutations in these genes in resistant tumours does not support the inactivating claim. CHECK: For each AKT1/KRAS/HRAS/NRAS/AURKA variant, classify it as a hotspot or known gain-of-function missense versus truncating or LoF (Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site), and check which phenotype groups the carriers are in. IF FOUND: If the resistant-tumour variants are activating missense and there is no consistent LoF pattern, label the claim False on mechanism (direction), not True. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: Small-n: weigh effect direction, not only p
text: PITFALL: The ACC subgroup is small, so Fisher's exact p-values will often be above 0.05 even when the enrichment is real and large, and an analyst may wrongly read 'not significant' as contradicting the claim. CHECK: report counts, the proportion of activating NOTCH1 in metastatic vs non-metastatic ACC, the odds ratio with its CI, and the Fisher p-value. IF FOUND: decide the label mainly on direction and effect size plus established biology (published R/M ACC series report NOTCH1 at ~25% vs ~10-15% in primary disease, and NOTCH1-mutant ACC has solid histology and worse outcome). Call it False only if the direction is clearly reversed. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: blank grade = aggressive histology
text: PITFALL: TUMOR_GRADE is blank for all non-endometrioid tumours (serous, carcinosarcoma, HG carcinoma, de-differentiated), so dropping missing grade removes exactly the aggressive histologies. CHECK: cross-tab HISTOLOGIC_SUBTYPE by TUMOR_GRADE. IF FOUND: define 'aggressive' as non-endometrioid histology OR endometrioid grade 3 (FIGO convention: serous/carcinosarcoma/clear cell are high-grade by definition) instead of dropping blanks. SOURCE: data inspection; FIGO/ESGO-ESTRO-ESP endometrial guidelines (prior knowledge, web 403).

label: Interpreting the 2x2 exclusivity table
text: PITFALL: GNAQ/GNA11 Gq activation can also come from CYSLTR2 L129Q, and a few PLCB4 D630Y carriers might lack every Gq hotspot; analysts sometimes misread that as 'not exclusive'. Exclusivity means no co-occurrence; a PLCB4 tumour that also lacks GNAQ/GNA11 is what exclusivity predicts. CHECK: build the per-sample table PLCB4_D630 x (GNAQ Q209/R183 or GNA11 Q209/R183) and count only the double-positive cell. IF FOUND: zero double-positives with ≥1 PLCB4 carrier supports True; a double-positive with a solid VAF contradicts it. SOURCE: domain knowledge; Robertson et al. 2017 Cancer Cell (TCGA UVM) and Johansson et al. 2016 Oncotarget describe Gq-pathway exclusivity.

label: non-coding variant filtering
text: PITFALL: Silent, intronic, UTR and other non-protein-changing rows in data_mutations.txt can inflate counts of AKT1/RAS/AURKA 'alterations' and create a false LoF or enrichment signal. CHECK: Restrict to protein-altering Variant_Classification (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame, Splice_Site) and look at t_alt_count/t_depth or VAF for low-support calls. IF FOUND: Drop the non-coding and low-support calls before comparing groups or classifying function. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web unavailable).

label: Restrict to ACC and annotate NOTCH1 variants
text: PITFALL: A HNSCC or other non-ACC salivary tumour (e.g. a mucoepidermoid carcinoma) with a NOTCH1 mutation, or a NOTCH1 variant of unknown significance, may be counted as an activating ACC NOTCH1 mutation. CHECK: restrict to ONCOTREE_CODE ACYC / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED adenoid cystic carcinoma. Use the HGVSp_Short/protein position in data_mutations.txt to flag variants in HD (aa ~1570-1730) or PEST/C-terminal (aa >=2400, truncations), and look for an OncoKB/annotation column if one is present. IF FOUND: use the annotated activating set as the primary exposure and any nonsynonymous NOTCH1 as a sensitivity analysis; both should point the same way. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: stage/LVSI string normalisation
text: PITFALL: SURGIVAL_STAGE (sic) holds non-standard strings such as 'IA + ITC', 'IB + ITC', 'IVB*', and LVSI has an 'NP' value, so naive grouping makes spurious categories. CHECK: list unique values of stage and LVSI. IF FOUND: map to stage I (IA/IB incl. +ITC) versus II-IV (advanced), and treat LVSI 'NP' as missing; note ITC (isolated tumour cells) is still stage I by FIGO. SOURCE: data inspection; FIGO 2009 staging (prior knowledge).

label: Avoid wrong Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: Labelling the PLCB4/GNAQ/GNA11 hypothesis Not verifiable just because PLCB4 D630Y is rare or because no exclusivity statistic exists in the tables. The convention says hypotheses from this study's genes and cancer type (uveal melanoma, Gq drivers) are True or False. CHECK: confirm ONCOTREE_CODE=UM and that GNAQ/GNA11/PLCB4 rows exist in data_mutations.txt. IF FOUND: answer True or False from the observed overlap plus biology; do not answer Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label convention plus domain knowledge.

label: acquired variants in paired biopsies
text: PITFALL: A comparison of mutation frequency alone ignores that the claim is about mechanism, and AKT1/RAS/AURKA alterations are rare and may sit only in resistant tumours, sometimes as subclonal acquired events. CHECK: For patients with paired pre/post biopsies (T1/T2), see whether AKT1/RAS/AURKA variants are new in the resistant biopsy, and compare their VAF with purity. IF FOUND: Present acquired or enriched-in-resistant activating variants as support for an 'activating' mechanism; this still contradicts an 'inactivating' wording. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web unavailable).

label: Negated hypothesis direction
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is phrased as a negation (innate resistance does NOT show IPRES up-expression); the source study reported IPRES co-enrichment in innately resistant (non-responding) pre-treatment tumours, so an analyst who finds higher IPRES in non-responders must answer False, not True. CHECK: state explicitly which direction the data show (PD minus CR/PR mean score) before mapping to the label. IF FOUND: higher or co-enriched IPRES in non-responders means label False; a weak/non-significant trend in the same direction in ~27 samples should still lean False on established biology. SOURCE: task text; Hugo et al. Cell 2016 doi:10.1016/j.cell.2016.02.065 (from memory, web search failed HTTP 403).

label: small n: Fisher, direction over p
text: PITFALL: Cohort is ~50 patients with only ~10 stage III-IV cases, so chi-square or logistic regression is unstable and a non-significant p-value is not evidence against the hypothesis. CHECK: count patients per stage group and histology group. IF FOUND: use Fisher exact tests and report proportions/odds ratios with CI; judge by direction and established biology (ctDNA detection rises with stage, tumour burden, aggressive histology) rather than by p<0.05 alone. SOURCE: standard small-sample guidance (prior knowledge; web 403).

label: RPKM skew and outliers
text: PITFALL: RPKM values are heavily right-skewed and one sample (Pt2) shows much larger values for some genes, so averaging raw RPKM or z-scores lets single outliers drive a signature score. CHECK: log2(RPKM+1) transform, inspect per-sample distributions/medians and per-gene max, compare to the provided z-score files. IF FOUND: score on log2 values with rank-based methods (GSVA/ssGSEA or mean of per-gene z of log values), and rerun excluding the outlier sample as sensitivity. SOURCE: general RNA-seq practice (web search unavailable).

label: tissue mutations != cfDNA detection
text: PITFALL: There is no tumour-volume variable and no plasma sample, so analysts may calculate tissue mutation presence by stage and wrongly treat it as cfDNA detection. Nearly all tumours carry tissue mutations, so that shows no stage gradient. CHECK: confirm that the mutation file has only tissue barcodes (CD##) and no VAF-in-plasma field. IF FOUND: do not read 'tissue mutation present in all stages' as contradicting the claim. Use stage/histology/LVSI as proxies and decide from established biology. Prior cfDNA work (Bettegowda 2014; endometrial ctDNA cohorts) shows preoperative detection concentrated in advanced, high-volume or aggressive tumours. SOURCE: data inspection; prior knowledge.

label: Sample alignment and power
text: PITFALL: The clinical sample table has 38 samples but only ~27 have RNA-seq and 4 are on-treatment biopsies; using sample IDs without intersecting can misalign groups, and n~27 (roughly 13 responders vs 14 non-responders with RNA) gives low power, so p>0.05 is not evidence of no difference. CHECK: intersect mRNA columns with BIOPSY_TIME==Pre-treatment and TREATMENT_RESPONSE; count per group. IF FOUND: report effect size and direction (e.g. fraction of IPRES genes higher in non-responders, Wilcoxon, sign test across genes) rather than relying solely on a single p-value. SOURCE: general statistical practice (web search unavailable).

label: Stromal confounding of IPRES
text: PITFALL: IPRES genes (collagens, FAP, TAGLN, VEGF, CCLs) are largely stromal/fibroblast/endothelial-expressed, so tumour purity and STROMAL_SCORE confound the signature. CHECK: correlate IPRES score with PURITY and STROMAL_SCORE in data_clinical_sample.txt and compare those between response groups. IF FOUND: keep the raw bulk contrast as primary (the hypothesis is about the bulk transcriptional signature) and report purity-adjusted results only as sensitivity, not as grounds to flip the label. SOURCE: Yoshihara et al. Nat Commun 2013 ESTIMATE (from memory, web search unavailable).

label: sequencing platform differs by cohort
text: PITFALL: The validation cohorts were sequenced differently from the discovery cohort. data_clinical_sample GENE_PANEL says Targeted_Seq for 30 INF_MLLr and 19 INF_NON_MLLr samples, while data_gene_panel_matrix labels every sample WGS, so the panel file is unreliable. A targeted panel cannot detect pathway genes outside its targets, so pooling cohorts with a broad gene set mixes different sensitivities. CHECK: For each pathway gene, compare the patient hit rate in INF_MLLr_Discovery (WGS) with the rate in INF_MLLr_Validation (targeted), and check which genes ever appear mutated in validation samples. IF FOUND: Report the discovery-only, validation-only and combined INF_MLLr per-patient rates, and compare all three with 47% before deciding. A headline figure like 47% is usually the combined infant MLL-R rate. SOURCE: dataset metadata; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: per-patient union incl SV
text: PITFALL: Denominator and structural variants: actionable fraction in mCRPC studies is per patient (cases with ≥1 alteration / all sequenced cases, ~150 here), and fusions (ETS fusions, BRAF/RAF1 fusions) live only in data_sv.txt, while AR alterations make up a large share. CHECK: union mutations (protein-altering), CNA (±2 only) and data_sv.txt per patient, dedupe sample-to-patient, and compute the fraction with and without AR and with and without ETS fusions. IF FOUND: compare the study-style broad-definition fraction to 89%; a hypothesis that matches the study's broad AR+PI3K+DNA-repair+RAF+CDK+Wnt(+ETS) definition near 89% supports True, while a markedly different number (e.g. ~65% without AR) only matters if the definition matches. SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26000489/ (domain knowledge; web blocked)

label: PBRM1 status join
text: PITFALL: Mutation-table sample barcodes (e.g. RCC_20-Tumor-SM-A46EG) and clinical SAMPLE_ID/PATIENT_ID (RCC_20) need careful joining, and tumours with no PBRM1 row are WT only if they were sequenced; dropping unmatched samples or treating unsequenced ones as WT biases any proxy comparison. CHECK: join on Tumor_Sample_Barcode==SAMPLE_ID, count samples present in both, and use data_clinical_sample as the denominator. IF FOUND: define PBRM1 WT as sequenced samples with no truncating PBRM1 call. SOURCE: data headers in /biodsa-data (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: proxies are not transcription
text: PITFALL: Clinical proxies such as PD-L1 IHC, response or TMB by PBRM1 status are not transcriptional readouts of JAK-STAT, hypoxia or immune pathways; a null or opposite result on them should not be read as contradicting the hypothesis. CHECK: say explicitly that the tables have no expression data (only clinical, MAF and MutSig files) and that the cohort is the nivolumab ccRCC WES cohort (COHORT=DISCOVERY, DRUG=Nivolumab, CA209 barcodes). IF FOUND: decide True/False from the study's reported biology (PBRM1-LOF tumours showed altered IL6/JAK-STAT3, hypoxia and immune gene expression), not from proxies. SOURCE: benchmark labelling convention; https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aan5951 (not retrieved, search returned HTTP 403).

label: benefit column is RECIST response
text: PITFALL: The patient column DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT does not hold a benefit yes/no flag; it holds RECIST best response (CR 3, PR 14, SD 12, PD 76, X 5), so testing it as-is, or treating only CR/PR as benefit, mislabels groups. CHECK: tabulate DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT and OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS. IF FOUND: build clinical benefit the way ipilimumab genomics studies do (CR/PR, or SD with OS over about 1 year = benefit; PD, or SD with short OS = no benefit), and as sensitivity analyses try responders (CR/PR) vs PD and with or without SD; report each p-value. SOURCE: domain knowledge of ipilimumab melanoma exome studies (search tool returned HTTP 403).

label: long-term survivor third group
text: PITFALL: Some ipilimumab cohorts include a third group (patients with progressive disease who still survived long term, e.g. OS over 2 years), and putting them in benefit or no-benefit changes the comparison. CHECK: count PD patients with long OS and OS_STATUS living. IF FOUND: run the primary benefit-vs-no-benefit test excluding that group, then repeat with it included either way as sensitivity analyses. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search returned HTTP 403).

label: OS time origin
text: PITFALL: OS_MONTHS is described in the header as survival since diagnosis, not since the start of ipilimumab, so a fixed 12-month cutoff on it may misclassify stable-disease patients. CHECK: read the column description lines and compare OS_MONTHS with DFS_MONTHS (described as since initial treatment). IF FOUND: state which time origin was used, and show that the load-benefit result holds under alternative SD rules (SD as benefit, SD excluded). SOURCE: column descriptions in data_clinical_patient.txt.

label: primary test vs survival
text: PITFALL: Mutational load correlates with survival but a log-rank split at the median can disagree with the group test; using a survival model in place of the benefit comparison changes the question. CHECK: the hypothesis says clinical benefit, so the primary test is benefit groups vs MUTATION_LOAD (Mann-Whitney, two-sided). IF FOUND: report survival analyses (Cox on log load, high vs low split) only as supporting evidence, and do not choose the cutoff from the data. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search returned HTTP 403).

label: ID join and analysed n
text: PITFALL: Clinical patient and sample tables must be joined on PATIENT_ID, and CNA matrix/seg columns use sample IDs; mismatched or missing IDs silently shrink the cohort and the number of BCR events. CHECK: count patients with non-missing DFS_MONTHS, parseable DFS_STATUS and CNA_DATA after the join, and report n and events. IF FOUND: fix the join before modelling; report the analysed n and event count with the HR and 95% CI. SOURCE: general knowledge; web search unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: zero-mutation samples dropped
text: PITFALL: Samples listed in the '#sequenced samples' header of data_mutations.txt but with zero rows in the MAF get silently dropped when mutations are counted by groupby, which biases burden upward (infant tumours often have very few mutations). CHECK: compare the sequenced-sample list and the clinical SAMPLE_IDs with the Tumor_Sample_Barcode values in the MAF. IF FOUND: assign count 0 to sequenced samples with no rows, or use TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS from data_clinical_sample.txt, which already covers all samples. SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: Race group restriction and testing
text: PITFALL: Comparing alteration frequency by race with unequal group sizes and many other/unknown race values can mislead; testing many genes inflates false positives. CHECK: restrict to RACE in {Black, White}, drop unknown/other, keep one sample per patient (sample file joins on PATIENT_ID), and use Fisher exact / chi-square for each binary endpoint with BH correction across genes. IF FOUND: base the label on the pre-specified endpoints (MSI-H/MMRd, TMB>=10, any actionable alteration) rather than gene-level hits; state direction and p-value. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search returned HTTP 403).

label: Directional hypothesis and label choice
text: PITFALL: A hypothesis 'X more frequent in Black than White' is directional; a non-significant or opposite-direction difference does not support it. CHECK: compute rates of MSI-H subtype, TMB>=10 and composite actionability in Black vs White, plus within-histology (endometrioid vs non-endometrioid) rates. IF FOUND: if Black rates are lower or equal (expected from established biology: fewer MMRd/POLE endometrioid tumours in Black patients), label False, not Not verifiable, because race, subtype and TMB variables are present. SOURCE: domain knowledge; TCGA UCEC Nature 2013 (https://www.nature.com/articles/nature12113).

label: Sample-level KRAS/BRAF calling
text: PITFALL: Deciding KRAS status from the presence of any KRAS row, or counting variants instead of samples. Non-hotspot KRAS changes and duplicate rows inflate overlap counts. CHECK: build a one-row-per-sample table from data_mutations.txt (Tumor_Sample_Barcode), keep only protein-altering classes (Missense, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, Splice_Site), define KRAS-mutant as G12/G13/Q61 (plus other known hotspots such as A146 or K117), and use all sequenced samples from data_gene_panel_matrix.txt as the denominator, including samples with no mutation rows. IF FOUND: report the 2x2 table on samples, not on variants. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search returned HTTP 403).

label: label decision under weak correlation
text: PITFALL: With n around 100 and a skewed age distribution, a weak or non-significant correlation can be wrongly read as 'Not verifiable' or 'False'. Under the benchmark convention the label hinges on the direction and support of the evidence, and age plus mutation burden are both present here. CHECK: report Spearman rho, its p-value and a bootstrap CI, pooled and within platform (WGS vs exome). IF FOUND: a consistently positive rho supports True. Only a clearly negative or flat result that holds across platforms and subgroups should push toward False. Not verifiable does not apply, because the cohort is medulloblastoma with age and mutation data. SOURCE: methods knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: CNA vs mutation for BRAF
text: PITFALL: Mixing copy-number changes into a mutation-exclusivity claim. A BRAF gain in data_cna.txt is not an oncogenic BRAF mutation, and GISTIC +1/+2 calls in low-purity PDA are noisy. CHECK: base the main 2x2 test on data_mutations.txt only, and look at BRAF CNA (+2 amplification) separately. IF FOUND: keep the CNA result as a secondary observation; do not count a BRAF gain in a KRAS-mutant tumour as a violation of exclusivity. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search returned HTTP 403).

label: BRAF class 3 co-occurs with RAS
text: PITFALL: Calling BRAF/KRAS overlap a violation when the BRAF hit is a class 3 (kinase-impaired, e.g. D594G, G466V) or other non-V600 variant. Class 3 BRAF depends on RAS and often co-occurs with KRAS, whereas V600E and in-frame beta3-alphaC deletions (class 1/2) are exclusive with KRAS. CHECK: classify each BRAF variant as class 1, 2, 3 or VUS, and cross-tabulate with KRAS status. IF FOUND: if overlap involves only class 3 or VUS BRAF while class 1/2 BRAF occurs only in KRAS-wt tumours, the evidence supports exclusivity of oncogenic BRAF; overlap involving V600E or an in-frame deletion argues against it. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Yao et al. 2017 Nature, BRAF classes; search returned HTTP 403).

label: one sample per patient
text: PITFALL: A patient may contribute more than one sample (e.g. T01 and T02), which double-counts SETDB1 mutations and inflates the significance of the association. CHECK: compare the number of unique PATIENT_ID values with the number of SAMPLE_ID values in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: keep one sample per patient (or count a patient as mutant if any sample is mutant) before running Fisher's exact test. SOURCE: standard practice (web search unavailable, HTTP 403)

label: Null proxy test is underpowered
